## JOHANN ANDREAS PFEFFEL,

->Court Engraver to his<-

### SACRED IMPERIAL MAJESTY,

->and Art Dealer in Augsburg.<-

He came into the world in the year of our Redemption 1674, on the 5th of June, in Bischoffingen, under the jurisdiction of the most illustrious Margrave of Baden-Durlach. His father was the most venerable Pastor <note>Original: "Herder" (Shepherd), a common term for a minister.</note> of that place; his mother, Helena Boeklin, died the following year. In addition to a change of residence, the disastrous internal wars had also driven this best of fathers out of his office, which resulted in our Johann Andreas Pfeffel being brought to Augsburg in the year 1676. This benevolent mother city, encouraging him from that time on, instructed the youth in the foundations of the Art of Copperplate Engraving <term>Copperplate Engraving: A process where a design is incised into a metal plate, which is then inked and pressed onto paper.</term> with such great success that in the year 1697 he seemed capable enough to go to Vienna to display the specimens of his art in this most illustrious residence of the highest Sovereign. From there, he departed in the year 1698 for his Fatherland, intending to visit Paris; however, he changed his mind due to the rumors reaching his ears of the Imperial Wedding Ceremonies of the Roman Emperor JOSEPH I to be celebrated in Vienna. Having arrived there in 1699, he decided to remain there forever, strengthened in this by the favor of the greatest Monarch of the Christians, who deigned to accept him among the Court Engravers. However, the matter turned out differently; a very great mortality <note>Likely referring to the sudden death of Emperor Joseph I in 1711, or the plague outbreak of that period.</note> occurring unexpectedly, he returned from Vienna to his Augsburg in the year 1711. There, enrolled upon the list of Citizens, he took as his spouse the exquisite maiden *Magdalena Lefer*, by whom he begot three offspring <note>Original: "afzetsels," a term meaning 'reproductions' or 'prints,' used here as a pun for children.</note>; *Johann Andreas*, now following in his father’s footsteps, remains his beloved successor. Released from this first union in the year 1716, he entered into a second marriage in the year 1717 with a maiden likewise in her blooming youth, *Maria Catharina Auracher*, who has made him the father of three daughters and five sons; however, of these latter, he is tenderly raising only the youngest.

### JOHANN MELCHIOR FÜSSLI,
->of Zurich.<-

He was born among us in the year 1677, to the very brave Captain *Johann Caspar* and *Magdalena Stuz*. He laid the foundations of Art in his Fatherland in the year 1690 under the guidance of Mayer, which he refined to perfection in Berlin, where the very famous portrait painter Blesendorf directed him. Having returned to his Fatherland, he bound himself in marriage to *Anna Wetstein*, with whom, as the happy mother of twelve children—among whom is but a single daughter, *Anna Barbara*—he finds his delight.

# SPIRITUAL PHYSICS,

->THAT IS:<-

### The five Books of Moses treated naturally, and explained in a spiritual and clear sense, no less for the awakening of the spirit than for physical benefit and the recognition of our duty.

---

->God is the Beginning and End of all things.<-

## PRINTED PLATE I.

->*In the beginning GOD created Heaven and Earth. Genesis I. v. 1.*<-

Moses, known as the Most Ancient Writer, awakens man to the knowledge of God through the description of the rare and remarkable origin of the newly created world. Through this means, he endeavors to instill in us an attentive and useful contemplation of the entire *Universe*, along with a thorough recognition of ourselves. This threefold object is indeed the primary goal and the most important use which all Philosophy—and especially *Physics* <note>The author uses "Natuurkunde," which in this period referred to Natural Philosophy or the study of the physical world as God's creation.</note>—solely aims for and pursues.

Innate reason and our duty urge man sensibly enough to recognize God as Creator, although He is in Himself incomprehensible to our weak and limited understanding. The wonderful and immeasurable extent and harmonious consistency of this world is an absolute and eloquent Sign of God’s infinite goodness and Omnipotence, with which He *in the beginning created* this wild and well-ordered dwelling place for man’s service.

Man, called by the Greeks a *microcosm* <note>original: *kleine weereld* ("small world"); the concept that the human being is a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</note>, as if representing in himself concisely the entire constitution and working of Nature, feels himself urged—both inwardly and outwardly—to wonder at the Divine power and prudent arrangement that shines forth clearly everywhere in the masterly handiwork of the world's Creation; to praise it

<column-break/>

according to its merit, and to worship the Supreme Being in spirit with all possible reverence and submission. He is urged to employ himself and the powers of his soul in all its workings with diligence for the honor and spreading of God’s most holy name, never forgetting the humble awe which he *owes to that Sovereign Lord, who stretched out the heavens, founded the earth, and formed the spirit of man in the midst of it.* <note>A paraphrase of Zechariah 12:1.</note>

The Hebrew word, *Bereshith* <note>original: *Bereſchith* (Hebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית), meaning "In the beginning."</note>, in the Dutch <note>The translator has rendered this as "English" for the current readership.</note> "in the Beginning," is noteworthy because, like a flashing bolt of lightning, it completely shatters and annihilates the ridiculous dreams and groundless stubbornness of Aristotle and his followers regarding the world’s state of eternity. At the same time, it confirms God’s eternal and unceasing activity. He was certainly from Eternity, and was essentially working, He who at the beginning of time brought forth the world out of the endless abyss of Nothingness through His Omnipotence.

All of Nature seems sufficiently able to demonstrate by itself—even without the infallible confirmation of Holy Scripture—that the *world was formerly created, and indeed created out of Nothing*; yet only *Moses*, called by *Tertullian* <note>A prolific early Christian author from Roman North Africa.</note> *God’s confidant and closest initiate into secrets*, has instructed us regarding the years, months, days, and their succession and arrangement. Thus an Interpreter was necessary, who through God’s high

# SPIRITUAL NATURAL PHILOSOPHY,

->THAT IS:<-

### The five Books of Moses treated according to natural philosophy, and explained in a spiritual and clear sense, no less for the awakening of the spirit than for bodily benefit and the recognition of our duty.

---

->God is the Beginning and End of all things.<-

## PLATE I.

->*In the beginning GOD created Heaven and Earth. Genesis I:1.*<-

Moses, known as the Most Ancient Writer, rouses man to the knowledge of God through the description of the rare and remarkable emergence of the newly created World. Through this means, he seeks to instill in us an attentive and useful contemplation of the whole *Universe*, alongside a thorough recognition of ourselves. This threefold object is indeed the principal goal and the foremost use which the whole of Philosophy—and particularly *Natural Philosophy* <note>The term used is *Natuurkunde*, which in the 18th century referred to the study of the physical world and laws of nature.</note>—uniquely aims for and pursues.

Innate reason and our duty urge man sensibly enough to acknowledge God as Creator, although He is in Himself incomprehensible to our weak and limited understanding. The wonderful and immeasurable extent and harmonious composition of this world is an absolute and eloquent sign of God's infinite goodness and Omnipotence, with which He *created in the beginning* this wild and well-ordered dwelling place for the service of man.

Man, called by the Greeks *a small world* <note>original: "een kleine weereld," referring to the Greek term *microcosmos*</note>, as representing briefly within himself the entire constitution and working of Nature, feels himself urged internally and externally to marvel at the Divine powers and wise arrangement that radiate clearly everywhere in the masterly handiwork of the world's Creation. He is moved to praise Him

<column-break/>

according to His merits, and to worship the Supreme Being in spirit with all possible reverence and submission. He must employ himself and the powers of his soul in all its workings with diligence for the honor and propagation of God's most holy name, never forgetting the humble awe he owes to that Sovereign Lord *who stretched out the heavens, founded the earth, and formed the spirit of man in the midst of the same.*

The Hebrew word, *Bereshith* <note>Hebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית, meaning "In the beginning."</note>, rendered in Dutch as *in den Beginne*, is noteworthy because, like a flashing bolt of lightning, it utterly shatters and annihilates the ridiculous dreams and groundless stubbornness of Aristotle and his followers regarding the world’s state of eternity. At the same time, it confirms God's eternal and unceasing activity. He was surely from Eternity, and worked essentially, who at the beginning of time brought forth the world out of the endless abyss of Nothingness through His Omnipotence.

All of Nature seems to demonstrate sufficiently of itself, even without the infallible confirmation of Holy Scripture, that the world was formerly and indeed *created out of Nothing*. However, *Moses* alone, called by *Tertullian* <term>God's confidant and closest initiate</term> <note>Tertullian was an early Christian author from Carthage (c. 155 – c. 220 AD).</note>, has instructed us in the years, months, days, and their succession and arrangement. Thus an Interpreter was necessary, who through God's high—

# S P I R I T U A L

high enlightenment would make known to man the hidden Treasures, enclosed in the origin of all things.

Just as Moses discovers the world’s *beginning*, so too does not only Spiritual or sacred, but also secular or worldly *Chronology* <note>The study of historical time and dating</note>—founded upon the unchanging and steady movement of the Stars—show us the progress of time even unto this day.

The *Creator* is *God* Triune, expressed in the Hebrew language by the word *Elohim* <note>original: "Elohim," a plural name for God in the Hebrew Bible, often used by theologians to hint at the Trinity</note>, eternal, independent, living in the utmost perfection, entirely free and acting by Himself, ruling absolutely; being the supreme and simplest essence, spiritual and immovable, one in number and unique in Himself, omniscient, omnipotent, all-wise, all-good, existing by Himself, infinite, unlimited, incomprehensible, most merciful and most blessed from all eternity. Through these expressions, which *Sturmius* <note>Johann Christoph Sturm (1635–1703), a German philosopher and mathematician who sought to reconcile science with faith</note> cites in *Theosophy, Chapter 3*, one can easily obtain a fitting idea—at least as far as the power of our understanding reaches—to imagine God’s sublime and bottomless attributes in the spirit.

God, the most magnificent Supreme Being, perfect in all parts, has brought forth this Whole Universe out of Nothing for His own glorification, and created it through His eternal wisdom in the beginning of time; yet in such a way that the same did not spring from the Divine essence itself, much less that it could have produced its own origin, being a material and purely passive being. Consequently, Nature—which the Heathens wrongly regarded as the Deity—cannot be its original producer, unless one wished to understand by the word *Nature* the constant activity of all things, as the wild and irrational dwellers of the mountains and shores do. In this manner, the senseless doctrine of the *Spinozists* <note>Followers of Baruch Spinoza, whom the author accuses of Pantheism—the idea that God and the physical universe are the same thing</note> must necessarily collapse entirely, for they dare to assert that the world is co-eternal with God, or together of one and the same essence. Likewise, the opinion of the *Epicureans* <note>Followers of Epicurus; here referring to Atomists who believed the world formed by chance</note> is completely unfounded, who say that the world was formed by nothing but an accidental confluence of spaceless indivisibles <note>The author is referring to "atoms"</note>, through which they limit the Deity and wish to bind that entirely free-acting Being to Fate. For who has determined Eternal time? Who has taught the All-Wise arrangement? Who has brought strength or help to the Omnipotent? Who is he, says *Ambrose* in *On Faith in the Resurrection* <note>original Latin: "de Fide Resurrect."</note>, who has carried the rocks and mountains on his shoulders and brought them to the Creator? Who has contributed anything to the cost? Who has been in any way helpful to the acting Deity?

<column-break/>

That same God is He by whose Omnipotence everything is *created*, by whose wisdom everything is arranged and governed, and who, through His mercy, *sustains* the Whole Universe for the best. This is what the Greek word *Ktisein* or *Ktisis* <note>original: "Ktisein, Ktisis," meaning to create, found, or the act of creation</note> signifies, by which is understood not only the creation out of Nothing, but mostly everything that is commonly brought forth and formed. Let no one think that God created the *Whales* out of the so-called first Nothing, *Genesis 1:21*, because in the aforementioned word *Creation* <note>original: "Ktisis"</note> is contained not only the creation of Man, nor the production of other creatures, but also the accidents <note>In philosophy, "accidents" are qualities that can change without changing the essence of a thing</note>, as the famous Teacher of the nations, Paul, clearly indicates in *Romans 8, verses 38 and 39*. One may likewise consult the ingenious Gotthard Heidegger, a High-German writer, in his book *On the Groaning Creature, page 164* <note>original Latin: "de Creatura gemente"</note>.

Creation is a production out of Nothing; thus it is a work of an unlimited power, because there is an infinite difference between Nothing and Something, for even an endless multiplication of Nothing can never make One, much less a number. However, nothing more than a single nod of God’s will was necessary for the world’s creation. Does someone ask how much time? *Ambrose* answers: He willed, and it was.

expressed; He was as righteous from eternity as when He punished evil in time; likewise, His infinite mercy was in no way increased by His voluntary gifts. From this, it is sufficiently clear that He must necessarily have been Omnipotent, Glorious, Righteous, and Charitable within Himself from all eternity.

By the words *Heaven and Earth*, we are to understand the general principles of the Universe, both the active and the passive: the "overlying" ones, as some prefer to say, or the highest, and the "underlying" or lowest, which are the fine (even the very finest), the thick, and the thickest. Or, to speak more clearly, one can understand by this the Universe in general—that is, all and every body, whether bright, transparent, or dark, specifically those that concern the spheres of Earth, Water, and Air. In this manner, and certainly quite easily, the previously praised *Heidegger* <note>Johann Heinrich Heidegger (1633–1698), a Swiss theologian</note> understands by the word *creature* in *Romans 7:22* <note>Though the text cites Romans 7:22, this is likely a reference to Romans 8:22, which discusses the "whole creation" groaning</note> the entire foundation or circumference of the world with all that is within it. Likewise, in such a specific sense, *the world* is frequently expressed in Holy Scripture, as in *John 1:10: He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not. Matthew 26:13: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world. Mark 16:15: And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.* In these places, and many others like them, it clearly appears that by this must be understood the Globe, and even the creatures who inhabit it.

Whether all this came forth from the so-called *Chaos* <note>original: "Chäos," referring to a state of primordial confusion or a "mangled mixture" of all things</note>, being a completely unsuitable, confused, contradictory, and mixed-up matter; or whether the fundamental particles sprang in all their perfection out of mere Nothing; or otherwise whether the world (the Earth excepted) was created entirely in its absolute beauty, is left to the judgment of the Learned. *Descartes*, called *Cartesius* by the Latinists, that excellent Restorer of Philosophy, may have his own particular way in which he thinks to skillfully explain the foundation of the three primary substances—namely through little spheres and rotating motions <note>This refers to Descartes' "vortex theory," where he imagined the universe filled with particles of matter swirling like whirlpools</note>; yet his opinion seems to rest more on a vain imagination than on steady and convincing proofs. It is not every man’s work to fathom such hidden secrets.

<column-break/>

Likewise, it is not the intention here to strictly describe at what time of the year the world was created: because such is entirely uncertain if one wishes to look at the landscape or climate of Paradise. However, if one lets the eye travel over the entire extent of the Earth, the matter can be resolved much more easily, and it may be said—not without reason—to be "at all times." This is because at one and the same time, the four Seasons of the year—namely Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter—are found together upon the surface of the Earth. Of this, even the blooming and fresh growth of all things convinces us. The ancient Egyptians, who reckoned the beginning of the year from the month of September, are in favor of Autumn, when most all soulless and growing Creatures or fruit-bearing Plants stand fully grown in their youth. The Hebrews begin the civil year from the Month *Tishri* <note>original: "Thifri," a variant of Tishri, the seventh month of the Hebrew ecclesiastical year but the first of the civil year (Autumn)</note>, and besides their so-called Feast of Tabernacles, they have several others. Whatever the case may be, in such a doubtful matter, everyone is free to have his own particular opinion.

Furthermore, the Triune GOD has *created—that is, brought forth out of mere Nothing, and most anciently, in the beginning of time, arranged Heaven and Earth*—meaning not only the circuit of the Sun, but also all the Stars, both fixed and moving (otherwise called wandering stars or planets), alongside the intervening stretches of the endless circumference of the Heavens; having reserved the middle-lying space for the placement and singular execution of the Earth. Certainly, such a rare and almost incomprehensible Arrangement—especially that of the Solar path, whose inner intermediate plane we poor little humans, by God's grace, inhabit for a short time—is an excellent object of our contemplation, and rightly worthy to be displayed upon the Frontispiece of this Work. The other *Theories of the World* are the *Ptolemaic*, or that of *Ptolemy Fig. I.* <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), whose model placed the Earth at the center.</note> and the *Tychonic Fig. II.* <note>Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), who proposed a hybrid model where the Sun orbits the Earth, but other planets orbit the Sun.</note> depicted here; both of which, though they seem to offer something remarkable in their simplicity at first glance, nevertheless sufficiently reveal their own instability through their irregular arrangement, as they are in no way coherent. The first places the Earth at the Center, and positions the rings of the *Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn*, and finally the *Fixed Stars*, all in order as being likewise concentric, or of one and the same center. The second Principle shows two centers on one and the same orbit: namely that of the *Earth* for the *Moon* and *Sun*, and that of the *Sun* for the remaining *Planets*. To these is added a third theory *Fig. III.*, which holds the middle ground between the *Tychonic* and the *Copernican*, and places the *Moon, Sun, Jupiter* and *Saturn* around the *Earth* as the center; and leads *Mercury, Venus* and *Mars* around the *Sun*; in which manner it divides the Mastery of the orbit—which in *Copernicus* is attributed entirely to the *Sun*, and in *Ptolemy* to the always stationary Earth alone—into two.

One sees in *Fig. IV.* the proportionate size of the *Planetary* bodies depicted in relation to the *Sun*, from which drawing it clearly appears that our Earth-globe, when considered on its own in regard to the Sun alone—without even speaking of its incomparable orbit—must be reckoned as a single tiny dot. One can likewise see therein how the Planets appear and what their shapes are when one views them through *Telescopes* <term>Verrekykers: literally "far-seers"</term>.

The aforementioned writer of the sacred pages <note>Referring to Moses, traditionally considered the author of Genesis.</note>, making no further mention of the unmeasured vastness of the Heavens (which he names only simply), continues the Holy Scripture with a closer description of the Earth—that most magnificent dwelling place of humans and animals. In doing so, he left an example for geographers, from which they can learn that to make a proper description of a city, one ought first to speak of the Kingdom or Province in which it is situated.

Those who expect to find here a skillful and precise description of the world, completed in all its essential and proportionate parts, should heed the words of *Heidegger* in *Lecture IV, on the Mind of Creation* <note>original: "Prælect. IV. de Creat gemente"</note>, saying *that the nature of this division of the Universe into Heaven and Earth is like that in Deuteronomy 28:5: "Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store"; that is: whether divided as in your breadbasket and your leavings, or in your barns and remnants; or like the division of Socrates where he distinguishes between what one knows and does not know; or like that of Livy, who divides that which is performed inside or outside the house; or finally like that of a certain Athenian geographer, who was laughed at by the common people for his folly because he divided the entire globe into the Athenian territory and the rest of the land. Indeed, what can be said that is more fitting or better for instruction than to arrange matters so that they are placed opposite or, if you will, next to each other? That is: comparing the small against the large, the finite against the infinite, and Nothingness against the Universe.*

*The Earth was uncultivated, waste, and void, and darkness was upon the deep*, or according to the Greek, *the Earth was invisible and unformed* <note>original: "onzichtbaar en onbereid" - referring to the Septuagint (LXX) translation of Gen 1:2.</note>. L. I. C. 6."</note>. Perhaps the one called *Titan*, in *Irenaeus, Book V* and *Hornius' History of Philosophy, Book II, Chapter 11* <note>original: "Horn. Hift. Philof. L: II. C. 11"</note>, sprang from the same cause. This so-called *Chaotic* or mixed, unworked, and confused globe of Earth, currently still...

One can easily consider the aforementioned *Waste and Void* <note>original: Thohu Vabhohu</note> as a high, deep, and great sphere, consisting of various small bodies, namely Watery, Airy, and Earthy particles wandering through each other in disorder, as the Ancients learnedly intended to say. From this comes that *Darkness upon the Deep*, that thickest and also heaviest Lump, afflicted with the thickest Darkness; for how was it ever possible that the Sun's rays, even when they shine at their most powerful, could penetrate an atmosphere fifty or more, yes perhaps fifty thousand miles large, with their light, since even a thin cloud prevents the shining through of Sunlight? One might perhaps see in this way, with *Clüver* and *Whiston* <note>William Whiston (1667–1752) proposed that the Earth originated from a comet.</note>, in this *Chaotic* or misshapen state of the Earthly sphere, a *Comet* or "tail-star," or else an unformed Planet, a wandering star, surrounded by a thick crust of dark vapors: or otherwise, if one wished to compare the first-created Earth with the renewed or reborn Earth after the general

Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.* It is not at all objectionable what the English propose regarding the so-called *Chaos*, otherwise the *Void*, with their *Atmosphæra Cometieca* or Cometary atmosphere; one may also devise what one wishes regarding this matter, so long as it represents in some way that first-created confusion and disorder of the Earthly sphere. Regarding this, *Whiston's Theory of the Earth, Book II* may be consulted.

...ness, an error to which the thorny and hateful *Spinoza* <note>Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677), a Dutch philosopher whose ideas on God and nature were often condemned as atheism or pantheism by his contemporaries.</note> was entirely bound, since all his most fundamental and principal axioms were of that very nature. To their collective shame, one might say that *Ovidius Naso*, though a pagan, produced much healthier and better thoughts regarding this subject in his *Metamorphoses, Book I*, where he says in his own language:

> *Before the Sea and the Lands, and the Sky that covers all,* <note>original: "Ante Mare & Terras, & quod tegit omnia Cœlum..."</note>
> *Nature had but one face in the whole world,*
> *Which they called Chaos, a raw and unordered mass,*
> *Nothing but a sluggish weight, and the discordant seeds*
> *Of things not well joined together, heaped in the same place.*

Thus brought into Dutch rhyme by the widely renowned poet *Joost vanden Vondel* <note>Often called the "Dutch Shakespeare," Vondel (1587–1679) was the preeminent poet of the Dutch Golden Age.</note>:

> *Before Earth, and Sea, and the waves,*
> *And Heaven, which spans the All, were created,*
> *The entire World and Nature and the world’s state*
> *Had but a single face and a uniform appearance,*
> *Called the CHAOS,* <note>original: "BAYERT"; an archaic Dutch term for the primordial void or a state of confusion.</note> *a misshapen colossus,*
> *And a raw heap of mixing, a heavy, clumsy weight*
> *Of seeds, conflicting and mingled together,*
> *Piled up wildly into one form.*

One must confess that this description—provided one presupposes God as the Creator and moving cause of all things—comes very close to that of *Moses*.

Indeed, who would dare deny that the Earth would ever have become a habitable and fruitful place if the *Spirit of GOD* had not hovered over the waters? That is to say: if the Divine power had not moved and arranged everything. The acting cause of matter, motion, and the collective cause of the Laws of motion, is no less almighty than it is all-wise. He who traces these Laws, institutions, and arrangements enters into GOD’S sanctified mysteries, and surely holds the most capable means at hand to learn to know GOD and to show Him reverence.

By the phrase, the *Spirit of God*, one must not understand a powerful nor a violent wind, according to the opinion of *Onkelos* (a Chaldean Rabbi), *Maimonides*, *Aben Ezra*, *Theodoretus*, *Tertullian*, *Episcopius*, *Hobbes*, *Simonius*, and many others, who have all asserted such for various motives and interests. Likewise, one must not understand it as a primary material Light, as *Fr. Valesius* <note>Francisco Vallés (1524–1592), a Spanish physician and philosopher who wrote "Sacra Philosophia."</note> claims in his *Sacr. Philos. p. 28*; nor the *Sun*, drying out the Earth and Water through the glow of its rays, according to the saying of *Jo. Alba* (a Spaniard mentioned by *Hackspan*). Nor the Angels, as with Cardinal *Cajetan*; nor the so-called *Heleen* <note>A reference to the "Hyle" or "World Soul."</note>, which appears under the name of the *Soul of the World* in the works of *Comenius*, *Crellius*, *Fludd*, *Democritus Christianus*, and others of that kind—most of whom were singular lovers of *Chymistry* <note>original: "Chymie"; referring here to alchemy and early chemical philosophy.</note>. Furthermore, it is not to be understood as any force of Magnetism or Lodestone, by which the entire bodies of the world are pressed toward the general center of gravity and sink down, turning themselves upon their own axes—of which opinion *Leonh. Christ. Sturm* was in his *Clear Explanation of Passages of Holy Scripture, p. 10*. Rather, by the aforementioned expression, nothing else can or may be understood than the *Spirit of God*: that is, the *Spirit of GOD* Himself, the third Person of the Most Holy Trinity, who by His infinite power moved, warmed, and made the Chaos fruitful. That *Spirit, who renews the face of the Earth. Psalm 104:30. Unfelt de Chao Mundi. p. 39.*

Thus *Moses* describes with brief words the origin and first formation of the Earth, yet not in such a way that he absolutely means the entire circuit of the Sun, much less the whole Universe. Indeed, it would strive against all sound reason if someone wanted to imagine that the Earth-lump—still mingled and misshapen—extended as far as the orbit of *Jupiter* or *Saturn*, much less to the Fixed Stars. The sacred Writer makes not the least mention of these Constellations, but speaks only of the physical Point of the Earth itself; describing nothing other than the realities and histories of the ancient world: as one reads in *2 Peter 2:5: ...and spared not the old world... when he brought the flood upon the world of the ungodly.* In this sense the world is also taken in *2 Peter 3:7: ...but the Earth, by the same Word, is kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of Judgment, and perdition of ungodly men.* Certainly, *Moses* openly had in mind only the Chaos or earthly Mixed-heap in the aforementioned text, and not the general confusion and misshapen state of the entire Universe.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical inquiry into the origins of the world. Having discussed the concept of Chaos on the previous page, the author now addresses whether the Universe was created solely for humanity, arguing against such "anthropocentrism" by citing the vastness of the cosmos and the wisdom of both modern scholars and ancient philosophers like Thales.</meta>

<page-num>8</page-num>
<header>SPIRITUAL</header>

This saying seems to provide enough light to resolve the question: was the world created solely for the sake of Mankind? As far as the globe of the Earth alone is concerned, the matter speaks for itself; but such a thing may not be said of the structure of the Universe. Indeed, it would be judged entirely unjust and extravagant if someone wished to claim that the Universe, viewed in its full extent and immeasurable circumference, was brought into being only for Our sake—we humble and earthly mortals. From what has been said above regarding the size of the Earth and the other celestial bodies or constellations, it is sufficiently clear that such a view would utterly overthrow, damage, and turn upside down the magnificent arrangement of all things. It would mean that the most perfect beings of immortal matters would be subject to weak and powerless creatures, and indeed, the boundless Universe, so great and glorious, would be subservient to its smallest and least significant part. Would it not be a shame to maintain that the high Heavens, which we have never even beheld, and the stars so far removed from us—which we are scarcely able to track or reach even with our thoughts—were created and arranged solely for Our sake? It would likewise conflict no less with reason if one established that the infinite number of spiritual and intelligent beings—namely the Angels, whether viewed in higher or lower degrees of exaltation—were brought forth for nothing but the service of Man. In my opinion, this would be as much as saying that Lions and Eagles were born for the sake of Flies, Gnats, and Frogs. Thus speaks *Burnet* in his *Theory of the Earth, page 123.* <note>Thomas Burnet (c. 1635–1715) was an English theologian and geologist known for his "Sacred Theory of the Earth," which attempted to reconcile biblical history with geology.</note> Alongside this may be placed the illustrious testimony of *Samuel Köleser de Keres-eer* in his *Roman-Dacian Gold Mines, page 3*, <note>Samuel Köleséri (1663–1732) was a prominent physician and scientist in Transylvania (Dacia).</note> where he reasons thus: it is certainly far too great a vanity and pride to think that each and every thing was created and brought forth for Man alone, for such thoughts can only arise from an abominable excess of over-inflated self-love. Indeed, what proportion is there between the countless positions of the heavenly bodies, the rapidly rotating mass of the Fixed Stars, and finally the entire starry heavens, and Man? Consider the silent and almost unknown multitude of all kinds of seeds of subterranean plants, covered by the rough bark of the Earth; the hidden architecture of the inner-earthly palace, in the bowels of the Earth, so

<column-break/>

magnificent in itself, even though deprived of sunlight. In a word: all that we see with our eyes, all that affects our senses, all that can be touched and handled with hands and feet—all those occurring and present things, I say, serve the careless and inattentive Man to no use or advantage, unless one attempts to gain the use of them through singular attention, through accurate investigation, and through rightful labor, along with a proper application. It would be absolute folly to imagine that the Earth—that small, remote speck—rightfully deserved, in view of the Glory of all supra-earthly bodies, that so many glittering rays from such a great and vast circumference should have to strike and be confined to the center of the Earth. Furthermore, if there are inhabitants of the Sun, Moon, and Stars, as some have supposed, what would then remain for that breed of "Star-dwellers"? The so-called *Geophili* <note>term: Geophili; literally "Earth-lovers," referring here to those who maintain a geocentric view, placing Earth at the heart of God's purposes.</note>, otherwise lovers of the Earth, who placed it in the center of the Universe, had a certain kind of application for all creatures toward the Earth; but nowadays one sees an endless number of Constellations, entirely indefinite in both mass and distance, and finally, in these last centuries, for the most part discovered and made known. It also does not square well with reason to regard our Earthly globe as the sole target and end of the entire Creation, since a fireball fifty thousand times smaller and not nearly as far from us as the Sun—which is such a vast and excellent body—would have been large enough for the warming and illumination of the Earth. The tradition of the ancient and Pagan Philosophers, who believed the *origin of all things to be from water*, is noteworthy, the more so because it seems to have its derivation from the description of the Earth by Moses, which they possibly did not rightly understand. *Cicero* testifies to this in *The Nature of the Gods, Book I, Chapter 10*, <note>Marcus Tullius Cicero (106–43 BCE), the famous Roman orator and philosopher.</note> where he says: *Thales of Miletus, who first searched for such things, said that water was the beginning of things, but GOD was that Mind which formed everything from Water.* <note>original Latin: "Thales Milesius, qui primus de talibus rebus quæsivit, aquam dixit esse initium rerum, DEUM autem eam Mentem, quæ ex Aqua cuncta fingeret."</note> Upon these words, *Minutius Felix* in *Chapter 19* <note>Marcus Minucius Felix was one of the earliest Christian apologists, writing in the 2nd or 3rd century AD.</note> exclaims as follows: *Oh, the reason for Water and Spirit is higher and more sublime than can be found by Man, having been handed down by GOD. You see the opinion of the primary philosopher is deeply in agreement with ours.* <note>original Latin: "Eho, altior & sublimior Aquæ & Spiritus ratio, quam ut ab Homine potuerit inveniri a DEO tradita. Vides Philosophi principalis nobiscum penitus opinionem"</note>

It bridges early scientific discovery with theology, referencing thinkers like Thales and Cicero to suggest that even ancient pagans recognized a divine mind working through primordial water.</summary>

...to agree with this opinion. <note>original Latin: "nionem consonare"</note> That is: *Truly, there is a more divine and loftier reason for the Earth and the Spirit than can be traced by man, given by GOD.* <note>original Latin: "Verum est divinior quaedam et excelsior ratio Terrae et Spiritus, quam ab homine possit investigari a DEO data esse."</note> You see that the sentiment of the most prominent Philosopher <note>Referring to Aristotle</note> agrees in all parts with our own. This doctrine was certainly among the very first—if ever any other of a similar nature was so widespread—to extend throughout the world, and it appears to have passed from the Jews to the Heathens and other nations. *Anaxagoras*, *Pythagoras*, and even the so-called *Brahmins* <note>The author uses "Brachmannen," referring to the Hindu priestly caste in India</note> (otherwise known as Indian ministers or priests, as can be seen in *Strabo, Book 15*), and almost all the most famous men have followed this sentiment. If anyone wishes to satisfy their curiosity further, they may look up what *Aristotle* says in his own language in *Metaphysics, Book 1, Chapter 3*, where he gives the reason for the infernal flood *Styx*, <note>Styx: In Greek mythology, the river that forms the boundary between Earth and the Underworld.</note> adopted through the use of a curse or oath by the ancient Heathen Gods. Alongside this may also be placed the sentiment of certain *Stoic* Philosophers, and among the moderns, that of the *Helmontians* (or followers of Van Helmont); and finally, there may be added to their advantage the testimony of the Apostle in *2 Peter 3:5*: *...by the Word of GOD the Earth was standing out of the water and in the water*, which words in the translation are rendered thus: *the earth has its standing out of the water and in the water through God's Word.* Furthermore, even modern observations regarding inanimate and growing plants—which are seen to be nourished and grow through the moistening of water—seem to remarkably favor this proposition, accepted by so many, which derives the origins of all things from water. However, *Woodward* <note>John Woodward (1665–1728), an English naturalist who performed early hydroponics experiments.</note> says that there is deception or misunderstanding hidden within this, and demonstrates with irrefutable arguments in his highly learned discourse, *Dissertation on Vegetation*, that the nutrition and growth of plants must not be attributed to the Element of Water in itself, or considered as simple water, but to the Earthy matter that is mixed with the water and hidden within it. *Swedenborg*, in his *Miscellaneous Observations, page 43*, <note>Emanuel Swedenborg (1688–1772), the Swedish scientist and later mystic.</note> likewise attempts to prove that the Globe sprang from water as the very first matter, also from a certain roundness that presupposes a horizontal pressure; from the original softness of all earthly bodies, especially of the outermost and crusty matter, which would have taken their origin 

<column-break/>

from their location under the Sea, or through the outflowing of the same, which even today occupies the largest part of the Earth; or else from the Deluge, or from the very first and fluid matter.

One can avoid almost all obstacles of offense and objection if one considers the Element of water not on its own, nor entirely separated from others, but together with or alongside the Earth; or if one understands the water described by Moses as being impregnated or made fertile with many other parts; or even if one chooses to understand the word *Water* with a much broader meaning for all fluid or moist matter. In this way, even the Air would be fine and thin water. In that same sense, Fish do not only swim through the water, but Birds also fly through it. Likewise, the most fluid and finest celestial air, playing between water and wind, cannot be excluded here. Even the Heavens, called *Schamaim* in Hebrew—just as in that language *Esch* and *Maim* mean Fire and Water <note>The author is using a traditional but linguistically debated etymology of the Hebrew "Shamayim" (Heavens) as a combination of "Esh" (fire) and "Mayim" (water).</note>—seem to be Fire and Water, as if the first word *Schamaim* was composed of the other two, *Esch* and *Maim*, together, though they are not compared to empty or void space because of their fineness. *Fire* itself is fluid. Possibly the aforementioned lovers of water (or, if you will, Water-philosophers, called *Udrophili* in Greek) intended to indicate such a thing by alluding to the word Water. Certainly, in that sense, *Thales* would have meant his *Water*, *Heraclitus* his *Fire*, *Epicurus* and *Democritus* their so-called *Atoms* (or indivisible and placeless little bodies, or particles almost invisible and wandering through the air), and *Aristotle* his *Common Subject* <note>original Latin: "Subjectum Commune"</note> (or General Subject from which all things arise). Probably the *Cartesians* <note>Followers of René Descartes' mechanical philosophy.</note> mean the same with their *Extension* <note>original Latin: "Extensum"</note> (extended, or a broad and long being divided into a multitude of small particles or little bodies); which, however, may only be valid as long as one stays within the circumference or concept of the Earth.

The Creation of the chaotic mass, such as the *Chaos* or *Abyss* <note>The author uses "Bayert," an old Dutch term for the formless void or chaos.</note> has been, in no way conflicts with the Perfection of Divine works. It did not please the Supreme and Solely-Governing Lord to create the Globe in a single moment, entirely and completely in all its parts at one and the same point in time, but successively and one after the other; although it depended solely on the free and unhindered will and Good Pleasure of GOD to bring forth the Universe in but a wink. Just as one must consider a work according to the degree of its elaborateness as a whole, so likewise must this most artistic and...

# SPIRITUAL

<meta>catchword: OUT-</meta>

...be esteemed according to its value as God’s most excellent masterpiece.

It has been God’s will and pleasure to manifest His Omnipotence and Wisdom not only in the magnificent arrangement of a rough and ungraceful Chaos <note>original: "Mengelklomp," referring to the formless matter that existed before the world was ordered.</note>, but also in the wise governance of all creatures, who still daily spread the fame of the Creator through their successive and continuous reproduction, trumpeting His name aloud through a silent eloquence and eternalizing the Glory of their Supreme Lord. The widely renowned <margin>*Hottinger, History of Creation, p. 37.*</margin> <note>Johann Heinrich Hottinger (1620–1667) was a Swiss philologist and theologian.</note> speaks very learnedly on this subject, where he says: God willed first to create an unfit and confused Chaos, which He afterwards brought to perfection, because it pleased Him to leave us a sample of His eternal Wisdom as a fit and useful example for instruction—showing how man ought to ascend step-by-step from the imperfect to the perfect, from the lowly to the Glorious, and from the Earthly to the Heavenly. In this, we are bound by duty to trace that All-Wise Teacher with diligence and industriousness, at least as much as our weakness, supported and strengthened by the Spirit, allows. The Creator intended something else in all His workings that likewise concerns man: namely, that we should give thanks to Him alone for the beginning, progress, and end of all things—both of individual creation and the steady continuation of the same, in body as well as in Spirit—showing our rightful acknowledgment and reverence for all His generous gifts. Furthermore, He has taught man to regard nothing as so hideous or so deformed that he should judge it impossible to ever be changed by the most artistic hand of this Master-Craftsman and covered with a completely different form, wherever and whenever it pleases Him; to the end that one might have proper awe for that wonderful All-Governor, whose judgments are incomprehensible, whose arrangements are unsearchable, and whose Glory is infinite, and wonder at His Omnipotence, through which the Universe could once again become entirely wild and fall into nothingness.

<column-break/>

One shall finally leave the erroneous spirits <note>referring to heretics or those with heterodox views.</note>—who hold the *Darkness upon the deep* to be an absolute evil substance and the direct cause through which all evil came into the world—to their own stubbornness, without wishing to bring anything against their two co-eternal principles, by which they recognize a good and an evil Beginning. Zoroaster, who is held by some to be Ham, the son of Noah, and by others (among whom is Epiphanius) to be a contemporary of Nimrod, may keep his opinion, wherein he maintains that from the beginning there have been two causes: namely Light, to which he ascribes Fatherhood, and Darkness, to which he ascribes Motherhood. One also does not intend here to refute the ancient Persians with their *Oromasdes* and *Arimamus* <note>Referring to Ahura Mazda and Ahriman, the dualistic deities of Zoroastrianism representing good and evil.</note>, the first of whom was a God born of the purest light and the origin and fountainhead of all good; the Other, having come forth from Darkness, they held to be the cause of degenerate Nature. One shall also quietly overlook the Egyptians who, besides their three good Gods *Isis*, *Osiris*, and *Horus*, honored *Samael* <note>Typically a figure in Jewish lore, here equated by the author with Egyptian concepts of darkness or evil.</note> as the Prince of Darkness. The opinion of Pythagoras, who, according to the testimony of *Porphyrius in his life* <note>Porphyry’s "Life of Pythagoras."</note>, honored Darkness as an evil Spirit, may be placed alongside the others. The principle of the Basilidians, or followers of Basilides, who in the second century held *Light* and *Darkness* to be two eternal substances, seems doomed to the dark grave along with that of the Manichaeans, whose principal error was of the same nature as the others. We only wish to assert here that Darkness may by no means be held as an absolute Evil or the cause of it, whether one regards it as an absence or deprivation of the essentially shining Light, or as something that is naturally dark in itself without any essential Light or illumination being presupposed. See concerning this <margin>*Unfelt, Dissertation on Chaos, p. 33.*</margin>

# NATURAL PHILOSOPHY.
## PRINT SHEET III.

*And GOD saw the Light, that it was good: and GOD divided the Light from the Darkness.*
*And GOD called the Light Day, and the Darkness he called Night: And the evening and the morning were the first day. Genesis I. v. 3. 4. 5.*

One might almost call the life of creatures, if it were deprived of Light, a death—or at least an invisible beauty. *With Light, the creation of the world began; through Light, everything that the entire World contained was clarified and made visible. Light brought forth everything that was beautiful and glorious and which lay as if hidden*, says *Theophilus to Autolycus, Book II.* <note>Theophilus of Antioch (2nd century) was an early Christian apologist. This quote emphasizes light as the medium through which the beauty of creation is revealed.</note> GOD, who is an incomprehensible and unapproachable Light, reveals Himself and His Glories to Mankind through Light.

GOD himself, Creator of all things out of Nothing, whose Spirit hovered over the waters *v. 2.* When He was to change the chaotic features of the Chaos <note>original: "Bayerts" – a term referring to the formless, confused mass of matter before the creation of the world</note> or Medley of the Earth into a suitable dwelling place for the service of future Earth-dwellers, has as the sole and eternal Sovereign, as much in Omnipotence as in independent freedom, through CHRIST, the Anointed, called the *Word* in *John I. v. 1.*, calling and awakening the things *which be not as though they were. Rom IV. v. 17.* said; *let there be Light, and there was Light.*

It is indeed probable that the Sunlight and Fixed Stars shone upon the Globe before the work of this first day was perfectly carried out, but that the rays could not penetrate that fluid and thick Medley. As soon as the Earth was unburdened and separated from the airy and watery parts and their intermingling, and was settled upon its center through the power of the Laws prescribed to the world by GOD, it could be clarified by Light. *Then the Light is born, when it begins to act and to shine through the fluid, transparent things.*

Thus it is unnecessary to stipulate that there was a Light distinct from the Sun or Star-light, shining around the Earth, or spread uniformly throughout the whole world, and finally divided into circles in the following days; or with *Rambertus in Chapter I. Genesis p. 69. etc.* to make of Light a general concept of arrangement, movement, and counter-friction; or finally with *Leonhard Christoph Sturm in Plain Explanation of Holy Scripture p. 12.* <note>Sturm (1669–1719) was a German mathematician and theologian who sought to harmonize the Bible with the mechanical philosophy of his time.</note> to ascribe to the Solar circle a certain power of Magnet or Lodestone-like nature and movement.

<column-break/>

One wishes here in no way to dispute *Longinus* <note>Dionysius Longinus, the Greek philosopher to whom the treatise "On the Sublime" is attributed. He famously cited the "Let there be Light" passage as a prime example of the sublime style.</note> and many others regarding what they have said about the sublimity or transcendence of Light. It is true that Moses' description is simple and Historical, but also sublime; and certainly sublime both in respect to the matter itself and in regard to the manner of expression: for who must not absolutely confess that all that, in respect to us, is of GOD or is brought forth by Him, is sublime, glorious, and incomparable.

> The duty of Man requires that highly esteemed be
> All that the Sovereign has ever brought into the Light.

God, in Himself an eternal uncreated Light, did not need the created Light, but brought it forth for the welfare of Mankind and the Earth, so that the inhabitants of the planets <note>original: "Planeetbewoonders" — reflecting the 17th/18th-century scientific view that other planets might be inhabited.</note> might have warmth and illumination from the Light. These effects, proceeding from Light, make the world lively through their influence and decorate the Earth's surface. Thus it is also fitting that Man gives thanks to the great God, that uncreated Light, through whom the created has its being, for His infinite loving-kindness and charity, the more so being convinced that just as GOD is the eternal Light, so is He also eternal Good.

Certainly, the proportional and well-ordered distribution of Light instilled into each particular Planet deserves to be noted with attention

...to be noted, of which our Earthly Globe is surely the foremost and most public witness. If the Chaos <note>original: "Bayert" – a term for the formless mass of matter at the beginning of creation</note>, spoken of above, whether considered Cometic or "tail-starred," <note>original: "Staartstarrig" – an archaic term for comets</note> or *Planetary* or "wandering-starred," <note>original: "Dwaalstarrig" – an archaic term for planets, which appear to move or "wander" against the fixed stars</note> had been placed closer to the Sun or any other shining constellation, undoubtedly the solid bodies would have become soft and thin, the liquid things driven off and scattered, and the form of the Earth, viewed from afar, would have shown itself not as a lit Globe alone, but as a fiery coal or glowing iron. On the contrary, if the Earth had been located further from any Fixed Star, such as the Sun, all the Waters, both above and below, would have frozen and stood fast like icebergs; everything would have stiffened and hardened through excessive cold, yes, even the animate bodies would have been soulless, the living dead and stiff as stony statues. Never would the green Spring have decorated the fields of the air with fragrant flowers, nor the fruitful Summer have provided and fed needy Mankind with a rich Harvest.

> If the Earth had stood closer or further away
> From the Light of Sun or Stars, all would surely have perished;
> Set ablaze by heat, or indeed by cold into Ice
> And stone transformed: thus also never in Paradise
> Would that deadly Wood, that Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil be born;
> Through which the first Man lost his well-being.

Furthermore, GOD saw the *Light, that it was good*; although He knew its goodness absolutely from all eternity, before the *Light* was ever created: and, because He foresaw the goodness and utility of the *Light*, through which the Earth and all other Creatures were to be warmed and made as if alive, through His Omniscience, He brought forth the *Light*. But let no one think that by these words, says *Augustine in "On Genesis against the Manicheans," Chapter 48* <note>original: "Augustinus de Gen. contr. Manichæos" – a work by St. Augustine of Hippo defending the book of Genesis</note>, it is suggested or shown that some unusual, sudden, or unknown good appeared before GOD'S face, as if something strange had occurred to Him, but only that He took pleasure in the perfect Light. We see for ourselves and find, as soon as we but open our eyes, that the *Light* is good and useful; and if we wish to follow what reason instills in us, we shall necessarily have to recognize the inscrutable wisdom, power, and goodness of the Creator, and be driven by that knowledge to thank Him for His invaluable benefits and to worship Him religiously.

Thus it is, that All which GOD has created, all that He still daily brings forth and ever shall bring forth, is good and perfect; good, just as He himself is good, yes, the very best, just as He himself is the very best; good is movement, good are the Laws of movement, which He has established. *He has established them for ever and ever: He has given them a command, which none of them shall transgress. Psalm 148:6. You have ordered all things by measure, number, and weight. Wisdom 11:21.* <note>original: "Sap. XI. 21." – The Book of Wisdom (Sapientia), a book of the Bible found in the Apocrypha or Deuterocanon</note>

<column-break/>

Without doubt, it would have resulted in significant disadvantage, both to our Earthly Globe and to other *Planetary* Spheres, if the presence of Light and warmth had never been interrupted, but had been constant. To be sure, the juices of living Creatures, being too much moved and driven, would have evaporated and become powerless; the Herbs of the Earth would have withered, the Trees and other Plants dried up, and also Men would have been much less able to endure the everlasting Light than the inhabitants of the arid or hot tropics can endure a day of more than twelve hours, or Days that lasted months or years, without discomfort.

For this reason, *Darkness*, or the absence of *Light*, deserves to be esteemed no less than *Light*; since each is good and useful in its particular operation. Opposing things placed next to one another are best distinguished, because one excels or differs more or less from the other.

> One sees distinction best, and can first pass judgment,
> When we place opposites against one another.

Through the *Darkness*, the dying Plants and animate Creatures maintain their life; the tired and weary, like Humans and Animals, have their rest and refreshment through the same. It is also for that reason that GOD *made separation between the Light and between the Darkness*.

Moreover, this change of Light and Darkness—otherwise the disappearance of Light through Darkness—besides the goodness, utility, advantage, and beauty that it contains within itself, has its fixed determinations, degrees, measures, proportionality, and arrangement.

# NATURAL SCIENCE.

D 2

<meta>catchword: what</meta>

If we were deprived of the obscurities of the Night, there would be no opportunity to behold the Stars that sparkle and are visible at night: there would be no means to recognize anything in the Starry Heavens beyond the circuit of the Sun's sphere. *All Astronomy*, says that renowned Astronomer *Kepler* <note>original: "Kleperus" — Johannes Kepler (1571–1630), the German astronomer who discovered the laws of planetary motion</note>, *who in this capacity served and outlived three successive Emperors, rests upon the obscuration of Light, so much so that these darknesses serve as the eyes of Astronomers; these defects of light are an abundance of learning, and these blemishes illuminate and clarify the minds of mortals with the most precious pictures.* <note>original Latin: "Univerfa Aftronomia... Lumen obfcurationibus innititur, adeò, ut hæ tenebræ fint Aftronomorum oculi, hi defectus doctrinæ fint abundantia, hi nævi mentes mortalium pretiofiffimis picturis illuftrant."</note> Truly an excellent testimony, worthy of praise among all nations, for the exaltation and glorification of Darkness and shadows!

The alternation of Light and Darkness, or of Day and Night, according to the very translation of the Holy Writer, is shown in verse 5; *GOD called the Light Day, and the Darkness He called Night.* This is another sign of His Divine Goodness and Wisdom.

It pleased the Most High and Most Gracious Creator to arrange the Day and the Night for the convenience and welfare of the Earthly Dwellers, and possibly also for the service of the *Inhabitants of the Planets* <note>A common 18th-century speculation that other planets were inhabited by intelligent beings</note>, in such a way that the Day and the Night would arise in a certain measure and proportional alternation, as required for the preservation and lasting state of the common good of those who would enjoy the utility and comfort of this pleasant change. He did not wish that the full *Day* should suddenly turn into the thickest *Darkness*, nor on the contrary that the *Darkness* should change in a single moment into a bright Day, because the Earth could have endured such a change much less than a prisoner, who is suddenly brought from a deep and dark dungeon into the Sunlight, can endure the power of the rays. Thus it was necessary that the *Day* should arise gradually, and the *Night* should cover the Earth almost imperceptibly through a moderate fading of the Light. Upon this is founded the institution and use of *twilight* <note>original: "fcheemeringe"</note> through the weakening or withdrawal of the rays.

Asia alone, as the birthplace of the first of Mankind, was not to have the sole privilege in the full enjoyment of the

<column-break/>

Day and the Night; in such a benefit, being universal, the entire Earth had to have its share through the warming by *Day*, and through the refreshment of the *Night*. Thus it has pleased the all-wise mercy of GOD to provide for all living Creatures created within the first six days, and those to be born in later times, equally throughout the entire world.

For that reason, the movement of the Sun, or, to put it better, the rotation of the Earth past the *Equator* <term>Middellinie: literally 'middle line', the equator</term> would by no means have satisfied the Creator’s aim; for the regions situated under the Southern span of the Sun’s path would have been uninhabitable; and those lying under the Equator would be stifled and scorched by the constant heat; and those extending toward the span between the Northern and Southern *Poles* <note>original: "Afpunten" — literally 'axis points'</note> would have been stiffened and suppressed by the sharpest and everlasting cold. Thus it was necessary that the Sun, in its turn, approach the Northern as well as the Southern Pole, so that through that equal rotation all living Creatures on Earth might be preserved. This the most provident Creator of the Universe carried out through the regular movement past the Equator, from which the *Ecliptic* <note>original: "Eclipfis" — here referring to the Ecliptic, the sun's apparent path which creates the seasons</note> or the obscuration of both Sun and Moonlight arises, and the distinction of *Days* and *Nights* has its origin, whether in each place of the world in particular, or in one region in respect to another.

If in those lands or regions situated under the Equator, or directly under the South, the Day lasted longer than twelve hours, everything would undoubtedly wither from the heat; and on the contrary, if the days were shorter, or if there were fewer Weeks and Months in those regions lying under and within the span of both Poles, everything would perish from the cold.

By this well-ordered and successive change of *Light* and *Darkness*, of *Days* and *Nights*, one must firmly presuppose that the movement of the Earth is perfect or centric every day, or that it makes its full round daily, so that one land or region of the world after another is turned past the Sun; or otherwise, that the Sun runs around the immovable and stationary Earth within the time of twenty-four hours; just as meat stuck on a rotating roasting-spit is roasted by the fire, or as if one would want to move the fire around the meat. Finally, that difficult and oft-disputed question comes down to...

# SPIRITUAL

what more accords with reason?

What *Cluverus* <note>original: "Cluverus" — Johannes Clüver (1593–1633), a German theologian and historian who wrote 'Geologia sive de mundo'</note> supposes in his *Geology* regarding a *Six-Year* instead of the common *Six-Day* Creation is very allegorical. The production of the Animals seems to Him disproportionate to the duration of an ordinary Day, or the interval between Day and Night. He holds the same view regarding the assembly of the Earth's watersheds and the production of growing things. If, during the central rotation of the Earth (which, however, remains to be demonstrated), there was no pause or alternation of Light and Darkness before the fall of the first Man, it would have constituted a full Year, rather than an ordinary Day. Nor can one deny that Years are often taken for Days, and Days for Years in Holy Scripture. Absolute examples of this can be found in *Genesis 4:3, Numbers 14:34, Ezekiel 4:5 and 6, Daniel 12:11, and Revelation 11:3, 12:6.* Furthermore, it is well known that the *Memory* of the Creation was traditionally celebrated in Judaism not only on one day or daily, but also once every seven years, and what is more, every seven times seven Years; that is, every forty-nine Sabbatical Years, according to *Leviticus 25:3 and 8.* Also, no one can contradict that the common and most customary interpretation of the *six Workdays*—whereby the tiny speck of the Earth, one of the least among the other Planets or wandering stars, is usually allotted four full days—is disproportionate and unfair, while the Sun, Moon, and the remaining Stars are granted no more than one Day for their specific Creation. There were certainly learned men, even in ancient times, who hardly dared to determine specifically what kind of Days the six-day Creation consisted of. Hear what *Augustine* says on this: *qui Dies cujusmodi sint, aut perdifficile nobis, aut etiam impossibile cogitare, quanto magis dicere. L. II. de Civitate Dei. Chapter 6.* <note>original Latin: "What kind of days these were is either very difficult for us to think about, or even impossible, much more so to say." From 'The City of God'</note> That is: *it would be very difficult for us, or even impossible to think, much more to say, what nature or character those very first Days possessed.* Meanwhile, it is a certain matter that the *All-Creator* and *Sovereign Lord*, had it pleased Him, could have carried out the complete production of the Whole Universe in a single moment. Likewise, it is certain that it depended solely on the Creator's nod and free will to produce the entire World within the time of six Days or indeed of six Years. However this may be, it is safest to hold fast to the common and everywhere

followed counting of the Days.

*Evening* and *Morning* are presented here as the principal parts that make up a whole natural Day. For this reason, the *Evening-Morning* in *Daniel 8:14* is called *Erebb-Boker* <note>Hebrew: "Ereb Boker"</note> by the Hebrews: *Bochart Hieroz. Part I. Book II. Chapter 3. page 84.* <note>original: Samuel Bochart (1599–1667), a French Protestant scholar who wrote 'Hierozoicon', a treatise on the animals of the Bible</note> In this country, according to the Dutch language, one would say *Evening* and *Morning*, understanding by the word *Morning* the entire Day of *Tomorrow*, so long as the Sun shines upon our horizon; with this distinction, however, that the word *Morning* taken in that sense does not mean what *Others*, and even our countrymen—indeed all Europeans in general—commonly understand by it, namely the *Dawn*, *Morning*, or *Forenoon alone*: just as the *Evening* is taken for the other part of the Day, or for the latter part of the Afternoon.

Upon the aforementioned verse, not only the ancient *Days of the Jews* but also the modern ones of the *Italians* seem to be based, which are reckoned as one Day from one Evening to the next. The *Romans*, *Egyptians*, *Astronomers*, and even we ourselves commonly reckon the Day from one Midnight to the next. Among the *Babylonians* and *Greeks*, each Day began and ended with the *Rising of the Sun*. The Jews were not free to celebrate their Feast days otherwise than according to the institution of the first Day. Regarding this, one sees a clear command from the Lawgiver in *Leviticus 23:32*: *It shall be unto you a Sabbath of rest, and ye shall humble your souls: on the ninth of the month at evening, from evening unto evening, shall ye rest your Sabbath.* Or, *It is a Sabbath of rest to you, and you shall humble and afflict your Souls on the ninth Day of the seventh Month; from Evening to Evening shall you celebrate your Sabbath.*

It seems all too high-flown and allegorical, that which the aforementioned *Leonhard Christoph Sturm* <note>German architect and writer (1669–1719)</note> in his *Understandable Explanation of passages of Holy Scripture, page 2*, posits as beyond matters of faith: namely, that the six-day Creation should be a model for the six-thousand-year state of the World. He intends to suggest by this that just as the entire work of Creation lasted six Days, the world would likewise remain in existence for six thousand Years: as if the Creation were a prelude to the *Restoration of all things*, and the Church had to depart toward a certain divine oracle. The Highly Learned Mr. *Dr. Johann Wilhelm Baier* <note>original: "Jo: Guil. Bajer" — a Lutheran theologian at Altdorf (1647–1695)</note>, a prominent theologian of Altdorf, in his Preface to the mentioned book, considers this opinion or mere guess...

...which is more in agreement with reason?

What *Cluverus* <note>Detlev Clüver (c. 1645–1708), a mathematician and scholar</note> supposes in his *Geology* regarding a *Six-year* instead of the common *Six-day* Creation is very symbolic. The production of the animals seems to him to be disproportionate to the duration of an ordinary day, or the interval between day and night. He holds the same opinion regarding the complexity of separating the waters from the Earth and the production of growing things. If the rotation of the Earth on its axis (which, however, remains to be demonstrated) before the fall of the first human involved no pause or alternation of light and darkness, then a "day" would have comprised an entire year rather than an ordinary day. One also cannot deny that years are frequently taken for days, and days for years, in the Holy Scripture. Absolute examples of this are found in *Genesis 4:3, Numbers 14:34, Ezekiel 4:5 and 6, Daniel 12:11, and Revelation 11:3 and 12:6.* Furthermore, it is well known that the *remembrance* of Creation was celebrated among the Jews not only on one day or daily, but also once every seven years, and what is more, every seven times seven years—that is, every forty-nine Sabbatical years, according to *Leviticus 25:3 and 8.* Also, no one can deny that the most common and customary interpretation of the *six working days*—whereby the tiny speck of the Earth, one of the least among the other planets or "wandering stars," is usually assigned four full days—is disproportionate and unfair, since the Sun, Moon, and the remaining stars are granted no more than one day for their specific creation. There have certainly been learned men, even in ancient times, who hardly dared to determine with certainty what the nature of the days of the six-day creation was. Hear what *Augustine* says on this: <note>original: "qui Dies cujusmodi sint, aut perdifficile nobis, aut etiam impossibile cogitare, quanto magis dicere. L. II. de Civit. Dei. C. 6."</note> *What kind of days those first days were is either very difficult or even impossible for us to imagine, and much more so to describe.* Meanwhile, it is a certain thing that the Creator and Supreme Lord, had it pleased Him, could have completed the perfect production of the Universe in a single moment. Likewise, it is certain that it depended solely on the Creator's nod and free will to produce the entire world within the span of six days or indeed six years. Be that as it may, the safest course is to hold fast to the common and universally followed division of the days.

Upon the aforementioned verse, it seems that not only the ancient days of the *Jews* are based, but also those of the modern *Italians*, which are counted as one day from one evening to the next. Or: It is a Sabbath of rest for you, and you shall humble and oppress your souls on the ninth day of the seventh month; from evening to evening you shall celebrate your Sabbath.*

### PLATE IV.

*And GOD said: let there be an Expanse in the midst of the waters; and let it divide the waters from the waters.*
*And GOD made the Expanse, and divided the waters which were under the Expanse from the waters which were above the Expanse: and it was so.*
*And GOD called the Expanse Heaven: and the evening and the morning were the second day.* **Genesis I. v. 6, 7, 8.**

The work of the previous day, otherwise said of *Yesterday*, which was the very first Day in time, and consequently the beginning and head of all succeeding ages, consisted in the Creation of Light, or the orbit of the Sun around the Earth: or otherwise, if one wishes to establish it so, the central rotation of the Earth; from which the distinction of Day and Night, and consequently some illumination of the Earth- Water- and Air-globe has come. Today the Creator proceeds through his ever-working power and wisdom by more and more purifying and separating the Atmosphere <term>Dampkring: literally "vapor-circle," referring to the envelope of air and mist surrounding the Earth</term>, which currently still consists of a chaotic mixture of the remaining elements. The watery parts mostly descend and remain upon the surface of the Earth, forming a water-circle <note>The hydrosphere</note>, by which the entire terrestrial globe is surrounded and, as it were, enclosed. Through this, the uppermost or hanging waters have formed the Clouds. Thus the *Air* cleared up, so that the work of this Day may, not without reason, be called a purification of the Atmosphere with which the terrestrial globe was surrounded, or indeed a general illumination.

If one wishes to understand the matter as it has been established, the aforementioned *expanse CD*—called in the Hebrew language *Rakia* or *Rakiang* <note>Hebrew: רָקִיעַ</note>; in the Greek *Stereoma* <note>Greek: στερέωμα, meaning a solid structure or foundation</note>; and in the Latin *Firmamentum*—must be viewed as Air, through which the lower waters B C, which surrounded the entire terrestrial globe, are separated from the upper ones, namely the Clouds E. Truly a work of God’s Omnipotence, no less useful than glorious, and above all necessary for the production and means of life for all Plants and Animals, which were to be created shortly thereafter. A wise and prudent work of a single Day, whereby a certain portion of the Waters was arranged here below by GOD to fill the hollow channels and trenches—or, to put it better, those which afterwards had to be deepened and hollowed out in the surface of the Earth by the flood and the scouring of water—from which the Seas, Rivers, and all kinds of Springs have their origin: the other portion of the waters being used by the Creator with equal providence for Clouds. Now, if one assembles the mentioned upper waters or Clouds and counts them as one body, then one may call the Air that is between this portion of Waters and the Earth an interspace or an inter-partition; yet, if one views them as being scattered and extended everywhere equally through the clearing of the Heavens around the entire Atmosphere, then one might say that it is a cohesive expanse, or rather a cohesive and yet at the same time a divided expanse, through which countless water-vesicles <note>The author uses a contemporary 18th-century theory that clouds were made of microscopic "water bubbles" or "blaasjes" that allowed them to float.</note> are held together and extended, so that each swims on its own and can be driven by the wind.

### P L A T E V.

**O**ne may often say with the proverb that there is almost nothing new under the Sun: since one daily finds that, just as with Men, matters, and facts, likewise opinions and particular theories have their fluctuations, entrances and exits, returns or renewals; being regarded and cheered as Divine Oracles at one time, while at another they are disparaged, rejected, and cried out against. It also happens frequently that antiquated and almost worn-out things appear under a modern finery. In this way, the Highly Learned Mr. *Christ. Leonh. Sturm* in *Intelligible Explanation of Holy Scripture p. 14* <note>Christoph Leonhard Sturm, an 18th-century commentator who applied physical laws to the Bible.</note> seems to dress up and bring to light that old and almost forgotten opinion regarding the permanent and *Crystalline Spheres*, representing the supra-terrestrial or Heavenly waters, as if with a new garment. However, he brings us closer to the matter from the Starry-heaven, above which he had placed the Upper-waters, having invented a Hypothesis which, if it pleases the Learned, could be regarded as something new; yet worthy of occupying this Plate, so that others may judge whether it deserves any observation and attention. In this Hypothesis, the very first created Earth appears with an entirely new shape and face, because the Sunbeams are here dispersed and extended everywhere, yet broken <note>Refracted.</note> toward the side of the two poles, whereby the great heat of the Torrid Zone is moderated, and nearly the entire Terrestrial Globe is granted an equal amount of warmth, or at least a temperate air: one might almost say a perpetual Spring <note>The "Perpetual Spring" was a common 18th-century theory suggesting that before the Great Flood, the Earth's axis was not tilted, resulting in a perfect climate.</note>, which was likely the primary cause of the long and healthy lives of the first men. Let us establish by example that A. is the Earth, B. the Air; C. the shell of the Upper-waters, spread around the Terrestrial Globe at a certain distance, in the manner of a vault or shell, in which the Egg S 1. lies enclosed. If the Clouds, or the celestial Waters above, were coarser, thicker, larger, and more numerous, the Earthly globe inhabited by mortals would be unable to receive sufficient Light or warmth from the Sun: it would rain too abundantly and snow too much; one would see thicker and heavier hailstones falling. The Springs and Brooks would swell beyond measure and more than was necessary; the Rivers and other floods would overflow, and finally, the entire surface of the Earth would be submerged under water, just as happened at the time of the Great Flood <note>The author refers to the Deluge of Noah as a literal historical event caused by an imbalance in these "upper waters."</note>. On the contrary, if the Clouds were finer, thinner, and fewer in quantity and number, we would lack the necessary rain and snow; the frequent frosts would destroy the Crops and Herbs of the Earth; then a too-fierce cold would arise, then again an immoderate heat. The Springs and Brooks would dry up; the Trees would wither, and the Rivers would lose their flow. If they stood fixed and immovable in one place, without being able to be driven everywhere by the wind, then all those Regions or Provinces not situated directly beneath them would be deprived of many useful benefits; while the others would have to undergo heavy inconveniences, both from the constant shadow or dampness and from the abundant downpours, hailstorms, etc., as well as from the continuous heat of the burning Sun.

It was very useful and beneficial to the Earth that the Clouds were mobile and active; from this has arisen that advantageous and so necessary use of the *Winds*, on whose wings those fruitful rain clouds—drawn up from the Sea by the Sun and pressed downward from the high mountains—are transported now and then over all regions, Lands, Villages, Fields, and Forests for the well-being of the Earth and poured out. Which Winds also come into consideration in this place, since they are a fluid and floating Air, and besides infinite other conveniences and advantages, serve as such a glorious means for the life and preservation of all Creatures, for the Commerce of Men, and especially for navigation.

Thus we descend step by step from the Sublime to the humble, from the High to the low, from the Heavenly to the Earthly: that is, from the Upper Works to the Lower Creatures, among which the Earthly and Watery Globe, of which we here specifically speak, is surely the most prominent. *He who sends the springs into the valleys, so that they walk between the mountains.
