They give drink to all the beasts of the field, etc. He waters the mountains from His upper chambers: the Earth is satisfied with the fruit of Your works.* And in other places, he frequently cries out with gratitude: *Who shall express the mighty acts of the Lord, or show forth all His praise?* <note>These are references to Psalm 104:10–13 and Psalm 106:2.</note>

Whether this rising of the mountains and the sinking of the valleys, or the upheaval and tearing of the paths and topsoils by the movement of the Earth, or perhaps by the power of fire, occurred before as well as after the Deluge <term>Zondvloed (The Great Flood of Noah)</term>, shall not be further investigated here. Let it suffice that GOD’S will alone was powerful enough to do so. For who does not understand that if the topsoils of the Earth had all remained so elevated and equally high, it would have been impossible for the waters to flow down from higher places to lower ones, much less to the subterranean hollows.

Stand here, *God-loving reader*, stand here a while and worship GOD, that most provident and ingenious Architect, Land-and-World-measurer; observe with attention those excellent signs and eternal remnants of His wisdom; notice that perfect proportion of the elevations in respect to the depressions, of the protruding parts with the hollowed ones, of the dry with the watery. Admire His singular arrangement, especially in such a general state of confusion and disorder; admire, I say, that magnificent foundation of Divine Architecture, whose methods might nevertheless appear to some to be entirely displaced and confused by such decay or collapse. Notice that inexhaustible and bottomless Moisture-cellar of the Sea-waters, which is nevertheless made according to the constitution of the Earth and for its well-being. See those sky-high Mountains of Water, which at every moment discharge themselves into the Sea through countless outflows and inflows of even the largest Rivers; against which, however, the Sea exercises no right of equal treatment by flooding the Earth in its turn. Note at the same time that on the one hand, just as much water is either driven away and taken by the winds or sheltered within the subterranean watercourses, as comes flowing in on the other. With what wonder must we regard that wild expansion of the boundaries, both for the liquid and for the dry—that is, for the Waters and for the Earth—established by GOD? How rare is 그 constant circulation and action of the Waters, not only through the bowels and the surfaces of the Earth, but also through the very Air. Let no one think to doubt whether there were Seas and Lakes in the first World before the Deluge, since one is sufficiently convinced of this, both by the present testimony of Holy Scripture, which explicitly teaches such, and by the abundant multitude of remains and monuments—even of walrus teeth <note>original: "Walrus-tanden"</note>, ribs, vertebrae, and other fish and sea-shells—which are still found in the world today.

The Voice of GOD—who, just as He creates everything through His Omnipotence in verse 6, thus forms everything through His infinite Wisdom in verse 10—teaches the Naturalist the distinction *between Earth and Water, between the Solid and the Liquid:* two general fundamental rules for surveyors as an example of how Land-measuring <term>Landmeetkunde (Geometry/Surveying)</term> ought to be divided into Geography <term>Landbeschryvinge (Description of Land)</term>, understood in a narrow and definite sense, and also into Hydrography <term>Waterbeschryvinge (Description of Water)</term>.

In my opinion, it will be no less pleasant and entertaining than useful and profitable to display the almost innumerable and wonderful variety and nature of *Flowers* in this place. Knowledge of them is all the more necessary because on this Plate only such examples and characteristics are shown that nearly all plants that could ever be produced by Nature in the world can be brought here and must be applied to the Primary Flowers presented here; in which the method of *Tournefort* <note>Joseph Pitton de Tournefort (1656–1708) was a French botanist famous for creating a system of plant classification based on the shape of the flower corolla.</note> and his own divisions and indications have been followed.

I. Herbs and Plants that produce single-petaled flowers, like Little Bells.

Among which some are shaped like single bells (marked A); others like elongated or tube-like bells, wide at the top and broad at the bottom (B); some are more open or wider in bloom, like a bowl or dish (C). Others have round-bellied flowers, like hollow globes, closing narrowly at the opening (D). To this sort belong Mallow, Gourd, and Bellflower.

### P L A T E X.

> *And GOD said: Let there be Lights in the Firmament of the Heaven to divide the Day from the Night; and let them be for Signs, and for Seasons, and for Days, and Years.*
> *And let them be for Lights in the Firmament of the Heaven to give Light upon the Earth: and it was so.* Genesis 1:14, 15.

->*Today shine SUN and MOON, two bright Eyes of Heaven,*<-
->*Which, as Witnesses of the Creator’s Omnipotence,*<-
->*Drive their team of Fire and Light around the Globe,*<-
->*So that we might know GOD’S Almighty Power by Day and Night.*<-

Today, the artistic and magnificent stage of this world is opened for the first time and glorified by the light of the sun. The glittering Stars, both the *Fixed* and the *Wandering Stars* <note>term: "Dwaalstarren" (Wandering stars), an old term for the planets</note>, newly created, now make their brilliance excel across the entire earth, as the air has been further purified and cleared. It is now that the Sun first begins to be the Sun of the Earth—a "World-torch," which is to say, for the service and benefit of the same. Now its light and warmth serve for the use, refreshment, and preservation of the Earth. Wondrous is the arrangement and mercy of the Almighty GOD, who is pleased to use the greatest and, if one may say so, the noblest being of the Universe for the service of a grain of sand—indeed, a speck of dust—compared to that All-illuminating World-torch and (to our weak sight) almost unobservable Eye of Heaven, for the convenience and well-being of the Earth. The greater is subject to the lesser. The exalted Sun serves the lowly Earth. It is a remarkable thing that the material Sun first shone on the Fourth Day and shared its light with the Earth, just as the Eternal Sun of Righteousness, CHRIST our Savior, in the Four-thousandth Year <note>This refers to traditional biblical chronologies, such as that of James Ussher, which placed the birth of Jesus 4,000 years after the Creation</note> after the Creation of the World, deigned to dwell among mortal men on Earth in human form.

<column-break/>

It is well known that one Star is placed incomparably higher than another, and consequently, one is significantly farther from our Earthly globe than another. This is clearly evidenced by a certain difference, called *Parallaxis* <note>original: "Parallaxis" (Parallax); the displacement or difference in the apparent position of an object viewed along two different lines of sight</note> in Latin, which is clearly found to exist between one Star and another; for this reason, it is the surest means and the safest way by which the Heavenly lights are customarily observed and their true position can be measured. If someone were to ask, *How then are those Stars placed in the Firmament of Heaven?* one would present to such a curious Lover of Astronomy the Principal Proposition of EMPEDOCLES <note>Empedocles (c. 490–430 BCE) was a Greek pre-Socratic philosopher</note> regarding the *Double Sun* <note>original: "de Duplici Sole"</note>; which in all parts agrees with the Account of Moses. The opinion of this Philosopher and Astronomer was that there is a certain first-created, original, and Essential *Fire* enclosed in the center of the chaotic World-globe; the other Sun he believed to be the reflection or radiation of this Fire, by which our atmosphere is outwardly shone upon and illuminated. Without doubt, such a general central *FIRE* existed in the beginning (verse 1): but the other first appeared on the Fourth Day, when it illuminated the air with its rays. This ancient opinion and thought—

This conception regarding the sunlight has been recently renewed and, as if dug up from the dark grave of oblivion, brought back into the light by that excellent astronomer <term>Starrekyker: literally "star-gazer," a common 18th-century term for an astronomer.</term> and world-famous engraver **Joh. Christoph. Eimmart** in his *New Graphic Contemplation of the Sun* <note>original: "Ichnograph. nova Contemplat. de Sole"</note>. If one were to assume that the atmosphere—which until then had remained in its disordered state of <term>Baaiert: a Dutch term for a chaotic, primordial state of matter, similar to "the void."</term>—was like a rough and unpolished glass, then today, being the fourth Day of Creation, it might be compared to a glass that, though slowly and gradually ground, is now smooth and fully polished. For example, in **Figure I**, let **HDG** be the Earth. **EBCF** is the vapor-circle or atmosphere. **ABC** is a semi-circle, pointed at the top, of solar rays shooting down from the sky onto the atmosphere. **BC** is the base of the aforementioned inverted circle, which tapers to a point at **BDC**, at whose point **D** is the observer's eye. This being established, one will find that there are as many suns, in the manner of reflections in a rainbow or a cloudy halo around the moon, as there are eyes. Because of this, it often happens that one metaphorically "embraces a cloud instead of Juno" <note>An ancient Greek idiom meaning to mistake an illusion for reality. According to myth, Ixion tried to seduce the goddess Juno (Hera), but Jupiter replaced her with a cloud.</note>; that is, that we take a shadow for a person, or otherwise, consider the image of the Sun to be the Sun itself. What is more, I dare to say that we humans, with our entire globe, live, wander, and exist partially within the Sun itself.

This proposition is confirmed by daily experience, which clearly shows us that in certain regions of the North, the Sun never sets so far that its light vanishes. Even though it has descended below our horizon, it can still be seen by those inhabitants, namely by means of the refracted or reflected solar rays **AC** from **C** onto **F**, as seen in **Figure II**. Meanwhile, ingenious men, whose understanding has been sharpened by experience, may freely pass their judgment on these main theses, as everyone is free to feel about them as they wish.

Be that as it may, it is nevertheless certain that the two *Lights* spoken of here are bodies that either have their own light or otherwise borrow it from others; we speak here primarily of the Sun, Moon, wandering stars <note>Planets</note>, and fixed stars, insofar as they provide their light for the service of the inhabitants of Earth, and indeed even for the inhabitants of planets, if such beings indeed exist. Regarding the latter, one can consult **Huygens** in his *Cosmotheoros* <note>Christiaan Huygens (1629–1695) was a Dutch scientist; his book *Cosmotheoros* speculated on the existence of life on other planets.</note>, where he treats extensively of their days, nights, signs,

<column-break/>

and seasons. The aforementioned two great lights, namely the Sun and the Moon, besides all the other stars, are presented and shown first to the Jews, and also to all other mortals of the world, not as independent bodies that were born of themselves and remain in existence through their own power; but as beings which, regarding their essence, origin, light, movement, effect, and significance, depend absolutely upon their Creator. They are clear signs of GOD’S omnipotence, so that all rational creatures, recognizing their Lord through His wonders and blessings, should never deviate from their rule of conduct through a faithless denial, nor fall away from the Creator to the creatures—from the True Religion, which is owed to GOD alone—into the foolish and idolatrous worship of the Sun or Moon. This would be following the godless example of the **Cainites**, or the descendants of **Cain**, who, according to the testimony of the famous **Heidegger** in his *History of the Patriarchs* <note>original: "Hist. Patr. Exerc. VIII. Tb 4."</note> following **Maimonides** <note>A famous medieval Jewish philosopher.</note>, worshipped the stars. As for other idol- and star-worshippers and despoilers of GOD’S honor who have arisen in later times, we shall pass them all by in silence.

The steady alternation of Day and Night, two singular blessings from GOD, arises from the rotation of the Earth around its own center. For if there were no rotation, only one half of the globe would enjoy the sunlight and warmth; indeed, what is worst, all regions and provinces situated on the illuminated and warm side would be scorched by immoderate heat. On the contrary, those on the other side, covered with thick and everlasting darkness, would entirely stiffen and perish from the continuous, fierce cold. Furthermore, if this rotation were slower or faster, it would result in the usual and determined time of Day and Night lasting more than twenty-four hours in one place and less in another through their irregular alternation.

Likewise, the years are measured and determined according to the annual revolution of the Earth within that most fluid wheel, but mostly according to the most exquisite measures of Divine Wisdom. Now let **Momus** <note>The Greek god of satire and mockery; here used to represent a cynical critic.</note>, that senseless talker, assert if he dares that this revolution could be completed within the time of six months. What would follow? That the fixed seasons of the year would be half as short, and consequently, the cold winter would come upon us sooner,

If He desired that the movement were slower and more sluggish, then the <term>Principal Seasons: referring to the four seasons of the year.</term> would be more extended and long-lasting; consequently, it would be Summer for longer than was useful, whereby everything would wither; one would not be able to gather the harvest more than once within the span of two years. The Winter would last an entire year, whereby our entire supply of food would be completely hindered and taken from us by frost and cold.

The *Seasons*, namely of the *Year*, are based on the point of the Earth which does not stand straight up and down above the plane of the <term>Ecliptic: the apparent path of the Sun across the sky, or "Sun-circle."</term>, but lies deviated by 23 1/2 degrees to the side; if one wished to remove that deviation, the condition of the Earth—far from being considered an Edenic or Earthly-Paradisal state of prosperity and happiness, as some have imagined or dreamed—would beyond doubt be the most miserable and disastrous. It would be the end of all the Northern Peoples; those unhappy earth-dwellers would be utterly lost, because the Sun could never share her light more closely with them than she does now in the Spring and in the Autumn, while the other regions of the world would be oppressed and perish from too great a heat due to the continuous and unchanging position of the Sun above the Equator. Otherwise, if one were to suppose that the movement of the Axis were generally changeable and inconstant in its deviation, the condition of all things would surely be the most unhappy, because one would fall from one extreme to the other; that is to say, there would be too sudden a leap, namely from the very harshest cold, which the Greenlanders feel in <term>January: literally "the Louw-month," an old Dutch name for the first month of the year.</term>, to the most scorching heat, which even the Moors and Southerners could scarcely endure.

Furthermore, the *Days*, mentioned for the second time—namely the *Length of the Days*—serve as an irrefutable sign of Divine Goodness, because they step out and complete their course with equal strides alongside the various Seasons of the year.

Who must not confess that all these incontrovertible proofs absolutely convince us that the aforementioned Great Lights of the heavens were given to Man by GOD as perfect and public signs of His Omnipotence, Wisdom, and bottomless Loving-kindness, which He still daily demonstrates to His creatures through so many almost incomprehensible wonders? Added to this is their singular usefulness for the convenience and use of Men, who find annually that through their fixed course, the various Seasons of the year, the Days, Nights, and Months are measured and determined. So too are various uncommon workings of Nature, atmospheric phenomena, heavenly sights, the Solar and Lunar eclipses (otherwise called *Eclipses*), as well as those that occur on **Jupiter**, one of the seven primary planets. Furthermore, the state of the air and the changeability of the weather, winds, storm and tempest, ebb and flood, the turbulence of the sea—in a word, all the vicissitudes of the Earth are measured and determined by them. They serve, moreover, as certain precursors of the general plagues and scourges of the world, as safe and faithful guides for navigation, and as infallible measures of longitude, etc. Everything thus being perfectly arranged by Divine Providence in the course of nature, mortals must necessarily confess that it is a foolish and entirely useless effort which they employ in the invention and application of certain "Signs" sought by the stubbornness of one or another conceited <term>Star-gazer: an 18th-century term that could refer to astronomers, but here specifically targets astrologers.</term> and derived from the appearances and influence of the stars. By these signs, like ridiculous soothsayers, or to put it better, wicked tricksters, they predict the vicissitudes and changes of Kingdoms, Principalities, Republics, and other such worldly matters; as also the death or long life of Kings, Princes, and prominent men, the fortunes of all men in general, the durability of times of peace, or the approaching disasters of bloody wars, etc., with which such a sort of people often tend to fill the heads of the gullible and deceitfully mislead them.

Finally, these heavenly lights are not only given to us as signs, but also as *Lights*, that is, as brightly burning earthly torches and general world-tapers, which illuminate the wild and great dwelling-place of mortals—the lowly Earth—through their glittering rays and glorify it with a new radiance; just as the same are called with emphasis, or with a sublime manner of speaking in *Ezekiel 32:8* <note>original: "Echel. # P L A T E XI.

*And GOD made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also. And GOD set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth, And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and GOD saw that it was good. And the evening and the morning were the fourth day. Genesis 1:16, 17, 18, 19.*

> The starry roof, sown with nearly countless LIGHTS,
> Which each perform their duty in the service of Man,
> Confirms through its Radiance GOD'S Power and Glory,
> And points us to the path that leads us to Heaven.

God thus made on the fourth Day, or brought to completion, that which he had already begun and made previously. The Perfect changes into more than Perfect, a literal expression or time-signification in which the Hebrew language is deficient <note>The author is referring to the nuances of Hebrew verb tenses (the perfective aspect), which can imply an action started in the past is now fully realized.</note>. He divides the Dominion of Light, and commits the principal and proper part or office, namely that of the *Day*, to the *Sun*, and the other, that is the alternating Dominion of the *Night*, to the *Moon*: so that the first has her own Light, and the other a borrowed shine or reflection. From this it appears that the *Sun* alone has remained the Sovereign of *Light*, the Ruler of the Day, and the universal Light-giver; whereas for the *Moon*, that bright and pleasant Queen of the Night, that dutiful Guide in the darkness, no more than the Vice-royalty has fallen to her share.

The proportion of the *Sun* in size relative to the *Earth* is as 1,369,078 to

<column-break/>

one; that is, like one million three hundred sixty-nine thousand seventy-eight to one in number. That of the *Moon* relative to the *Earth* is in size as one relative to forty-seven. Consequently, the proportion of the *Moon* in size relative to the *Sun* is as one relative to sixty-four million three hundred forty-six thousand six hundred seventy-six in number. Notwithstanding this, this minor part—indeed, a single speck in comparison to the *Sun*—is placed on equal footing with that almost inexpressibly large *Sea of Fire*. Although the *Moonlight* is so much less and fainter than the *Sun*, it nevertheless deserves to carry the name of a Great Light. Just as the *Sun* is great in terms of the service and use that Mankind derives from it, so likewise the *Moon*, being of equal utility as the other, the *Sun*, is also great in consideration of her *Light*, great...

# PRINT PLATE XII.

He must be very inattentive, distracted of thought, indeed almost deprived of his senses, who does not notice and understand that the well-ordered and sequential manner of Creation wonderfully corresponds with the very nature of the creatures themselves, and that everything is arranged according to the Nature of things by Divine providence. First, the Atmosphere had to be purified, cleared, and put in order. After that, the Earth required warming, just as it was in turn warmed and made fertile by the sunlight. This being performed and accomplished through GOD’S Goodness, immediately all kinds of Earthly growths, Herbs, Grass, and Trees raised their elegant and green heads from the ground, and covered their Fertile Mother, the Earth, with a newborn and natural garment. Today is the birthday of all Animals <note>The author uses "Animals" here to specifically refer to the creatures of the water and air created on the fifth day</note>, who arrive quite fittingly, or, as is commonly said, just in time, being the very first to tread the globe, while the Birds fly through the Air: I say, "just in time," because upon their emergence they already find the necessary supply for the maintenance of their lives abundantly provided and prepared beforehand by the all-provident Creator, so that from now on they have, as the saying goes, a "worry-free meal"; since the already full-grown Herbs and other Greenery serve them as food, and daily provide sufficiently fresh nourishment.

First of all, the Waters brought forth *a swarming of living Souls*, that is, all kinds of *creeping Animals*, or as they are called, *small creatures* <term>original: *Ongedierten* - in this 18th-century context, this refers to insects and small invertebrates rather than "pests"</term>: yet not such that Nature alone, by itself—that is, through its own power and operation—bred these creatures, or formed them from mud and slime, but by the powerful command and will of the Almighty Creator alone were they brought into the world. GOD spoke, and as soon as it was said, He brought it forth through His WORD, having impregnated the Waters with certain seeds or tiny eggs, not to say that He brought the eggs themselves, however small and insignificant

<column-break/>

they may be, into being in all their perfection. Such will never be doubted if one is willing to take up and consult with attention for instruction the modern *Philosophy* <term>Natural Philosophy - what we would today call the natural sciences</term>, which leads Man to GOD. One need only maturely consider within oneself the infinite variety, the wonderful changes, the most provident preservation, and the incomparable constitution of all things, to be convinced that each and every creature, both small and large, are the most skillful and entirely inscrutable masterpieces of GOD’S own hand. Just pay attention to even the very smallest Animals, among which one finds those of which up to Thirty Thousand in number live in a single drop of water; notice now their Intestines, Veins, Nerves, Muscles, Joints, Vital Spirits—in a word, everything that one can call the design, movement, and well-orderedness of a Body. See with what dexterity these little creatures know how to lay and hide their eggs in such places as mostly Leaves, Flowers, Fruits, Plants, Trees, and Walls, where they, having become ripe or having fully emerged, can find their food. Trace with your thoughts how sticky and excellent that kind of glue must be, with which they so artfully attach their eggs, so that they can remain in safety against all the turbulence of the Air, such as Wind, Rain, Storms, Cold, and Heat. Observe how cleverly some know how to wrap their eggs in rolled-up leaves; while others lay them with singular ingenuity in the thin twigs of Trees, which they have first pierced with their stingers, or at least wounded, damaged, or bitten through. See with what caution some tie their physical gains, or eggs, between the wrinkled bark of Trees, or often to the bark itself, as if with silk and almost inseparable threads, here and there, or, that which seems somewhat strange, and yet—

vermin and insects, it has been found good and useful to add here some species of similar creatures, which Plate XII depicts, such as *butterflies* <note>original: "Pepels" or "Zomervogeltjes," literally 'summer birds'</note>, commonly called *Whites* here in this country, and named *Capelles* <note>A regional Dutch term for butterflies or moths.</note> by enthusiasts; *caterpillars* or *grass-worms*; *ground beetles* <note>original: "Schallebyters"</note> or *horse-worms*; *one-* and *two-horned beetles*, of which one is called *Rhinoceros* and the other *Stag Beetle* <note>original: "Vliegend Hart," literally 'Flying Heart'</note> in this country; *beetles*, green and venomous *tree-worms*, otherwise called *Spanish Flies* <note>A type of blister beetle used historically in medicine.</note>; *grasshoppers*, *spiders*, and more of the like, called *dragonflies* <note>original German: "Augenschieffer"</note> and *locusts* <note>original German: "Heuschrecken"</note> by the High Germans. When one views the mentioned Plate, one must at the same time pay attention to the supplementary prints or ornaments that stand beside it, which decorate the Plate in no small way, as these depictions certainly deserve no less attention and description, since they show the wondrous transformations of the insects, and are useful in this place to take one as an example—namely those of the *ant* and the *butterfly*.

NATURAL HISTORY.

## ILLUSTRATION PLATE XIII.

> The thriving FEATHERED FLOCK,
> That above the Earth doth soar,
> Sings of the Creator’s Glories:
> Their pleasant Voice
> Calls Heavenward to Him
> The Earth-dwellers from below.

The dignified spectacle of this world increases daily more and more in glory. Lift your eyes Heavenward, you Earthlings—who can barely lift the heavy burden of your body a foot high from the ground of the Earth by your own strength, and whose noble and free soul sits imprisoned here below; look upward, I say, and praise God's Greatness. Observe how the newborn feathered creatures—so artistic <note>The author uses "Konst-" (artistic/skillful) to imply the intricate design of nature.</note> and numerous in variety of nature, size, and all kinds of colors—adorn the upper chambers of the sky through their free and joyful flight, through the pleasant and swift movement of their elegant wings, and through the lovely and soul-stirring sound of their throats, and seem to invite the humble Earth-dwellers to Heaven through their song. Fly after them, at least with your thoughts, and sing with the luxuriant birds the hymns of your Creator. It is true that here the lesser has been placed before the greater—that is, the base insects <term>Ongedierten: historically referring to small creeping things or insects rather than "pests"</term> before the thriving birds—although each is remarkable and excellent in its kind; yet for that reason, it was judged fair to let those creatures of the air occupy a unique place, and to treat the birds here in particular. Furthermore, this is all the more necessary because their variety is so great and extensive that one could barely contain and describe them in their entirety and as the matter requires, even in a whole book, such as that by the famous English Knight *Willoughby* <note>Referring to Sir Francis Willughby (1635–1672), a pioneer of ornithology.</note>, who excellently handled this subject in his Latin work called *Ornithologia* <note>original: "Ornithologia" — English: Ornithology (The study of birds).</note>. For this reason, we shall be satisfied to present here one or at least a few more of each kind of bird to avoid long-windedness. Let it be enough to display here the *Eagle*, King of the Earthly and hook-taloned birds, marked A., alongside the *Parrot* B. as an example. Among those that have straight and less-curved beaks and claws are the *Raven* C. and the *Hoopoe* D. Among the Earthly birds, the *Ostrich* E. is the largest. Among those with short and straighter beaks, the *Hen* F. with her *Rooster* G. are surely the most prominent.

### ILLUSTRATION PLATE XV.

> *And GOD Created great Whales: and every living, swarming soul, which the Waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind; and every winged Fowl after his kind: and GOD saw that it was good.* Genesis 1, verse 21.

It is noteworthy that Holy Scripture says, *GOD Created...* so that Man might clearly grasp that he owes the creation of the Fish and other Sea creatures to GOD alone, the Creator of All. From this it also appears that the Waters had no sufficient power of their own to be able to bring forth such large and fearsome bodies as *Whales* and many other Sea and River monsters; thus, the Sea has given nothing more to those Water-creatures than itself as a dwelling place for their preservation—which is itself GOD’S own Handiwork and Structure. If anyone should not be sufficiently convinced of this truth, he has only to consider, on the one hand, the impotence and simplicity of Water, and on the other, the rare and distinct creation and form of the Fish. He should first observe the various and unusual placements of their Teeth, which almost all of them have in the mouth, in one or more rows; others in the throat, and also some in their stomach. Furthermore, let him observe their Eyes and Fins, with which they know how to move themselves as if with oars, turning back and forth, and with an unbe-

<column-break/>

lievable speed swimming away. Let him pay heed to their Tail, which they use in the manner of a rudder: to their Scales, their small and few Brains in relation to their whole body; their Sensation, which is so fine and so closely attuned that it seems to serve them as Hearing as well; their Ears, if one may speak so, which serve them in place of Lungs; their Stomach and manifold intestines: their swim- or Air-bladder, by which they move themselves upward and downward, and keep themselves everywhere in a certain equilibrium with the Water. How wonderful and numerous are their Muscles; how manifold is their Procreation; how rare is their distinction into all kinds of Species and Genera?

For the same reasons, one could place all creeping Creatures—whether they have blood, like the Snakes, or on the contrary, like the Worms and all other such vermin <term>Ongedierte: historically referring to small creeping things or insects rather than "pests"</term>, are bloodless—among the aforementioned wonders of GOD’S Wisdom and Omnipotence. Here, by *Living Swarming, that is, moving souls*, must especially be understood all *Bloodless Creatures* <note>In historical biology, "bloodless" (exanguia) referred to invertebrates or animals without red blood.</note>, thus specifically named; first of all the Sea-creatures, both the soft ones, namely the...

# N A T U R A L H I S T O R Y

...the Cephalopods <note>Original: "Veelvoetigen," literally "many-footed ones."</note> and other fish that have black blood; such as the hard or crustaceous ones, that is, those covered with shells, among which the sea-crab, sea-urchin, and the so-called starfish; as well as the shellfish, like mussels, all kinds of water-snails, and all other sea-spawn of that nature that live in shells, may be counted.

Just as GOD has always shown Himself the greatest even in the very smallest and most insignificant creatures, so has He likewise let His boundless Power and Greatness appear in the very largest Animals. Among these, the Sacred Writer *Moses* names the *Great Whales* as kings among all Swimming Water-creatures, with a certain mark of excellence. By this, without doubt, all kinds of large Sea-fish of whatever nature or sort they might be are to be understood—those who, in the manner of Four-footed Fruit-bearing <note>meaning mammals</note> Animals, draw their breath through lung-pipes, physically mate, conceive, bear living young, and raise them with milk or suckle them at their breasts. Among this sort of *great fish*, the so-called sea-monsters or *water-beasts* may be counted, as these are also among the very largest. From the aforementioned Sea-fish or Whales, as well as the latter, those that are *Cartilaginous* <note>Original: "Knarsbeenig," literally "crunch-boned," referring to fish with skeletons made of cartilage rather than bone.</note> must be especially distinguished—that is to say, those that are neither flesh nor bone—and also the *Prickly* ones, or those that are set and armed with thorns. To the first-mentioned sort of great Sea-fish or Whales belong the *Dolphin*, the *Sea-Ox* or *Sea-Calf* (called *Phocena* <note>original: "Phocena," referring to the harbor porpoise</note> in Latin), the *Whale*, the so-called *Leviathan*, and more other Sea-monsters known to the Latins by the names *Physeter* <note>original: "Physeter," the sperm whale</note> and *Clus*.

Much has been written about *Whales*, though most of it is fictional and unbelievable; in this style of writing, the Hebrews are by far the masters. They testify to the extraordinary size of said Sea-creatures, which seems all the more fictional and unbelievable when they dare to bring forth some of that kind of animal which they say were five hundred Stadia long—that is, according to the determination of modern road-measurements, more than sixty of our Miles <note>In the 17th/18th century, a Dutch mile was roughly 5 kilometers, making this claim over 300 kilometers long.</note>: certainly a great, but rightly suspicious length. Whatever the truth of this may be, it cannot compare in length to that terrifying and uncommonly large Sea-monster in *Bava Batra folio 73* <note>A reference to a tractate in the Babylonian Talmud known for its tall tales and allegories.</note>, upon whose back a well-sailed

<column-break/>

Ship took three full days to sail from one fin to the other. What does the reader think of such a "little stickleback"? Away with such fish; make room for much larger ones! Such shall be brought before us by the Arabs, who understand the art of forging fables far better than all other writers. Stand back, for here they come dragging in a little fish that, according to their testimony, is so large that the entire globe of the Earth can very easily rest and lie firm upon the back of that fish alone—in the manner of certain large drinking cups whose bowl rests and stands firm on the tails or backs of Whales, Dolphins, or Sea-creatures. Goldsmiths often use such decorations as a support or pedestal for such drinking bowls, as is still common today. In my opinion, it would be somewhat safer to stick to more definite measurements and lengths, as modern observations present to us, since such a sort of Sea-fish in our times very rarely reaches a length of more than one hundred feet.

The aforementioned Illustrious Knight *Willoughby* <note>Sir Francis Willughby (1635–1672), a pioneering English naturalist.</note>, an Englishman by birth, has published an extensive work on *Fish*. Thus, we shall be content to cite one or a few of each sort as examples in this print. The beginning is as follows, namely:

N. 1. Of the Long Fish that are neither flesh nor bone <note>i.e., cartilaginous fish</note>, the *Shark* is the first, called *Carcharias* <note>original: "Charcharias," usually referring to the Great White Shark</note> in Latin, and the *Sea-dog* by the High Germans.

N. 8. Of the short, rounded fish that have no fibrous or flexible fins, the *Pufferfish*, in Latin *Orbis Muricatus* <note>original: "Orbis Muricatus," meaning "prickly sphere," a porcupinefish or pufferfish</note>, called the *Sea-dove* in High German.

N. 10. The *Seahorse*.

N. 11. Of those that have three fins on the back, the *Cod*.

N. 12. Of the Sea-fish that have two fins...

## PLATE XVII.

> If GOD'S Wisdom is worthy of praise even in the SMALL,
> It belongs to the LARGE with even greater right.
> Praise Him, who gives us the SMALL SEA FISH for food:
> While the LARGE WHALE is provided for our use.

Because of the limited experience one has with that uncommon class of Great Sea-fish, it is not possible to dissect them perfectly according to the requirements of all their specific properties. It seems neither safer nor more advisable, in order to speak of them with any certainty, than to bring forth such matters as are capable of convincing everyone of the absolute truth. Therefore, one shall present here several parts that are still found today and serve as public and irrefutable evidence, depicted in their natural size and shape as a complete proof for the eyes, starting with:

A. The Eye of a **Whale**, which is little larger than an orange, according to the observations of **Ruysch** <note>original: "Ruysch. Thes. Anat. IV. Tab. I." Frederik Ruysch (1638–1731) was a famous Dutch botanist and anatomist known for his developments in anatomical preservation.</note>

B. Its so-called **Crystalline Humor** <note>The lens of the eye.</note>, which, in proportion to the coarse size of its body, is very small, being little larger than that of a Calf’s Eye.

C. The **Teat**, whose milk ducts can be seen with the naked eye.

D. A **Tooth** of the aforementioned Sea-fish **Orca**, otherwise called **Leviathan** <note>original: "Leviathan". A biblical term often used historically to describe any massive sea creature.</note>, depicted from life, which the writer of this work received as a gift from the famous Mr. **Hazaeus**, and still holds in high value in his memory.

E. A transverse cross-section of the Male member <note>The penis.</note> of an immature Whale, which rests in the Writer’s own Cabinet of Curiosities; where at **a** one sees the opening of the urethra <note>original: "Waterloozinge", literally "water-discharge".</note>. **b. c.** Depicts its external nervous and spongy structure, being naturally yellow-colored and transparent like Amber. **c. d.** Its internal nervous and spongy nature, being in character and form like that of man himself and also of the four-footed Animals. **e. e.** Thin skins or membranes, with which the passage of the urethra is here and there joined and attached to the external spongy body, serving for the further expansion or retraction of the said urethra.

# SPIRITUAL ILLUSTRATION XIX. XX.

### ILLUSTRATION XIX. XX.

->*Here Nature flaunts her finest, by God’s all-wise power,*<-
->*In Shell and Horn, with their hue, and luster, and clarity;*<-
->*Whatever is strange or beautiful, is here brought together:*<-
->*The Sea provides a Cabinet of Art of every rarity.*<-

***

Among the countless multitude of remarkable and priceless treasures, which ever-active Nature—through the inexhaustible goodness of the most skillful Creator—reaches out with generous hands to the Art-loving Man in daily abundance; among so many uncommon and precious Gifts, wherewith we poor Mortals are favored and enriched by her unceasing fertility; among so many unsearchable Wonders and manifest Signs, through which the great GOD allows His glory to excel at all times, surely the least are not those beautifully colored and mobile Houses, those charmingly compact and glossy hiding places, those most artistic and translucent Chambers, among which some seem to deserve the name of Golden and Silver Palaces not improperly. I mean those rare *Sea-horns* and *Shells*, in which the *Creeping* and *Swarming Water-creatures*, such as *Snails* and *Mussels*, have their dwelling and resting places. It is not without reason that many a Lover of Art <note>The Dutch term "Liefhebber" refers to a connoisseur or amateur collector of natural curiosities.</note> holds them in such high esteem; while by others they have been valued so greatly that they have not hesitated to devote much effort and labor to publishing accurate Books about them, and to depict them from life in fine Print-plates. Rightly are expensive Cabinets of them collected, since they are not only a very pleasant object of attention and contemplation for the eye, but can even serve for a sweet and moral delight of our Spirit. This obliges us to make at least a brief mention of them here, even though they deserve a much more extensive and accurate description; however, to save space and time, since they are so numerous in multitude and variety, we shall present to the Reader's satisfaction no more than one or a few of each kind.

Among the twisted *Sea-horns*, otherwise called *Snail-houses*, which are glossy and shining like Mother-of-pearl on the inside, the following are counted, as they are named and known by contemporary Collectors here in this land.

<column-break/>

A. The *Nautilus* or *Shell-fish*, called the *Schiff-kuttel* <note>original: "Schiff-kuttel". German for "ship-tripe," an old name for the Nautilus.</note> by the Germans.
B. The so-called *Ammon's Horn*, called the *Post-horn* by the Collectors.

### PLATE XXI. XXII.

*And GOD said: Let the Earth bring forth living souls, after their kind: Cattle, and creeping things, and wild Beasts of the Earth after their kind: and it was so. And GOD made the wild Beasts of the Earth after their kind, and the Cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground after its kind: and GOD saw that it was good.* **Gen. I. v. 24, 25.**

> The UNREASONING BEASTS, created for Man’s service, <note>The author uses "redeloos" (without reason) to distinguish animals from humans, who possess a rational soul.</note>
> Have something from which the Spirit can gather a moral lesson:
> Their moderation rebukes the Drunkard and the Glutton,
> Who daily exceeds himself in food and drink.

Although the *Birds*, *Fish*, and *Insects* <note>original: "Ongedierten." While often meaning vermin, in this 18th-century context it frequently referred to small crawling creatures or insects.</note>—due to their nature, constitution, and other physical qualities—correspond more closely to human nature than *Plants* do; nevertheless, such a correspondence of the aforementioned creatures of Air and Water is by no means to be compared to the similarity and certain harmony of nature that exists between Man and all kinds of *four-footed* and *creeping animals*, especially those of the *Serpent-Kind*. For this reason, we shall present their external and internal bodily form here by way of a concise anatomy, until finally, after a careful observation of the unreasoning Animals, we approach with our thoughts and physical contemplations the most noble and prominent of all earthly creatures: I mean *Man*.

The present object of our observation immediately provides us with irrefutable evidence by which even the most insensitive and stubborn Freethinkers <note>original: "Vrygeesten." This term refers to skeptics or atheists who challenged religious orthodoxy during the Enlightenment.</note> could be sufficiently convinced of the absolute truth: that there is necessarily a GOD, a Supreme Being and Creator of All, who not only created *Man* (of which we are all fully convinced within ourselves), but also each and every creature found in the entire created order of Nature,

<column-break/>

brought forth by His free and independent Almightiness. This is all the more certain because we are aware that no mortal on Earth has ever had such power or knowledge that he could, solely by himself—that is, by his own strength and action, without any external and cooperative aids—summon anything out of Nothing; far from having originally brought himself forth, or (what would be far less significant than the other) being able to keep his life, which he has received from GOD alone, eternally within the body. Who is so arrogant and frantic that he would dare to doubt the existence of GOD by placing weak and powerless Nature before the effective and all-governing power of the Creator? Who, I say, has strayed so far from rationality that he would dare to attribute the dependent and limited workings of creatures, which must be ascribed to GOD alone, to *Nature*, when one attentively considers the rare form, character, and constant life-movements of not only the so-called *Domestic Animals*, but also the *Wild Beasts*? Assuredly, the permanence of this truth is shown to us patently by the wonderful constitution of those organ-like <note>original: "Orgelwyzige." Refers to the complex, mechanical-like arrangement of biological systems, similar to the pipes and bellows of an organ.</note> instruments moved by Air- or Vital-spirits, <note>original: "Leven-geesten." In historical medicine, these were believed to be subtle fluids or vapors that animated the body.</note> as all *four-footed Animals* [are]...

...beasts are, without also wishing to compare those of Man—though he is nearly equal to them in almost all parts, *Reason* alone excepted—with theirs. This is evident first from the most skillful creation and almost untraceable flow of their blood; from the ever-moving air- or valve-membranes of their lungs, which serve them for breathing and especially for the thinning of the blood; <note>In 18th-century physiology, it was believed the lungs "thinned" or "rarefied" the blood to prepare it for circulation.</note> from the steady circulation of the vital fluids; from the internal movement of their bodies; and above all from that wonderful fineness of countless thin and fibrous veins, of which a multitude of *seven hundred and ninety-two thousand* combined hardly makes up the thickness of a thumb. What else is there but GOD’S Omnipotence to be read in the inimitable masterpiece of their Heart and most powerful Fire- and Water-engine, <note>The author uses "Vuur- en Waterſpuyte" (Fire- and Water-engines), a common metaphor of the time comparing the heart's pumping action to the newly invented mechanical pumps used in firefighting.</note> in their Arteries, in their so-called second Heart, <note>This likely refers to the liver or perhaps a specific anatomical understanding of the heart's chambers as separate entities.</note> in their further Blood-vessels and Water-vessels with their respective Valves? Furthermore, as a certain proof of GOD’S Essence, serves that wonderful carving, rumination, swallowing, and digestion of the consumed food; the changing of the same into milky nutritious juices; the progression or transformation of these juices into Blood; the separation of the Blood from various other parts that are not of the same nature. Also especially the insensible and invisible passage or evaporation of bodily vapors through their skin; the gathering and steady formation of seed in their testicles; the singular operation (if such be found among the Animals) of their vital spirits in the Head. Add to this the operations of their external senses, namely those skillful instruments of Sight, Hearing, Taste, Smell, and Feeling, without overlooking the internal senses common to all living creatures, such as Imagination, Memory, the Motion or the contraction and extension of muscles and nerves, through which all bodily movements occur; Sleep and Wakefulness, and finally their manifold reproduction; the steady maintenance both of each species in particular and of all the genera of Beasts in general. Moreover, that wonderful diversity that is still perceived in the particular species and genera, both in nature and other properties, besides more other precise observations that one could cite here regarding the Animals, but which are passed over for the sake of brevity.

To the *four-footed Animals* should be added in this place all kinds of *creeping Creatures*, namely all that are rich in blood, especially the *Serpent-Kind*, which, like all four-footed Beasts, breathes through the Lungs, yet is footless.

### PRINT PLATE XXIII.

> *And GOD said: Let us make Man, after our image, after our likeness; and let them have Dominion over the Fish of the Sea, and over the Fowl of the Heavens, and over the Cattle, and over the whole Earth, and over all creeping Things that creep upon the Earth.*
> *And GOD created Man after his image, after the image of GOD created he him: Male and Female created he them. Gen. I. v. 26, 27.*

->*The World is fully built: The Human race*<-
->*Is brought into the light last, as the Noblest,*<-
->*So that everything might be at his service in this life:*<-
->*Therefore it suits his intellect to always give the honor to GOD.*<-

Today there appears upon the completed Stage of the World the Noblest of all Creatures, GOD’S own Image and His viceroy on Earth: namely, MAN. Truly a sublime and magnificent Condition, an invaluable and nearly incomparable quality for a creature, which is to be esteemed all the higher, and held in all the greater value, as it comes closer to the DIVINITY. Thus the Greeks, not without reason, called Man a *little world* <note>original: "kleine Weereld" or Microcosm</note>, because Nature itself sufficiently teaches that he is a brief summary of all created things; that is to say, that he concisely encompasses within himself, in his small and delicate body, all the workings and qualities of the Universe.

Here again, a convincing sign of GOD’S Providence and Loving-kindness reveals itself, who created Man at such a perfect time that he found all necessary provisions for his maintenance prepared and ready, so that one might say the well-set table of the Earth seemed to wait for nothing more than the arrival and seating of the newly-created Guest.

First, the Sun had to il-

<column-break/>

luminate the Earth; the Stars had to adorn the Firmament of Heaven; the Atmosphere <note>original: "Dampkring"</note> had to be purified and made fit for the growth of Earthly plants and for the breathing of all Animals: the Waters had to be divided and separated from one another, so that the Upper waters could serve as clouds, and the Lower as the dwelling place of the Fish and the refreshment of the Earth: the Moist had to be separated from the Dry—that is, the Water from the Earth—and each placed separately. The Earth had first to be clothed with fruit-bearing Trees, with green Shrubs, with golden Grass, fragrant Herbs, and other elegant plants, and moreover be adorned and provided with all kinds of Flowers and Fruits. First the cheerful Birds, then the abundant Cattle; in a word, all irrational Animals had to be created before Man, who would finally crown the magnificent Work of the six-day creation, came forth. Such was required by GOD’S arrangement, as he was to be set as Chief and Ruler, next to GOD, over *all the works of his hands: everything had to be put under his feet, Sheep and Oxen, all of them:* Also

# SPIRITUAL

...also the Beasts of the Field, the Fowl of the Heavens, and the Fish of the Sea, whatever passes through the paths of the Seas. Psalm VIII. 7. 8. 9.

It is well to imagine that the newly created Man, in his first glance and upon that sudden and unexpected sight of the elegant and well-ordered state of the World, was for some time enraptured in spirit. Being gifted with the purest understanding and accompanied by a most free will, he must have immediately, from the depths of his heart, praised and thanked his most benevolent GOD and Creator with a full voice for the singular grace by which it had pleased Him to bring Man forth. I seem to hear him cry out: *When I behold your Heavens, the work of your Fingers, the Moon and the Stars, which you have prepared. What is Man, that you are mindful of him: and the son of Man, that you visit him, and have made him a little lower than the Angels, and have crowned him with honor and glory? You make him rule over the Works of your hands; you have put all things under his feet. O Lord, our Lord, how glorious is your Name in all the Earth!*

If one wishes to observe the accompanying Print Plate <note>Referring to an illustration in the original volume</note> with attention, one will undoubtedly find in the external physical posture of the newly created Man, as he is depicted there, that he appears as if exalted and enraptured by wonder at the sudden sight of so many strange and miraculous objects that appear before him at first glance; which is why one could introduce him here, reasoning with himself thus:

> *Who am I? Where, by whom? How long have I been?*
> *I am here now: I think and work with the spirit.*
> *I see the green Trees; I hear the Birds singing;*
> *I smell the fragrant herb: I see two great Circles* <note>The sun and the moon</note>
> *Of Fire and Light: I feel a pleasant breeze,*
> *And taste with delight the sweetness of this ripe fruit.*
> *Wherever I turn or twist, I find only Earth-dwellers,* <note>The animals</note>
> *Who watch and surround me in silence,*
> *And are different from me. What now? What is to be done here?*
> *Where do I want to go, where shall I go, what shall I start first?*
> *I feel, and wish, and sigh, and know not how to begin,*

<column-break/>

> *And yet I feel something, something that teaches me to love;*
> *To love! Yes: but whom? Where do I seek him? Where shall*
> *I [find] the object of my love.... o Creator of the Universe,*
> *Adorable God, whose incomprehensible being*
> *In me, and all that lives, is sufficient to be read,* <note>Seen or understood through nature</note>
> *You alone are the one I recognize as Supreme Lord;*
> *You are He by whose grace I am a fleshly creature.*
> *You are He whom I alone must fear and love:*
> *It is enough for me to win your favor through my conduct;*
> *Teach me how I best show You my duty and homage,*
> *So that I may live in this world according to your will.*
> *I owe You thanks for my origin, and wish all my life,*
> *To give signs of awe and submission:*
> *I swear to You an oath of Faithfulness and Subservience,*
> *As a dependent of the Supreme Majesty.*

Here, as with all the particular Works of the general Creation, nothing else was needed for the bringing forth of Man but the single and ordinary Word which the Creator, as a complete proof of His Omnipotence, had used in everything until this day: namely, FIAT <note>Latin: "Let it be done"</note>, that is, the *Let it be*, or the *Be it so*. Although one might say that a sort of secret Consultation of the Most Holy Trinity was convened for that purpose, so that this singular creation—which is sufficiently distinct from all other creatures—should cause us to constantly remember the loftiness and nobility of our Nature, and at the same time the frailty and weakness of the same in respect to GOD'S most exalted and adorable Being. This was done by keeping before our eyes the high dignity of the absolute Supreme Dominion which has been granted to us over all other Earthly Creatures through an excellent mark of Divine grace. This glorification, far from carrying Man away into pride or vanity, should instead serve more and more as an encouragement and constant reminder to fulfill his bounden duty all the more diligently, regarding the homage and submissive acknowledgment that he must show to GOD for such singular benefits through a most humble submission of himself and a most reverent adoration of his Creator. It is also noteworthy that the Patriarchs <note>Early church fathers or biblical ancestors</note> derived from that singular expression, *Let us make Man*, a certain foresight or sign of those high and hidden Mysteries of the most exalted and incomprehensible—

...the Holy Trinity must have had, so that this aforementioned way of speaking or expression does not actually seem to have been a preceding deliberation or consultation; but rather an *effective intention* or *firm purpose* of GOD’S Will, who from all eternity had resolved within Himself to create Man at the beginning of time. See *Heidegger, History of the Patriarchs, Exercise IV, Thesis 8.* <note>Referencing Johann Heinrich Heidegger (1633–1698), a Swiss Reformed theologian.</note>

No one should doubt that Man, among all other creatures of this world, was by far the most noble and worthy, although he has made himself most miserable through sin, because he was created and formed by GOD Himself after His image, without having come forth through other men, as happens today with his descendants; whereby he seems to have deserved the glorious name of *Son of GOD*, which is attributed to him in *Luke 3:38*, in the sense mentioned above. This is also confirmed in the Acts of the Apostles 17:28 by these words: *For we are also His offspring*, <note>Original: "Want wy zyn ook zyn Geslachte"</note> that is, descending from GOD through Creation: which expression or way of speaking the Teacher of the Nations <note>A traditional title for the Apostle Paul</note> borrowed from *Aratus*, an ancient Greek writer who wrote about the course of the Heavens, as a sign that even the natural light—which Reason instills in us—sufficiently indicates the exalted origin and high descent of Man. The ancient saying of the Heathens, *Beginning with Jove*, <note>Original Latin: "a Jove principium"</note> meaning *all beginning from Jupiter*, seems to intend the same meaning.

It is true that, when one observes this glorious Image of GOD distinctly, one must marvel to the highest degree at the singular dignity and exalted created nature of Man: but on the contrary, one stands ashamed at his present fallen and unhappy state, into which the sinful creature, through the transgression of the Divine Command, has brought himself. One sees how far Man has strayed through sin from that special communion which he previously had with GOD in the state of his original innocence. What shall one say of his most exalted origin and—so to speak—almost Divine descent, of which he has made himself unworthy, and which he has completely dishonored and stained through a shameful apostasy? Let us look further into the matter.

Although one must admit that our Soul is a rich treasury of all kinds of ideas, which in both multitude and variety of nature may be called infinite, yet there is between the spiritual workings of the uncreated and the

<column-break/>

created Being—that is, between the thoughts of GOD and those of the Human Soul—this distinction: that GOD thinks in a most perfect, free, completely independent, and unlimited way; and that, on the contrary, the Soul of Man is very limited and imperfect in its Thoughts! Moreover, these thoughts are mostly confused, interrupted, hesitating, and enclosed within very narrow bounds; they are also of almost no, or at least very short, durability.

Furthermore, our Soul is immortal, yet not in the sense that it had no beginning, but because once it has been brought into being by GOD, it will never have an end, or be able to be destroyed. This immortality depends solely on the most free and effective will of the Creator, with whom, as *Paul* well notes in his first Epistle to *Timothy 6:16*, only immortality is to be found. *Man*, says *Augustine in Book VI on Genesis, Chapter 25*, <note>Original: "L. VI. de Gen. C. 25."</note> *is mortal because of the external shape of his body, which in many parts corresponds with that of the irrational Animals; but his soul is immortal through the singular favor of the Creator.* It was GOD’S good pleasure that the soul, although it could die <note>i.e., it is not inherently eternal by its own nature</note>, should nevertheless never die.

> Do not care then for the body, which is mortal;
> but do
> Your best for the noble soul, which must live eternally.

The soul of man thinks and works Freely, yet by far not with such perfect Freedom and activity as GOD, because we often find within ourselves that our Freedom of thought differs little or almost not at all from slavery. This appears clearly from our internal spiritual movements; for how often does it not happen that one almost does not know where to turn or go, or how or what is best to undertake? How often does one not stand in doubt before one dares to intend or establish anything certain? How long does one sometimes linger and deliberate when one is to choose or put into effect something of importance? How often are we not tossed back and forth by our own passions and—like a motionless ship on the open sea without sails or oars—flung here and there by the ravishing waves of external objects? Moreover, there are, in my opinion, not such great and weighty reasons that one should insist strongly on the Freedom and unhampered nature of our Will...

can boast, since none of us is powerful enough to move even a single hair of his head by his own means, much less to shift or bring into motion the smallest speck outside of his body. One might almost say that our will appears limited, and in some sense powerless and incapable, because even all the particular movements of our mind depend not so much upon ourselves as upon GOD, as the primary cause; yet not so much that one would wish to entirely suppress or take away free will. The rest is left to the Theologians. <note>The author likely refers to the complex debates regarding predestination and free will that were central to Dutch Reformed theology in the 17th and 18th centuries.</note> Furthermore, the mastery and power that all Men have over themselves—that is, over their passions and many other bodily movements and carnal impulses—is so narrowly constrained, so weak and fickle (not to call it alternating, inconstant, and changeable), that all the thoughts and workings of our soul must give way to one another, so that each may have the upper hand in its turn. Thus, one may rightly say that the crown of this Mastery is often snatched from our heads, even against our will, and the staff of authority, with which the Spirit must restrain the Body, is taken out of our hand.

->*Now the SOUL, then the BODY holds the highest command:*<-
->*If the Spirit turns to virtue, the Body follows him not:*<-

Among the remarkable characteristics of the Divine Image—namely, Man—the general supremacy granted to him by GOD over all earthly creatures is perhaps the most prominent. It pleased the Creator, who had placed the newly created Man in such a glorious and blessed state, to glorify him even further; therefore He said, after He had blessed him: *Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the Earth, and have dominion over the Fish of the Sea, and over the birds of the Heaven, and over every animal that creeps upon the Earth.* With this in view, GOD brought all the animals of the field and all the birds of the Heaven that He had made to Adam, to see what he would call them: and whatever Adam would call every living soul, that would be its name. What did this signify other than a sort of Homage, which the Creator desired should be shown to Adam through this act. It also seems to have been for the same reason—that is, by virtue of this Dominion—that two of every earthly Animal came to Noah

<column-break/>

in *Genesis 7:14*, to remain preserved in the Ark with him and under his protection. It is true that it follows from this that it was GOD’S will and pleasure that Man should Rule over all the Animals of the Earth: but how imperfect, how powerless, how minor and "fief-bound" <note>The term "leenroerig" refers to a feudal relationship where power is held only by the grace of a higher lord.</note> is this Dominion compared to the Divine one, which, on the contrary, is absolute, steadfast, unhindered, and can never be interrupted or stopped; GOD’S Supremacy over all the creatures of the whole of Nature being everywhere fully and uniquely powerful and universal. What is more; the privilege that Man seems to have over the Animals is, in my opinion, of such a nature that it might much sooner be called a *Use* or *Enjoyment* than a true *Dominion*. Man had to know the nature and natural properties of the Animals, so as to praise and thank GOD the Creator of All the more zealously, and to use those irrational creatures all the better for his service, and most especially for food. This is evident from the Charter or Commission which GOD granted to *Noah* after the general *Deluge* in *Genesis 9:2, 3, 4*: *The fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every Animal of the Earth, and upon every Bird of the Heaven, and all that moves on the ground, and in all the Fishes of the Sea: they are delivered into your hands. Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; I have given it all to you, even as the green herb.*

Another characteristic of our soul is *Simplicity*, <note>In 18th-century philosophy, "simplicity" (eenvoudigheid) refers to the soul being a single, indivisible substance, unlike the body which is made of parts.</note> but of such a nature that it can or may hardly be compared in any part to that of the Divine Being; because GOD’S thoughts are infinite, unlimited, perfect, and present everywhere at one and the same time; whereas ours, on the contrary, are divided and confused; one excludes the other, and all are followed and relieved by each other in turns.

*Understanding* and the *wise* conduct of all our actions is likewise one of the special marks of our Soul: but how minor, how weak and powerless is that as well—not to say entirely incomparable—given the present state of our corruption and blindness? GOD knows and understands everything in a most perfect manner; Man, far from knowing and understanding everything, possesses hardly anything more than an imperfect and hindered knowledge of that which he does know, which knowledge is, moreover, very limited and imperfect. Furthermore, a great curiosity—an absolute sign of our ignorance and lack of knowledge—to know much, is innate to us.

# NATURAL PHILOSOPHY

# M

<meta>catchword: world-</meta>

The greatest part of all that we know is certainly the smallest part of what remains unknown to us. Moreover, what great effort, care, labor, and attention must one not apply—indeed, even spending all our understanding and all the powers of our soul in the sweat of our brow—just to obtain some small amount of knowledge or science? Of this truth, *Paul*, the Teacher of the Gentiles <note>A traditional title for the Apostle Paul, referring to his mission to non-Jewish populations.</note>, seems to have been convinced, as he even openly confesses to having no perfect knowledge of all things, saying: *We know in part, and we prophesy in part.* <note>original: "Wy kennen ten deele, en wy propheteeren ten deele." 1 Corinthians 13:9</note>. This must not be understood, however, to mean that we do not now know all that is necessary for our salvation. But, since a broader discussion of this matter might intrude upon the office of the Theologians, we shall leave it recommended to their care.

Notwithstanding all the reasons mentioned above, something sublime and infinite still seems to shine forth in the Image of GOD. Man knows GOD, that infinite and eternal Being; he knows His infinite and purest perfections and understands all the attributes and qualities of his Creator; yet without perfectly knowing himself, or knowing what is most useful, advantageous, and blessed for him. Although he may perhaps have far more knowledge of other matters, he must nevertheless confess that he is entirely unskilled and ignorant in the knowledge of himself. It is also an absolute truth that when Man wishes to devote himself to a precise contemplation of Divine and supernatural things, he sees as much as one might see in the deepest abyss of clear and transparent water.

The most lamentable thing of all is that, among all the aforementioned particular qualities and workings of the *Soul*—in which Man differs incomparably far from GOD—that noble and artful image has, since his fall, become most estranged and deviated from its very first and original Pattern (namely, its Creator) in *Goodness, Truth, Uprightness, Holiness,* and *Justice*.

Who does not see what sad misfortunes and adversities fallen Man has brought upon himself through sin? Who does not notice what evil and mischief his reckless curiosity has caused him? No sooner had he sinned than he was ruined. Wretched Fall! Unfortunate cause of unspeakable miseries! But how? Is there then no hope or remedy left by which Man might save himself? Des-

<column-break/>

-pair not, O Man; do not lose heart entirely: the way of your restoration is prepared for you through GOD’S Grace. His bottomless Goodness does not allow that noble and high-born soul to remain helplessly stuck in the stinking pool of corruption; sin plunged her into an abyss of wretchedness, but GOD’S mercy does not want her to perish. Therefore, the most gracious GOD offers us abundant means by which the soul—if not entirely, then at least in large part—can restore itself to its former state of Glory. He reaches out His hand to help her. His Divine Word serves her as a brightly shining torch, by whose glorious radiance she may be enlightened in the dark night of her daze. The fiery rays of this Spiritual Torch shall brighten the nearly extinguished sparks of our first understanding from the ashes of our wickedness and help them to glow once more. This same Word teaches us to seek eternal Happiness with GOD and through GOD; it teaches us to be subject to the Divine Will in everything; it makes us practice true virtue and pursue nothing but what is good and glorious. It teaches us to practice Justice, to follow GOD’S laws, to shun evil, and to have a horror of all that is harmful to us. It teaches us to live for and because of GOD, and to aim for the Glory of His Name in everything: it admonishes us to restrain the extravagant passions of the flesh and to spend the short time of our lives with diligence, not for the lust of our senses, but for GOD’S greater honor and our salvation alone. Finally, GOD’S most holy Word teaches us to use worldly goods for our necessity with moderation, and to overcome the difficult obstacles one sometimes meets on the narrow and thorny path of Virtue with patience, until at last, through untiring labor and industry, we reach the desired and perfect restoration of our first Perfection.

Thus, through GOD’S Grace, there remain to us as eternal monuments of our former excellence: Intellect and Will, the impression of Good and Evil, the idea of Right and Wrong, some remnant of Dominion over the Creatures, though also impure, corrupted, and hindered Thoughts, and finally the infallible Fundamental Truths or mathematical and irrefutable Axioms <note>The author refers to "wiiskunstige Hoofdstellingen," meaning self-evident principles or geometric-style proofs that were considered the highest form of certain knowledge in the 17th and 18th centuries.</note>: but this disorder must above all be improved and reformed; the present state of our humiliation must...

...be raised up and restored again. Does anyone wish to know by what means? Through a blameless and holy life: *If indeed you have heard Him, that is, CHRIST, and have been taught by Him, as the Truth is in JESUS: Namely, that you put off, concerning your former conduct, the old man which grows corrupt according to the deceitful lusts: and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and that you put on the new man which was created according to GOD in true righteousness and holiness. Ephes. IV. v. 22. etc.* <note>The author quotes Ephesians 4:22–24 to explain the spiritual "re-creation" of the human soul.</note>

Thus far we have considered GOD’S Image in the Human Soul, insofar as it thinks, understands, wills, judges, and is immortal. Now, in the same manner, we must speak of the Body, which, as well as the Soul, has been graciously favored by the most skillful Creator with exalted and remarkable qualities. Abundant material for this is provided by the extraordinary sublimity of that incomparable masterpiece, formed and executed by the hand of that most wise and eternal Artist—so gloriously entwined and joined with the Soul, so wonderful in all its actions and movements, through which it causes a vivid impression of sensible and external objects in the soul, and even submits itself to the soul's will and pleasure in certain effects. It is certain that these two united principal parts, namely Soul and Body, make up the "New Man" of whom Paul speaks above. In the same sense, we must understand what he says to those of Corinth: *Chap. V. v. 17. Therefore, if anyone is in CHRIST, he is a new creation: old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.* <note>original: "Zo dan indien iemand in CHRISTO is, die is een nieuw schepzel..." 2 Corinthians 5:17.</note> This same truth the great Teacher also intends to convey by what he writes to the Thessalonians, saying: *And may the GOD of Peace Himself sanctify you completely: and may your whole upright Spirit, Soul, and Body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord JESUS CHRIST. C. V. v. 23.*

Finally, our Human Soul is, in its essence as well as in all its other qualities and workings, of an entirely different nature and constitution than the soul of <term>irrational animals</term><note>A common early modern distinction between humans, who possess "reason," and animals, who were thought to possess only "vital spirits" or "sensitive souls."</note>. It is a living soul, the Image of GOD, immaterial and immortal, whereas in contrast, that of the animals is material and mortal. The one thinks and knows what it thinks; the other—if, as some would assert, it might think at all—is at least gifted with no knowledge or ingenuity. The one is Spiritual, the other Corporeal. Holy Scripture, speaking of the soul of animals, says, *the blood is the soul [life]. Deut. XII. 23.* <note>original: "het Bloed is de Ziel." Modern translations usually render this as "the blood is the life."</note> that is: the finest and purest part of their blood. This soul is brought forth from Water and from Earth, *Gen. I. 21. 24.* whereas the Soul of Man has a Heavenly and Divine origin.

If anything might be found anywhere in the entire content of the Bible that seemed somewhat disputable and doubtful, or could appear strange and contradictory to some, it is above all the fixed location of Paradise, which is sought everywhere with all imaginable accuracy and effort. One might almost call its location a battlefield, upon which both Commentators and Geographers wage an everlasting war of books against one another. How many are found among them who have carefully wandered through all of Asia to finally discover that blessed dwelling place of the very first inhabitants of the Earth? But possibly they have all brought back from there no other reward for their labor than a weary body, an empty gold-purse, and an understanding devoid of knowledge. Some of these have even run so far off the tracks that they...
