Others seem to have acted with more caution in this matter, as they, in order to reach their goal more surely, have taken the entire globe as the fixed location of the Earthly Paradise. Some have sought it in *Mesopotamia*; while another party thought it was hidden in *Palestine*. There have also been not a few who said it was situated in the territory of *Babylonia*. One finds those who placed it in *Syria*, in *Arabia*, and in *Mesopotamia*. Some believe they have found its rightful place in *Armenia*, *Assyria*, or *Egypt*. If I may be permitted to express my opinion on the matter, it seems to me that they have all been much more concerned with discovering the true location of this aerial garden <note>The Dutch "Lufthof" refers to the theory that Paradise existed in a higher sphere of the atmosphere.</note> than with first carefully investigating whether such a place can even be found today. Therefore, they deserve to be compared to those who first divide a bear’s skin, or make a certain calculation of what they shall do with it, without even asking if the bear has been caught yet. In similar types of errors, the so-called greedy *Alchemists*, or, to put it better, those poor and gold-less gold-seekers, tend to overindulge: for those meticulous "nature-pluckers," those fine and sharp-witted sifters of matter, immediately join everyone else in searching for their so-called *Philosopher's Stone* <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"; a legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold.</note>, which they firmly believe can be found either in the air, or in the dew, or perhaps in saliva, in urine, in mercury, and who knows in how many more innumerable and strange things: without first investigating whether it is even possible that such a kind of wonder-stone is found in all of nature, or has ever been found.

<column-break/>

To continue with the pursuit of our design, one should know that modern observations, which are still made daily by very many meticulous lovers of physics and nature, and were also made before our times by the learned with great attention and singular caution, show us clearly enough and convince us that the previous condition of the first-created Earth must have been entirely changed and reshaped since the Great Flood <note>The "Zondvloed" or Noachian Deluge was a central concern for 18th-century geologists trying to explain fossil records and landscape changes.</note>. Who, and where, then, does one wish to go seeking the Earthly Paradise? Who is he who dares to determine its true location with certainty, or demonstrate it with mathematical proofs? But how? What then shall be done with the description of *Moses*? Or must it be held as a fictional and *Romantic* <note>In this context, "Romanche" refers to a fabricated fable or work of fiction.</note> tale of a strange and unknown land that can never be found and is to be discovered nowhere? By no means; for although the first-created realm of Earth suffered greatly through the irresistible violence of that heavy and mournful flood, and was thereby sufficiently devastated and destroyed, it was nonetheless happily restored by GOD’S Grace, and brought into nearly the same state and condition as before: the Rivers, Mountains, and Valleys that were on the globe before the Flood have all remained the same. Everything in the general reshaping or renewal of the Earth took place in the same manner as in the first creation, because the most benevolent Creator had the same goal in mind then, and the same equilibrium of bodies among one another, the same effects and movements, the same nature of things, and finally the same essential form of the Earth remained. In this way, everyone must confess that Holy Scripture is brought into agreement with Physics, and *Moses* is joined together with Reason.

Let us now see further (for without doubt quite a few remarkable and rare things will be seen in the Earthly Paradise) what various writers have imagined regarding this blessed place of pleasure. The famous *Sturmius* <note>Johann Christoph Sturm (1635–1703), a German philosopher and mathematician who sought to bridge the gap between science and religion.</note>, frequently cited in this work, will bring forth for us in this case abundant material of strange and wonderful opinions and feelings, all of which we shall attempt to analyze one after the other as best we can. Doubt not that this accompanying Map, though it is very small and brief in scope, will alone provide us with enough work to keep our attention busy.

First, he proposes to us the extraordinary opinion of that world-famous Englishman *Burnet* <note>Thomas Burnet (c. 1635–1715), author of "Telluris Theoria Sacra," who proposed that the Earth originated as a smooth crust over a watery abyss.</note>, which appears all the more wonderful as it deviates further from all others. This writer proceeds in his singular opinion with almost the same haste and extravagance as the reckless Phaëton <note>A figure from Greek mythology who lost control of the sun chariot, nearly destroying the earth.</note> of poetic history once did, who threw Heaven and Earth into turmoil through the unwise driving of his Father’s Sun-chariot, with which that ignorant youth caused a general conflagration and made everything change its form. So it is nearly the case here with our Englishman. He firmly imagines that the first-built world was very...

# NATURAL PHILOSOPHY

...was different in nature and constitution before the general Flood <note>The Great Flood of Noah.</note> than it is now. The entire globe, he says, as far as it extends, was everywhere nothing other than an Earthly Paradise, where an everlasting and delightful Spring resided: the three other seasons of the year were, in his view, completely unknown at that time. Everywhere one found the same pleasant and healthy temperance of the air. Everything was equally fertile, equally airy, and equally blessed. The common lifespan of mortals was much longer than the present, for according to his saying, they lived at that time at least eight or nine hundred years. Certainly a beautiful number of centuries for those happy Earth-dwellers of the first world. The fertility of the Earth was suited to the state of these first inhabitants; their way of life was very moderate and simple; one found all kinds of ripe and fully-grown fruits throughout the whole year: the ground lay much higher than today, and was built upon a deep and undivided Abyss of Waters; the ground was everywhere smooth and level; one found neither mountains nor valleys; one knew then of no hailstorms, nor of thunder or lightning, of storm or tempest, such as we nowadays often experience with great damage. Both the poles <note>original: "Afpunten"</note> were level with the Equator; the rivers of Paradise had their origin from vapors which, flowing together under the Equator, were driven toward the poles, and from there ran back with a gentle and still flood. The so-called Belt or mid-located hot air region <note>The Torrid Zone or Tropics.</note> was entirely uninhabitable, and has been identified by him as that *flaming blade of a sword* <note>original: "vlammig lemmer eenes zwaards"</note> of which *Genesis 3, verse 24* makes mention. He separates the world from the world itself, and sets the Northern regions entirely apart from the Southern ones, so that for him almost another world is found in the North than in the South. Here he places the so-called *Elysian Fields* of the Pagans, the *Fortunate Isles*, the *Pleasure Gardens of Hesperia*, which differ very little from those famous *Hanging Gardens of Alcinous* of which *Homer* speaks, and consequently may not be compared without reason to that *Heavenly Earth* of which *Plato* is the inventor in his *Phaedo*. The limitations of this space do not allow this proposition to be further analyzed according to the demands of the matter. Let it suffice that everyone knows that such an opinion rightly deserves to be held as very suspicious and rejectable by the whole world, because the sacred content of the Holy Scripture is thereby completely distorted and arranged according to the weak, limited, and deceptive understanding of a man, instead of wishing to conform somewhat to the simple style and the common manner of speaking of the Bible.

<column-break/>

All the particular opinions of other writers are much more easily brought into agreement with our main thesis; also, they would be able to understand each other much better than with the aforementioned *Burnet* <note>Thomas Burnet (1635–1715), author of "Telluris Theoria Sacra," who proposed that the Earth was originally a smooth shell over a watery abyss.</note>, because they all either remain closest within the boundaries of the world-state established by us, or at least do not deviate from the example of the first-created world in their opinion regarding the reformed or renewed world after the Flood.

*Johannes Herbinius* in his Latin work, *On the Admirable Cataracts of the World, Dissertation V: On the Cataracts of Paradise* <note>original: "de admirandis Mundi cataractis, Diff. V. de Cataractis Paradiafis"</note>, is of the opinion that the Earthly Paradise, or the *Garden of Eden*, is a wide-stretching landscape which occupies a large part of our accompanying map, and whose furthest boundaries toward the East and the Caspian Sea border Assyria, being enclosed to the North by Armenia and Cappadocia, to the West and the Mediterranean Sea by Palestine or the Promised Land, and to the South by Arabia, as far as the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. The geometric boundary line of this Paradise takes its course Westward along Phoenicia, the land of the Philistines and Egypt to the mouth of the Nile: toward the South along Stony and Desert Arabia; toward the East along Chaldea, Babylonia, and Assyria; and Northward along Armenia, Cilicia, and Syria as far as the landscape of Damascus.

*Dethleu Cluverus, Geology page 156* and *Whiston* <note>William Whiston (1667–1752), an English theologian and mathematician.</note> place the Earthly Paradise in the Southern regions of Mesopotamia, between Arabia and Persia. According to their opinion, the two main rivers, namely the Tigris and the Euphrates, having been joined with one another, had one and the same course along that most delightful valley, which itself was formerly the Edenic Pleasure Garden, but is now flooded by the waters of the Persian Gulf, which run into the Persian Sea through four different outlets, of which two retain their original names, to wit the *Tigris* and the *Euphrates*; but the other two have received the names of *Pishon* and *Gihon*.

*Johannes van der Mark*, that famous theologian, *Dissertation: On the True Site of Paradise* <note>original: "Diff: de vero Paradisi situ"</note>, may also not be counted among those who go looking for Paradise in the middle of Paradise itself, because of the great changes that formerly occurred in that Garden of bliss...

One finds those who have placed it in *Syria*, in *Arabia*, and in *Mesopotamia*. Some believe they have found its rightful place in *Armenia*, *Assyria*, or *Egypt*. If I may be permitted to express my opinion regarding this, it seems to me that they have all been much more concerned with discovering the true situation of this Pleasure Garden than first carefully investigating whether such a place can actually be found today. For this reason, they well deserve to be compared to those who first divide a bearskin <note>A Dutch idiom similar to "counting your chickens before they hatch," referring to selling the skin before the bear is caught.</note>, or make a certain estimate of what they shall do with it, without once asking whether that bear has even been caught. In a similar sort of error, the so-called money-hungry *Alchemists*—or, to put it better, those poor and gold-less Gold-seekers—are prone to overindulge: for those precise investigators of nature, those fine and sharp-witted sifters of matter, immediately join everyone in the search for their so-called *Philosophers' Stone* <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note>, which they firmly trust is to be found either in the air, or in the dew, or perhaps in saliva, in urine, in mercury, and who knows in how many more innumerable and strange things: without first investigating whether it is even possible that such a kind of wonder-stone is found in all of nature, or has ever been found.

To remain with the continuation of our design, one should know that modern Observations, which are still made daily by very many precise and physics-loving enthusiasts, and were also made before our times by the Learned with great attention and singular caution, show us clearly enough and convince us that the previous condition of the first-created Earth must have been entirely changed and reformed since the general Flood <note>The Great Flood of Noah.</note>. Who, and where then, would one go to seek the earthly Paradise? Who is he that dares to determine its true location with certainty, or demonstrate it with mathematical proofs?

<column-break/>

But how? What then shall be done with the description by *Moses*? Or must the same be held for a fictitious and *Romantic* <note>In this context, "Romantic" refers to a fictional tale or novel, rather than the later artistic movement.</note> tale of a strange and unknown land, which can never be found and is to be discovered nowhere? Not at all; for although the first-created Earth suffered greatly through the irresistible violence of that heavy and mournful flood, and was thereby sufficiently devastated and destroyed, it was nonetheless happily restored by God's Grace, and brought nearly into the same state and condition as before. The Rivers, Mountains, and Valleys that were on the Earth before the Flood have all remained the same. Everything in the general reformation or renewal of the Globe occurred in the same manner as in the first creation, since the most benevolent Creator then had the same purpose in mind; the same gravity of bodies among one another, the same effects and movements, the same nature of things, and finally the same essential form of the Earth remained. In this manner, everyone must confess that Holy Scripture is brought into agreement with Natural Philosophy, and *Moses* is joined together with Reason.

Let us now see further (for without doubt there will be quite a few remarkable and rare things to see in the Earthly Paradise) what various writers have imagined regarding this blissful Place of Pleasure. The renowned *Sturmius* <note>Likely Johann Christoph Sturm (1635–1703), a German philosopher and mathematician who sought to bridge science and theology.</note>, frequently cited herein, shall in this instance bring forth for us an abundance of strange and wonderful opinions and feelings, all of which we shall try to analyze one after the other as best we can. Doubt not that this accompanying Map, though it is very small and brief in scope, will provide us with enough work alone to keep our attention occupied.

First, he proposes to us the extraordinary opinion of that widely famous Englishman *Burnet* <note>Thomas Burnet (c. 1635–1715), author of "Telluris Theoria Sacra" (Sacred Theory of the Earth), which proposed that the Earth was originally a smooth shell over an abyss of water.</note>, which appears all the more wonderful as it deviates further from all others. This writer proceeds in his singular opinion with almost the same haste and extravagance as the reckless *Phaëton* did in the Poetic Histories, who threw Heaven and Earth into turmoil by the ignorant driving of his Father’s Sun-chariot, with which that unskilled youth caused a general fire and made everything change its form. So it is here almost the same with our Englishman. He firmly imagines that the first-built world was very...

# N A T U R A L   P H I L O S O P H Y .
<note>original: "NATUURKUNDE"</note>
N

...was of a different nature and constitution before the general Great Flood than it is now. The entire globe, he says, as far as it extends, was everywhere nothing other than an Earthly Paradise, where an everlasting and delightful Spring resided; the three other main seasons of the year were, in his thoughts, entirely unknown at that time. One had everywhere the same pleasant and healthy moderation of air. Everything was equally fertile, equally joyful, and equally blessed. The common lifespan of mortals was far longer than the present one, for according to his saying, they lived at least eight or nine hundred years in those times. Truly a fine number of centuries for those happy Earth-dwellers of the first world. The fertility of the Earth was suited to the state of the first humans; their way of life was very moderate and simple; one found all kinds of ripe and mature fruits throughout the entire year. The ground lay much higher than it does today and was built upon a deep and undivided Abyss of Waters; the ground was everywhere smooth and level; one found neither mountains nor valleys. People then knew nothing of hailstorms, nor of thunder or lightning, of tempests or storms, such as we nowadays often experience with great damage. Both the poles were aligned with the equator <note>The author is describing Thomas Burnet’s theory that the Earth’s axis was originally perpendicular to the sun, meaning no seasonal changes occurred.</note>; the rivers of Paradise had their origin in vapors which, flowing together under the Equator, were driven toward the poles and from there flowed back with a gentle and quiet tide. The so-called Torrid Zone <note>original: "Gordel of midden-in-gelegen heete Luchtſtreeck"</note> or centrally located hot climate zone was entirely uninhabitable and was regarded by him as that *flaming blade of a sword* <note>original: "vlammig lemmer eenes zwaards"</note> mentioned in *Genesis 3:24*. He separates the world from the world itself, and sets the Northern regions entirely apart from the Southern ones, so that in his view, one finds essentially a different world in the North than in the South. Here he places the so-called *Elysian Fields* of the Heathens, the *Islands of the Blessed*, and the *Pleasure Gardens of Hesperia*, which differ very little from those famous *Hanging Gardens of Alcinous* of which *Homer* speaks, and consequently may not without reason be compared to that *Heavenly Earth* of which *Plato* is the inventor in his *Phaedo*. The limitations of this space do not allow for a further dissection of these propositions as the subject requires. Let it be enough that everyone knows that such an opinion rightly deserves to be held as very suspicious and rejectable by the entire world, because the sacred content of Holy Scripture is thereby entirely twisted and adapted to the weak, limited, and deceptive understanding of a man, instead of wishing to conform somewhat to the simple style and common manner of speaking of the Bible.

All the particular opinions of other writers are much easier to reconcile with our Main Thesis; they could also understand one another much better than with the aforementioned *Burnet*, because they all remain roughly within the boundaries of the "World-Island" <note>A term for the contiguous landmass of the known world.</note> established by us, or at least do not deviate from the example of the first-created world in their opinion regarding the reformed or renewed world after the Flood.

*Johannes Herbinius*, in his Latin work *On the Admirable Cataracts of the World, Dissertation V: On the Cataracts of Paradise* <note>original: "de admirandis Mundi cataractis, Diſſ. V. de Cataractis Paradiciaſis"</note>, is of the opinion that the Earthly Paradise, or the *Garden of Eden*, is a wide-stretching landscape which occupies a large part of our adjacent map, and whose furthest borders to the East and the Caspian Sea border Assyria, being enclosed to the North by Armenia and Cappadocia, toward the West and the Mediterranean Sea by Palestine or the Promised Land, and to the South by Arabia, reaching to the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. The geometric boundary line of this Paradise takes its course westward along Phoenicia, the land of the Philistines, and Egypt as far as the mouth of the Nile; to the South along Arabia Petraea and the Desert; to the East along Chaldea, Babylonia, and Assyria; and northward along Armenia, Cilicia, and Syria as far as the landscape of Damascus.

*Dethleu Cluverus* <note>original: "Geol. p. 156."</note> and *Whiston* place the Earthly Paradise in the more southerly regions of Mesopotamia, between Arabia and Persia. According to their opinion, the two main rivers, namely the Tigris and the Euphrates, having been joined together, had one and the same course along that most delightful valley, which itself was formerly the Edenic Pleasure Garden, but is now flooded by the waters of the Persian Gulf, which run into the Persian Sea along four different outlets, of which two retain their original names—to wit, the *Tigris* and the *Euphrates*—but the other two have received the names *Pison* and *Gihon*.

*Johannes van der Mark*, that famous theologian, in his *Dissertation on the True Location of Paradise* <note>original: "Diſſ: de vero Paradiſi ſitu"</note>, should also not be counted among those who go looking for Paradise in the middle of Paradise itself, because of the great changes that formerly occurred in that Garden of Bliss...

# SPIRITUAL
<note>The header "GEESTELYKE" likely completes the title "GEESTELYKE NATUURKUNDE" or Spiritual Natural Philosophy.</note>

destruction was caused by the all-destroying Deluge; but he is of the opinion that of the four main rivers that flowed out of Eden, no more than three or possibly only two remain. He also holds as most provable that the true location of the Earthly Paradise can never be found elsewhere than in *Chaldea* or *Babylonia*, or perhaps in *Mesopotamia*.

Who knows whether the learned *Hadrianus Reland*, who, like several other prominent writers, treated the Earthly Paradise in his *Dissertation on Paradise* <note>original: "Dissert. de Paradiso"</note>, might not deserve the prize despite his opponents? He places the blessed *Eden* in *Armenia* (see letter B) and encloses it between four rivers, namely the *Phasis*, the *Araxes*, the *Tigris*, and the *Euphrates*, which in all appearance are those same four so-called Paradise streams *Pishon*, *Gihon*, *Hiddekel*, and *Phrath*. He suggests they once sprang from one and the same source, which today—like Paradise itself—is no longer found, as it is now perhaps hidden beneath the earth and lies locked away there like a concealed reservoir of water to feed these four rivers. This opinion is strengthened by *Tournefort* in his *Voyage to the Levant, Vol. II, p. 324* <note>original: "Voyage du Levant. T. II. p. 324"</note> who believes he found Paradise in the fertile valleys of *Georgia*, located on a certain path or region between *Erzurum* and *Tbilisi* <note>original: "Erzeron and Teflis"</note>, specifically at the place where the so-called Three Churches stand, which are situated about twenty French miles from the *Euphrates*, the *Araxes*, and the *Phasis*: so that according to his word, Paradise must have been in *Iberia* <note>A historical region in the Caucasus, roughly modern-day Georgia.</note> and *Armenia*.

The renowned *Huetius* <note>Pierre Daniel Huet (1630–1721), a French churchman and scholar.</note> considers the true Paradise stream to be the *Euphrates* joined with the *Tigris* in *Arabia*, discharging itself into the Persian Gulf via four particular outlets. Consequently, Paradise extends from C. to C., where *CE* is the *Gihon*, *Ce* is the *Pishon*, *Susiana* is *Cush*, and *Havilah* is toward the West side of the River *Ce*.

*Clericus* <note>Jean Le Clerc (1657–1736), a Genevan theologian.</note>, also a chronicler of Paradise, believes this blessed place of delight was located in *Syria* (see letter D), where he still points out the ancient riverbeds from the Flood of the *Pishon* in those of the river *Chrysorrhoas* <note>The Barada river in Damascus.</note>. He places the landscape of *Havilah*, inhabited by *Shem's* descendants, adjacent to that of *Cush*, toward the side of the River *Orontes*: he also maintains the *Euphrates* and the *Tigris* there alongside the others.

Van *Til* <note>Salomon van Til (1643–1713), a Dutch theologian.</note> places Paradise in a higher region of *Mesopotamia* (see letter A) and

<column-break/>

says that no more than one Flood <term>Flood|Here used to mean a great river or stream</term> A c. sprang from Eden, whose remains, according to his guess, are to be found in a branch which today is called *Odeine* and flows into the *Tigris*. He considers the river *Cobbaris* to be the *Gihon* and the *Delas* to be the *Pishon*. The adjacent Land of *Cush*, which lies by the *Euphrates*, he regards as *Arabia*.

The learned *Sturmius* <note>Johann Christoph Sturm (1635–1703), a German philosopher and mathematician.</note> seems to be of nearly the same opinion as the aforementioned *Clericus*, since he places Paradise not far from his, namely in *Aram Naharaim* <note>A biblical name for a region in Upper Mesopotamia, meaning "Aram of the Two Rivers."</note>, otherwise in the land of *Assyria*, which lies on the other side of the Euphrates. The river *Chrysorrhoas* was, so he believes, much wider in former times, and in its course traversed the ancient gold-rich landscape of *Havilah*, namely that which was inhabited by the descendants of *Shem*; for the other was undoubtedly that of *Ham's* descendants. The *Orontes* is, for him, the *Hiddekel*. Furthermore, he suspects that in previous times the *Euphrates* had its course in the Fields of *Damascus*, where he believes this river had its origin. He also asserts that even today certain signs or riverbeds of the *Gihon* can be seen at or near the rivers *Jabbok*, *Arnon*, and *Zared*, which all empty into the Salt Sea, otherwise called the Dead Sea.

Whatever the truth of this may be, I judge it not to be my duty to further dissect all the particular opinions cited above, or to enter the arena of debate against them all. Let it be enough to have brought forward the various opinions of these diligent Paradise-seekers for the satisfaction of my reader, without having to answer them all. Moreover, I find such a thing quite unnecessary given the abundance of material, with which one could very easily fill an entire book, something that would undoubtedly lead us entirely away from the objective we are aiming for. I am quite content that everyone chooses what pleases them in this matter; everyone may follow their own mind. I will freely confess that I shall never envy anyone the glory of having discovered the Earthly Paradise: this alone I wish for the nature-loving reader, for myself, and for all mortals: that even if we had never sought nor found the Earthly place of delight of our first parents, we may nevertheless reach the blessed possession of the celestial and eternal Eden through God's grace.

# PLATE SHEET XXV.

->*And the gold of that land is good: there is also bdellium, and the onyx stone.* <note>original: "En 't Goud dezes lands is goed: daar is ook Bedolah, en de steen Sardonix."</note> Genesis II. v. 12.<-

> The GOLD given to mortals by the CREATOR'S favor,
> To serve as an earthly ornament in this life,
> Soon drove Man to unholy selfishness,
> After Father Adam’s fall and his corrupt state.
> Why do men tremble in strife, discord, and bitter state-quarrels,
> Only to see their bloody role played here for glinting Gold?
> But let us remain silent here: GOD has deemed it good,
> For otherwise He would never have brought forth the gold mine.

Without doubt, the "good Gold" mentioned here by Moses is of the same nature as what we today call fine, pure, and raw gold, which has not yet been purified by fire: whether it be dug out of gold mines or fished out of the sand of rivers—which seems most likely—and is therefore called <term>gold dust</term> <note>Dutch: *stofgoud*</note> by us, and *Gold-sand* by the High Germans. This "stream-gold" or "river-gold" serves the scholar Reland <note>Adriaan Reland (1676–1718) was a Dutch orientalist and cartographer known for his studies on the Holy Land.</note> marvelously well in his opinion regarding the river *Phasis*, which he traces back to Paradise and to which he ascribes a gold-rich flood.

Certainly, this also serves as a singular glory for the ancient *Colchis*, which the aforementioned writer considers to be the previously mentioned *Havilah* <note>original: "Chauilah"</note>. In former times, it was one of the richest and most powerful cities in all of *Asia*; its inhabitants, according to the testimony of Agathias <note>original: "Agathias Hist. L. III. p. 72." — Agathias was a 6th-century Byzantine historian.</note>, once excelled above all other nations of the world in wealth, splendor, and abundance of Gold; yet today it is one of the meanest and poorest places. Who knows if his opinion regarding the mentioned *Colchian* or *Scythian* Gold is not strengthened by the saying of Elihu in *Job XXXVII. 22*: *From the North comes Gold?* <note>In many modern translations, this verse refers to "golden splendor" or fair weather, but the author here treats it literally.</note> By this, we understand in our translation "fair and clear weather" that is as bright as gold, especially if one wishes to maintain, as many are of the opinion, that Moses himself wrote the Book of *Job*.

Far more difficulty arises in accurately investigating what the sacred Writer actually intended to signify with the word *Bdellium* <note>original: "Bedolach"</note> mentioned above, as much can be argued against it. It is considered by many to be a <term>mineral</term>. The translators of the <term>Septuagint</term> <note>original: "LXX Overzetters"</note> called it the *Carbuncle stone* in their translations. Reland, along with many Jewish teachers or Rabbis who wrote on this matter long before his time, is of the opinion that one should understand it as *Rock Crystal* (depicted in Figure I). In this, the Septuagint translators even agree with him, as they translated that word in *Numbers XI. 7* in that manner. That *Crystal* is found in *Scythia* is testified by Solinus <note>original: "Solinus C. 15." — Gaius Julius Solinus, a 3rd-century Roman geographer.</note>: *There is also Crystal,* says this writer, *and although it is found in most regions of Europe and in a part of Asia, that which comes from Scythia is by far the most precious of all.* Moreover, according to the testimony of Dionysius Periegetes <note>original: "Dionysius Perieget V. 781." — An ancient geographer.</note>, the same is found in abundance near the river *Thermodon*, which lies next to the *Phasis*, from which the former received the name of "Crystalline Stream." Those who make of the *Bdellium* or *Carbuncle stone* a *Beryl* have little difference; for one even finds among the interpreters, for the first kind of *Crystal*, the word *Belur*, which is to say *Beryl*; because they likely read *Bedolach* in place of *Bedolach* <note>The author is likely noting a minor orthographic or phonetic variation in the Hebrew roots.</note>.

C. 5." — Samuel Bochart (1599–1667) was a French Protestant biblical scholar who wrote the *Hierozoïcon*, a treatise on the animals of the Bible.</note> even goes over to the small creatures and believes the *Bdellium* to be a <term>mother-of-pearl shell</term>. See Figure II. By this, it would seem, the location of *Havilah*, which he places in Arabia near *Calipha* and *Bahrain* where there is a large pearl fishery, would be somewhat confirmed. He also points out the reason why *Manna* is compared with *Bdellium* in *Numbers XI. 7*, namely on account of its whiteness and round shape. Furthermore, he derives its name from the He- <note>The text cuts off here at the catchword "He-", likely continuing "Hebrew" on the following page.</note>

<header>SPIRITUAL</header>

<columns>2</columns>

...the Hebrew word *Badal* <note>original: *Badal*; a root meaning to divide or distinguish</note>, which signifies *to separate* or *to divide*. This is possibly because the *Bedolach* <note>Usually translated as "bdellium," though its exact nature—whether a resin or a pearl—was a subject of great debate among early modern scholars.</note> must have been such a costly and excellent pearl that, due to its great value and singular excellence, it was distinguished from all other pearls. We shall not cite here the many other opinions of learned men who likewise consider the aforementioned stone to be a precious pearl.

Some of the translators who use the word *Bdellium* in their versions for the word *Bedolach* seek this precious commodity among the plants of the earth. This is the case in both of the Zurich Bibles, where the credibility of several excellent writers has been followed. There, the aforementioned *Bedolach* is translated as *Bdellium* and presented as a gummy plant, for the tree or plant is commonly taken to mean the gum itself. See <margin>Fig. III.</margin> *Dioscorides* <note>A Greek physician and botanist of the 1st century AD.</note> Book I, chapter 81, and *Pliny* <note>A Roman naturalist and author of *Natural History*.</note> Book XII, chapter 9—two ancient herbalists—speak more at length about the specific nature of this gum-bearing plant. Furthermore, modern botanists say that the so-called *Bdellium* tree, which is about as large as an olive tree, produces prickly leaves that are almost like those of an oak tree, though more oblong and narrow.

Everyone is free to judge the aforementioned *Bedolach* and its nature and properties as they wish. # SPIRITUAL

Hebrew word <term>Badal<note>original: *Badal*; a Hebrew root meaning to divide or separate.</note></term>, which signifies *to separate* or *to divide*; this is possibly because the <term>Bdellium<note>original: *Bedolach*; a substance mentioned in Genesis, variously identified as a resinous gum or a precious pearl.</note></term> must have been such a precious and excellent pearl that it was distinguished from all other pearls because of its great value and singular excellence. We shall not cite here the many other opinions of learned men who likewise consider the mentioned stone to be a precious pearl.

Some of the translators who use *Bdellium* in their versions for the word *Bedolach* seek this precious commodity among the plant life of the earth. This has occurred in both Zurich Bibles, where the reliability of various excellent writers has been followed, and the aforementioned *Bedolach*, here translated as *Bdellium*, is presented as a gummy plant product; for the tree or the plant is commonly mistaken for the gum itself. See <margin>Fig. III.</margin> <term>Dioscorides<note>A Greek physician and botanist whose "De Materia Medica" was a standard reference for centuries.</note></term> (Book I, chapter 81) and <term>Pliny<note>Pliny the Elder, author of the "Naturalis Historia."</note></term> (Book XII, chapter 9), two ancient herbalists, speak more extensively on the specific nature of this gum plant. Furthermore, modern botanists say that the so-called Bdellium tree, which is about as large as an olive tree, produces thorny leaves that are nearly like those of an oak tree, though more oblong and narrower.

Every person is free to judge the aforementioned *Bedolach* and its nature and properties as they wish. For my part, I would be in doubt whether to lean toward the side of *crystal* or toward that of *pearls*; nevertheless, to tell the truth, I favor the former more than the latter: just as the proposition of <term>Reland<note>Adriaan Reland (1676–1718), a Dutch scholar who wrote extensively on the geography of the Holy Land.</note></term> regarding the true location of Paradise pleases me far more than that of <term>Bochart<note>Samuel Bochart (1599–1667), a French scholar known for his work on biblical geography and animals.</note></term>, which he nonetheless believes he has demonstrated with so many and such powerful proofs that hardly anything seems to be lacking for a full conviction.

In the same way, the stone <term>Shoham<note>original: *Scholam*; this is a transcription or spelling variant of the Hebrew "Shoham," usually identified as Onyx.</note></term> is subject to no small amount of dispute and objection, notwithstanding that it was once esteemed of such value by the Jews that it served as an honorable breastplate ornament for the High Priest **Aaron** (Exodus 28:20, 39:6). <term>Aquila</term>, <term>Symmachus</term>, <term>Theodotion</term> <note>These were 2nd-century translators who produced Greek versions of the Old Testament.</note>, and several other High German writers and most all of their translators, put the word *Onyx* (which signifies a pearl) in place of *Shoham*. The aforementioned <term>LXX<note>The Septuagint, the earliest Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note></term> translators use the word <term>Smaragdus<note>The Latin and Greek root for "Emerald."</note></term> or *Emerald* for it, which is a green-colored and precious stone, found mostly in Scythia. This seems again to favor the aforementioned *Reland* in his presented location of Paradise. "That *sort of precious stone*," says Pliny (Book 38, chapter 5), "is held by the **Scythians** to be the most excellent and best of the whole land, and is therefore called the noblest Scythian stone: for one finds none like them elsewhere that are either finer in substance or have fewer defects; and as much as emeralds differ from other pearls, so much does this Scythian stone differ from emeralds." This is the reason that *Martianus* considers this *Scythian stone* to be the very best sort of emerald. *Sturmius* in his aforementioned *Explanation of Holy Scripture* (p. 45) identifies the stone *Shoham* as *Amber*.

# NATURAL SCIENCE.

### PLATE XXVI.

*And the LORD GOD commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:*
*But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die. Genesis II. v. 16. 17.*

> ->Eat, ADAM, what you desire, let it serve as your food,<-
> ->The Fruits of the Trees and all that EDEN bestows:<-
> ->Only beware of picking one fruit from this Tree;<-
> ->SUCH IS MY WILL, so that you do not harm yourself thereby.<-
> ->I do not intend for Man ever to taste these fruits,<-
> ->Let this be a commandment to you, which you must keep,<-
> ->Unless you desire that Death approach you:<-
> ->Know that you shall die as soon as you do otherwise.<-
> ->Therefore, O Man! do not deceive yourself,<-
> ->But do that which GOD commands you.<-

What does it profit a man to have the mere sight of something if he must be deprived of its use? What does it profit to behold with bare eyes that which one may not touch with hands? To what purpose then serve all those beautiful and delicious fruits of the Earthly Paradise, if *Adam* may not satisfy his eager appetite with them? Of what help is a well-laid table if eating is forbidden to us? From this very fact, GOD’S extraordinary Goodness toward Man is evident, for He daily brings forth—in place of the lost and consumed parts <note>The author refers to the biological process where the body "consumes" its own substance, requiring food to replenish it.</note>—an abundance of other foods that are exceptional in flavor, nourishing, and perfectly suited to the form of our bodies. For this reason, GOD THE LORD, to whom alone the supreme sovereignty over all creatures belongs by the perfect right of creation, commanded that *Man should freely eat of every tree of the Garden*; giving him moreover all the Herbs and Plants of the field for food, not wishing that such a noble and exalted creature should perish through want.

It only pleased the Creator to exempt one Tree, namely that of the *Knowledge of Good and Evil*, from among all others, to which He added a punishing and terrible threat, *that in the day that he, Adam, ate thereof, he should die the death*, or, according to the translation of others, *surely die*: <note>original: "zekerlyk zoude sterven"</note> that is to say, that the whole Man with all his exalted qualities and heavenly endowments would come to nothing. But hear in what manner!

*Adam* was created in the image of the most perfect Being, in the image of his Creator, in the likeness of GOD. He was endowed with a most

<column-break/>

pure Understanding, through which he could judge all things quite ingeniously without any effort or danger of committing any error, knowing the entire World and offering praise and thanks to GOD his Creator in a most perfect manner: having as a dwelling for his soul a well-ordered body, an artistic <note>In this context, "artistic" means "skillfully or intricately crafted."</note> and, in all its parts, a perfect Instrument, being kept in constant motion by air and <term>vital spirits</term> <note>These were believed to be subtle fluids or vapors that circulated through the body to provide life and movement.</note>. He found himself placed in a most fertile Garden of all kinds of Fruits and Plants, where there was a general abundance of every necessary provision: so that he lacked nothing in the world that could be in any way suitable, whether for the delight and pleasure of his Soul or for the sufficient satiation of his Body. Moreover, GOD had appointed him as Sovereign over three principal Kingdoms, namely over the *Animated*, <note>original: "Bezielde"</note> that is, all the living Animals of the Earth; over the *Vegetative*, that is, over all Trees, Herbs, and all manner of growing but soulless Creatures; and over the *Subterranean* or *Mineral*, that is, over all internal growths of the Earth, such as Gold, Silver, precious Stones, etc. The pleasant and healthy temperateness of the Air, the good condition of the Elements or <term>primary substances</term> <note>Referring to the classical elements: earth, water, air, and fire.</note> by which he was surrounded—in a word, the general constitution of all things—was so arranged for his comfort and well-being that he had no cause to fear the slightest discomfort or harm from any side; everything went according to his wish and pleasure: there was nothing that could hinder or disturb his perfect joy. He could have lived either eternally or at least for many thousands of Centuries without ever suffering any injury or detriment to his health...

It describes Adam as the sovereign over the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms, living in a world perfectly tuned for his well-being.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the theological discourse from page 55 regarding Adam’s life in Eden and the gravity of the single commandment given to him by God. It picks up mid-sentence discussing the requirements for Adam to remain in God's favor.</meta>

# SPIRITUAL

...to be worthy, so that finally, when it pleased the Almighty, he might be taken up from the Earthly Eden and transplanted into the Heavenly and eternal Paradise, where he would live for all eternity in a closer union with his GOD and Creator. However, that strict order, that Divine commandment alone—namely, a slight abstinence from the Fruit of one Tree—had to be strictly followed and faithfully maintained; for without this, it was entirely impossible to persevere in that blessed state forever. The Divine threat was of far too great a consequence: GOD’S Loving-kindness and Grace toward Man were exceedingly great, but the punishment He set alongside it against the transgressor was certainly no less. Who does not shudder when he considers that heavy threat of the Creator within himself? Let us see what was to follow. Immediately after the deed was committed, the transgressor would be a sworn enemy to GOD, the World, and himself: the clear enlightenment of his understanding would be completely darkened, numbed, and for a large part taken from him; his corrupt will would incline only toward evil; the Body would be subject to death; the wretched Man would have to struggle unceasingly with nameless diseases and discomforts, being forced to spend his entire life's course in an everlasting internal struggle and constant rebellion of his own passions, filled with sorrow. The firm bond of union that holds Soul and Body together would be loosened, and the close friendship that exists between them both would be entirely and forever separated on Earth. Moreover, if he were not snatched away by a sudden death immediately after the deed, mortality would at least follow, dragging after it an indescribable multitude of all kinds of disasters and miseries; and what is most terrifying of all, he would have to expect eternal death and exile from GOD'S Countenance. All creatures—Heaven, Earth, Elements, Times, Years, food and drink, and all that had been given to him for support—would all alike rise up against the unworthy and ungrateful tenant <note>The original Dutch uses *Leenhouder*, referring to a feudal vassal or tenant-farmer who holds land from a lord.</note>; in a word, the most happy Creature would become the most miserable, and he would have to exchange his Mastery for servitude, and his Dominion for slavery.

Regarding this matter, several Questions arise which the Learned are accustomed to propose concerning this subject; yet I have no desire to investigate nor solve such things. However, there seems to be one which I cannot well overlook in silence: namely, what kind of trees were that wondrous Tree of Life and that *Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil*, that unhappy wood of trial, actually? But, since Holy Scripture itself is silent, I can promise the curious Reader no other answer or solution than some slight and uncertain opinions of Learned Writers. Some maintain that it was a *Fig Tree*, which was therefore later cursed by *Christ*, and with whose leaves the transgressors covered their nakedness and rubbed and scraped their bodies out of repentance, in order to give outward signs of grief and regret. Others hold with the *Apple Tree*, believing its fruit—through its pleasant white and red-colored luster—to have been the bait of destruction. They attempt to clarify their opinion with this observation: namely, that when one cuts an apple crosswise through the middle, ten small lines that end in a central Pentagram <note>Original: *middelpuntigen Vyfhoek*. The author is referring to the five-pointed star shape visible in the core of a sliced apple.</note> are found in the cross-section, which they say is a prophecy or certain sign of the ten Commandments of GOD, against which the first Man would have sinned. If the aforementioned arguments do not give the Reader sufficient satisfaction, one may add the so-called *Adam’s Apple*, in which the poisonous scar of that deadly bite has remained forever; or otherwise, if one prefers, that *Adam’s Apple* <note>The laryngeal prominence in the human throat.</note>—that is, that cartilaginous lump which is commonly seen protruding under the chin in men, though more in some than in others.

There are also some who hold the *Vineyard* <note>Original: *Wyngaard*, referring here to the grapevine.</note> to be the Tree of destruction, because in Holy Scripture far more good and evil is attributed to the Vine than to any other Trees; all the more because GOD the Lord forbade all the High Priests who would approach the Sanctuary the use of Wine upon penalty of death, *Lev. X. 9.* <note>Leviticus 10:9: "Do not drink wine nor strong drink... when ye go into the tabernacle."</note>

NATURAL HISTORY.

# PRINT SHEET XXVII.

->And the LORD GOD caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the place thereof with flesh. And the rib, which the LORD GOD had taken from Adam, he built into a woman: and he brought her to Adam. Gen. II. v. 21, 22.<-

Let no one imagine that Adam’s deep sleep was a physical weakness or a case of lethargy. Far from it; that blessed Firstling of Mankind lived, both before and after that sleep, in perfect health, without being afflicted by any kind of illness. One should also not think that Adam fell asleep by God’s deliberate arrangement or with the intent that he would not feel the pain of the Creator’s intended work—namely, the production of Eve—which he otherwise would have felt if awake. For that same God, who had created Adam without his prior knowledge or feeling, could likewise protect him from all pain and sorrow that would commonly follow such an unheard-of operation. Such a sleep is called *Thardemah* in the Hebrew language <note>original: *Thardemah* (תרדמה), referring to a deep, divinely-induced slumber or trance</note>, and is of a singular nature, the likes of which cannot be found; from which Adam, having awakened, was exactly the same as before, without being changed in soul or body in any way. If one wishes to maintain that it was a *Trance* <note>original: *Zielverrukking*, literally "soul-rapture"</note>, according to the translation of the LXX <term>Septuagint; the earliest Greek translation of the Old Testament</term> translators, one must nevertheless distinguish it from the trance of a fallen human. Similarly, the Jewish teachers—otherwise called *Rabbis*—make a certain distinction between the *deep* and natural sleep, such as Adam's was, and the sleep of *Prophecy* or Prediction that came upon the Patriarch Abraham in *Genesis XV. v. 12*, as well as the sleep they call *Marmitha* <note>This likely refers to a "divine stupor" or "deadly sleep," as seen in 1 Samuel 26:12</note>, by which Saul's bodyguards were once overcome.

One may certainly say with good reason that the production of the first woman and universal mother EVE from Adam's Rib was very miraculous, indeed somewhat rare

<column-break/>

and rightly worthy of wonder; all the more so, because Man—or rather the Male—ordinarily has the number of twelve ribs on both sides, which is natural to humans, both before and after the creation of the Woman (which theologians usually call the "second creation"). It would be, in my opinion, very absurd and improper to suggest that there were thirteen ribs on one side and twelve on the other, or twelve on one side and no more than eleven on the other. It is true that perhaps the Hebrew root word signifies not only a *Rib*, but also generally a *Side*; just as the word *Selang* or *Zela* <note>original: *Tsela* (צלע), meaning side, rib, or structural beam</note>, understood according to the architectural meaning, signifies an *annex* or *side-building*—that is, a timber or masonry structure erected next to the Temple, of which mention is made in *Ezekiel XLI. 6*. Therefore, it seems more credible to me that EVE was formed or created from the side of Adam’s body, that is, from his internal parts or the parts lying around the heart, or perhaps from his muscular loins; especially because Holy Scripture clearly says that God *closed up and filled the place or side again with flesh*. It is a hideous and deformed fiction by those who maintain that the woman EVE was created at the same time and at one and the same moment as the man ADAM—indeed, what is most detestable of all, that they were grown together and stuck to one another at the shoulder blades or back. This would suggest that this creature, in the manner of the ancient Heathen monster *Janus* <note>The Roman god usually depicted with two faces looking in opposite directions</note>, or a *Hermaphrodite* <note>original: *Mannewyf*, literally "man-woman"</note>, represented Adam as a man from the front and Eve as a woman from the back.

### PRINT PLATE XXVII.

> *Then the LORD GOD caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place. And the LORD GOD built the rib, which he had taken from Adam, into a woman: and he brought her to Adam. Genesis 2:21, 22.*

Let no one imagine that *Adam’s* deep sleep was a physical weakness or a bout of lethargy. Far from it; 그that blessed Firstling of Mankind lived, both before and after that sleep, in perfect health, without being afflicted by any kind of illness. One should also not think that *Adam* fell asleep by GOD’S deliberate arrangement or intent so that he would not feel the pain of the Creator’s intended work—namely, the production of *Eve*—which he would otherwise have felt if he were awake. For that same GOD, who had created *Adam* without his prior knowledge or sensation, could likewise preserve him from all pain and sorrow that would commonly follow such an unheard-of operation. Such a *sleep* is called *Thardemah* <note>original: "Thardemah", a Hebrew term for a deep, divinely-induced slumber</note> in the Hebrew language, and is of a singular nature, the like of which is not to be found. From this sleep *Adam* awoke entirely the same as he was before, without being changed in soul or body. If one wishes to maintain that it was an *Ecstasy* <note>original: "Zielverrukking", literally "soul-rapture"</note> according to the translation of the Septuagint <note>The "LXX", an ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> translators, one must nevertheless distinguish it from the ecstasy of a fallen man. Similarly, the Jewish Teachers—otherwise called *Rabbis*—make a certain distinction between the *deep* and natural sleep, such as *Adam’s* was, and the sleep of *Prophecy* or Prediction that came over the Patriarch Abraham (Genesis 15:12), as well as the sleep called *Marmitha* <note>A term for a supernatural stupor or heavy sleep</note> by them, which once overcame *Saul’s bodyguards* (1 Samuel 26:12).

One may certainly say with good reason that the production of the first Woman and universal Mother EVE from *Adam’s Rib* was quite miraculous—even rare and rightly worthy of wonder. This is all the more so because man (or specifically the Male) typically has the standard number of twelve ribs on both sides, which is proper to humans, both before and after the creation of the Woman (which theologians usually call the "Second Creation"). It would, in my opinion, be quite absurd and unbecoming to suggest that there were thirteen ribs on one side and twelve on the other, or perhaps twelve on one side and no more than eleven on the other. It is true that the Hebrew root word may signify not only a rib, but also a *side* in general. In the same way, the word *Selang* or *Zela* <note>original: "Selang" or "Zela"</note>, understood according to its architectural meaning, signifies a *lower-structure* or *side-building*—that is, a timber or masonry work erected next to the Temple, as mentioned in Ezekiel 41:6. Therefore, it seems more credible to me that EVE was formed or created from the side of *Adam’s* body—that is, from his internal parts or the parts lying around the heart, or perhaps from his muscular loins. This is especially likely because Holy Scripture clearly says that GOD *closed and filled the place or side again with flesh*. It is a hideous and misshapen fiction of those who maintain that the woman EVE was created at the same time and moment as the man ADAM; indeed, what is most detestable of all is the claim that they were grown together and adhered to one another at the shoulder blades or back. In this view, this creature would have resembled the ancient Heathen monster *Janus* <note>A Roman god typically depicted with two faces, looking in opposite directions</note>, or a *Hermaphrodite* <note>original: "Mannewyf", literally "man-woman"</note>: Adam, a man, in front, and Eve, a woman, behind.

### PRINT PLATE XXVIII.

*Now the serpent was more subtle than any beast of the field which the LORD GOD had made; and he said unto the woman: Yea, hath GOD said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?* Genesis 3:1.

> The Snake, that cunning Snake, the slyest Beast of all,
> Is the cause that Man from his GOD did fall
> Through the transgression of the Divine command:
> Crawl, Footless one, crawl; be a mockery to Man and beast.

Regarding the calamitous Fall of the Human Race, many and very weighty difficulties arise, which we intend to treat here as briefly as possible, as many matters are involved that do not concern Natural Philosophy and fall entirely outside the boundaries of our philosophical scope.

Firstly, I am greatly displeased by the *allegorical* <note>symbolic or metaphorical</note> or borrowed and veiled way of speaking used by *Philo* <note>Philo of Alexandria, a Hellenistic Jewish philosopher</note>, who considers the Serpent to be an *emblem* of *charming and excessive pleasures*. But the views of *Cornelius Agrippa* <note>An occult writer and polymath</note> and those of *Hadrian Beverland* <note>A Dutch scholar known for his controversial views on original sin as sexual lust</note> are far more ungodly; indeed, they are such that even decency forbids bringing their loathsome conjectures to light—one of whom had to pay for his imagined thoughts with eternal imprisonment and the loss of his senses. Likewise, I reject the unjust opinions of all those who wish to claim that not only this present story, but the entire history of the World’s creation, as well as all the other works of GOD brought forth within the *first six days*, and that of the Earthly Paradise, must be understood in a symbolic and figurative sense, and held to be nothing other than a mere parable. The excessive freedom of such borrowed, corrupted, and veiled speech opens a path to all kinds of licentiousness; it is a destructive means to deceive all ignorant and gullible people, a fertile spring for a hollow head to learn to forge all kinds of harmful fables, and to twist the Holy Scripture to everyone’s whim. In a word, it is a smooth and slippery track that leads Man toward Freethinking <note>original: "Vrygeestigheid", referring to Enlightenment-era religious skepticism</note> and to his eternal ruin. That such views are in themselves nothing other than mere figments of the brain and self-imagined ideas of perverse and de-

<column-break/>

praved observers of nature is evident from the explicit mention made of the Serpent, even speaking, in the Holy Scripture, and from the heavy punishment imposed upon that deceptive animal by the Creator.

Also finding no entrance with me are the strange propositions of *Josephus*, of the *Jews*, and of many among the *Socinians* <note>A rationalist Christian sect that often denied the divinity of Christ and original sin</note>, who imagine that this Serpent was a completely natural animal, endowed with clear speech, reasoning, and human inclinations, cunning and crafty, and able to walk upright on its legs; in a word, such that it was also capable of proposing a question, stirring doubt in the minds, and forming a contradictory or wrong conclusion. Such singular qualities do not belong to a mindless beast that is voiceless and without speech, nor may they be attributed to any animal by men. *Isaac Abarbanel* <note>A famous Jewish statesman and theologian</note> seems to have judged far better and with more probability in one case, suggesting that the natural Serpent deceived and betrayed Eve not so much through its reasoning, but rather by its example and rare turnings, as it repeatedly climbed up and down the forbidden Tree, and ate of the fruit of this Tree without any ill consequence, since it was permitted to do so. If the matter were understood in such a sense, the entire deception would have consisted in Eve’s own sinful thoughts; however, this would absolutely conflict with the content of the Holy Scripture, as it explicitly says the general Mother was seduced and charmed by the craftiness and speech of the Serpent, and moreover, it clearly mentions both the Question of the Serpent and the Answer of Eve.

The so-called *Ophites* or *Ophinians*, otherwise *Serpent-worshippers* or *Serpent-venerators*...

# NATURAL SCIENCE

->P<-

As has been said, those mentioned in the surviving works of the ancient <term>Church Fathers<note>Early influential Christian theologians and writers, such as Augustine or Origen, whose works established early doctrine.</note></term> likewise rightly deserve to be banished from the community of Christians, since some among them departed so far from reason that they were not ashamed to maintain that **Christ** himself was the Serpent. Others of that same sect believed the Serpent to be a more exalted and greater being than **Christ**—namely, the origin, initiator, or inventor of all sciences. These improper and ruinous doctrines came either from the so-called *Nicolaitans* or from the *Egyptians*, among whom it was customary to show divine service and reverence to certain birds called snake-eaters, as well as crocodiles and serpents. It is true that the Lord our Savior deigned to take on the human and mortal body—that is, the form of a servant—and become like his subjects in the flesh; but one reads nowhere that he ever appeared in the form of a serpent. Likewise, the well-known **Brazen Serpent** <note>A bronze image of a snake on a pole which, according to the Book of Numbers, God told Moses to erect so that Israelites bitten by snakes could be healed by looking at it.</note>, which was set up in former times, was indeed a symbol of **Christ**, yet it was not **Christ** himself; far be it from us to think that such a mere image should be considered worthier and more excellent than the original and matchless Example.

I am also not a follower of *Cajetan* <note>Thomas Cajetan (1469–1534), a Catholic theologian who often sought literal or rational explanations for biblical miracles.</note> nor of *Bekker* <note>Balthasar Bekker (1634–1698), a Dutch minister who famously argued in "The World Bewitched" that the Devil has no physical power in the world.</note>, who are of the opinion that no serpent or any animal of that kind was present at all during this event, but that the Devil himself—who must here be understood symbolically and regarded as the Serpent—was the true seducer of the universal mother, *Eve*. These men, so it seems to me, depart without any necessity from the literal sense of Holy Scripture, which explicitly states that a serpent was present.

The famous *Bochart* <note>Samuel Bochart (1599–1667), a French Protestant scholar and author of 'Hierozoicon,' a massive study of animals in the Bible.</note>, who may rightly be held as a wise and learned writer, is of the opinion that the serpent that seduced *Eve* was infused with something supernatural through the power of the evil spirit, just as he believes happened in later times to *Balaam's* donkey; but in such a manner, the Devil would be granted a power that no created spirit possesses or is entitled to. It is only God's work to make incapable things capable and to make speechless creatures speak; thus, it happens only through God's omnipotence and permission when any irrational animal, which is provided with no suitable instruments for speaking, produces any speech. It is also for this reason that it is said in *Numbers 22:28* that the Lord God himself—and not an angel clothed in a visible form—opened the mouth of the donkey.

<column-break/>

Almost all Christian writers who have clarified Holy Scripture through interpretations join the evil spirit and the *natural* serpent together, and say that it was possessed by the Devil. But even among them, there is a great difference regarding the application. Be that as it may; I cannot, however, find it in my mind to believe it plausible that the evil spirit would have had the power to move and direct the physical instruments of the serpent—which were entirely incapable of speaking—in such a way that it would have produced clear and understandable words. For this reason, with the permission of others, I would much rather move toward the opinion of those who—without dismissing the presence of the natural serpent, and especially one of such a form that it appeared beautiful and charming to Man—not without reason lay most of the guilt for the transgression upon that ancient murderer of the human race, that crafty seducer of souls, that constant adversary, that ruinous instigator, that degenerate and fallen angel of darkness—I mean our common enemy, the **Devil**. For it is easy to believe that this cunning deceiver, having hidden himself behind a strange and alluring mask, spoke kindly to the curious and incautious Woman and finally brought her to her fall: just as he later deceived more of her descendants, and especially the desperate and foolhardy *Saul*, under the form of the deceased prophet *Samuel* (1 Samuel 28). Truly, he was that cunning beast, that crafty serpent, *more crafty than all other beasts of the field*, who through his disguised and entangling rhetoric first entangled and caught the Woman, and after that the Man, in the net of destruction. For it would be, in my opinion, quite absurd to wish to attribute to a natural serpent the ability to enter into mutual conversation and reasoning with Man, to raise a point of dispute, to call a matter into doubt, subsequently to make a false conclusion, and to frustrate the whole force of persuasive reasoning with a clever twist. Who must not confess that all these circumstances are not applicable to an irrational animal at all?

Consequently, by that *great dragon, that old serpent, which deceives the whole world...* <note>original: "grooten Draak, die oude Slange, die de geheele weereld verleid..." quoting Revelation 12:9.</note> of which the Evangelist **John** makes mention in his book of Revelation *Ch. ### PLATE XXIX.

->*Then the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.*<-
->**Gen. III. v. 7.**<-

Nakedness, which today serves as a cause for mockery and shame to mankind, was innocent and irreproachable in the state of <term>Innocence<note>The original Dutch term "Onnoozelheid" here refers to the state of Adam and Eve before the Fall, meaning "harmlessness" or "purity" rather than "foolishness."</note></term>. That which was a sign of innocence before the Fall, just as it is still regarded as such today in respect to young children, is now a public sign of the Fall and of corruption itself. But for what reason? Why must one feel shame for the shameful parts, since these are no less necessary than all the others? Why have the tongue, hands, feet, face, and all the other limbs of the body not undergone the same fate, since these, as well as the first-mentioned parts, are often misused for the most shameful and abominable excesses and mistakes? It is said, indeed, that shame clings like a stain even to the simplest and most innocent things, but that they have been turned into irregularities through a terrible misuse. But, to tell the truth, this does not satisfy me. Moreover, when I look more closely into the nature of things, I find nothing therein that can satisfy in any way. This, however, is certain: that the fleshly lusts for the continuation of the Human Race before the Fall were moderated and well-ordered according to the demands and necessity of Nature and according to the use of Reason, without being mixed with any evil or sinful defect, or being punishable. The footprints of this very first Law of Nature are even yet seen daily in all irrational Animals.

<column-break/>

The *Fig Tree* is the first plant of the earth mentioned in the Holy pages, possibly because Adam used its fruits for the nourishment of his body, just as he afterwards covered his nakedness with the leaves of this Tree; which Tree, if one wishes to give credit to the ancient fables of the Heathens, is of a Divine origin. The concise account of the following history will show the reason for it. *Sycea* <note>In Greek mythology, Sykeus was one of the Titans. To save him from Zeus (Jupiter), his mother Gaia (the Earth) transformed him into a fig tree.</note>, one of the descendants of the *Titans*, being pursued everywhere by **Jupiter**, the **Earth**, our common Mother, took pity on the sad misfortune of this youth and hid the unlucky wanderer for some time from the fury of that great Pursuer; finally, to place him in safety forever, she transformed him into a Tree of his Name, that is, into a Fig Tree, from which the city of *Syceë* in Sicily has derived its name. What would it be, if one wanted to presuppose that Adam himself was that wretched *Sycea*, fleeing from the face of GOD, and [hiding] his nakedness under a...

### PLATE XXX.

*Then the LORD GOD said to that Serpent: because you have done this, you are cursed above all Cattle, and above every beast of the Field: upon your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.* Gen. III. v. 14.

---

That the crawling of the Serpent along the ground is a punishment imposed upon it by the LORD GOD is absolutely evident from the aforementioned words of Holy Scripture. However, many Scriptural and Natural Scholars raise great difficulties regarding this, and believe they may, not without reason, call this matter into doubt. This much is certain, however: that the threatened penalty of death, for which Mankind was guilty, can find no place in irrational Animals, since they are subject to no laws, nor can they be summoned before any Judge, nor do they understand the Pronounced Sentences. This is why those who hold the view of the natural Serpent are of the opinion that it was punished by the Creator as a tool of the Devilish seduction, just as in the Old Law all Animals that were complicit in any unnatural crime used to be punished as a curse upon their villainy.

Holy Scripture provides us with many examples of this: such as first in *Exod. XXI. 28. 29.* <note>Exodus 21:28-29</note> regarding the goring Ox; in *Levit. XX 15.* <note>Leviticus 20:15</note> regarding the Beasts that were abused by Humans for the execution of abominable and degenerate excesses of carnal lust; and in *Deut. XIII. 15.* <note>Deuteronomy 13:15</note> where the LORD commands that even the irrational Beasts, as well as the Humans, be punished with death. This same principle is taught to us by modern legal custom, which is frequently practiced in capital law, of hanging the pen alongside the forged seals above the head of a forger, and burning books of magic along with the sorcerers.

Furthermore, it is unlikely that all the species of Serpents, which are so numerous in their genus and distinct in nature and form, descended from a single mother—just as the entire Human race, of whatever nature or constitution it may be, has one and the same general origin from the first-created Founders of Mankind, *Adam* and *Eva*. Why then was that species of Serpent alone, through which *Eva* was seduced, not specifically punished? What reason is there that the innocent, as well as the guilty, must undergo the same punishment? Why was that Serpent alone, I say, which was the first seducer, not specifically cursed and punished by the Creator, apart from all others of its kind? And what is even more: does anyone know the reason why GOD imposed a much lighter punishment upon that crafty and destructive Animal—that hateful serpent, which by its malicious and wicked conduct deceived innocence, misled simplicity, and brought the thoughtless Woman *Eva* to such a heavy fall, dragging the general ruin of the entire Human Race behind it—than He later willed to be inflicted upon the Beasts that were punishable for the so-called <term>Sodomitic sin</term> <note>A historical legal term for sexual acts deemed "unnatural" by the church and state, often resulting in the execution of both the human and the animal involved.</note>, or the goring Ox that had killed but one person? What mortal has ever entered so far into GOD’S hidden secret chamber that he can solve this weighty Question?

Let us examine this imposed punishment a little more closely, and analyze it piece by piece. First, the aforementioned scriptural expression, *on your belly you shall go*, offers the Jewish Teachers a fine opportunity to bring forth many fables regarding this matter.

->SPIRITUAL<-

A great multitude among them witness to this, who claim that before the Fall the Serpent walked upright on its legs like a Camel, on whose back, so they say, **Samaël** <note>In Jewish midrashic tradition, Samael is often identified as the accusing angel or the figure who rode the serpent to tempt Eve.</note>, whom they believe to have been the true seducer of **Eva**, would have ridden. Others assert that the Serpent formerly walked at least on two, or possibly even on four legs, but that this rogue Animal, as the worst among all two- and four-footed Animals, afterwards became mutilated and footless. Why then should someone not also be allowed to say that speech, with which it was gifted before the transgression of GOD’S command, was taken from it at the same time? For one reads nowhere that any Serpent ever spoke after that time, and all those of its kind are still speechless today. Why, I say, if it were a natural Serpent, and consequently a powerless and incompetent tool to resist the Devil, did GOD not take away speech from Man, who was his own master, who had feet, hands, arms, and ears? He, after all, was the one, not the Serpent, who came to the forbidden Tree on his own feet, who plucked the fruit with his own hands, listened with his own ears, and held a conversation with the Serpent that spoke to him. For what reason are the two- or four-legged Dragons—if such are found, or if not, those at least depicted so by Artists—also free from this punishment? Why is it necessary, after the perfect and well-finished work of Creation, to bring forth a new kind of creature that is entirely reformed from the structural parts of which it previously consisted, and made crawling by the removal of its feet? Moreover, if one wishes to pay close attention to the essential shape of Serpents, one will undoubtedly find that no feet fit their elongated and flexible bodies, much less that two or four legs would be enough; far from it, even twenty would not be enough for such as **Philostratus** <note>Flavius Philostratus (c. 170–250 AD), a Greek sophist who wrote about legendary creatures in "The Life of Apollonius of Tyana."</note> describes, which, according to his saying, are thirty fathoms long. Just as the four-legged Beast lacks nothing for the preservation of its life although it has no wings, so likewise nothing more is required for the comfort and welfare of a Serpent, even though it is footless and must crawl on its belly; for it seeks its food and necessities by crawling everywhere with a sufficiently fast movement, climbing along walls and trees, and returning to its hiding places by crawling. If someone asks what kind of Serpent it actually was that seduced the first Man, **Bonfrere** and **Delrio** will give as an answer that a <unclear>sort</unclear> of Serpent comes forward which in Latin is called **Scytale** <note>original: "Scytale"; a mythical snake of uniform thickness throughout its length.</note>, and in Dutch **Spiny-Mouse** <note>original: "Spinne-Muys"; likely referring to a shrew or a specific mythical viper.</note>. **Eugubinus** will bring forward the so-called **Basilisk**, and **Magus** the Dragon. Whatever the case may be; this however is the most certain: that if one does not wish to remain with the clear expression of Holy Scripture in this case, it is entirely uncertain and doubtful what Animal was the true seducer; and that all and every opinion of those who have written about it are nothing but individual guesses and headstrong riddles of the Authors.

<column-break/>

Since the opinion of **Didymus Caten. Lipom.** <note>Referring to Didymus the Blind as cited in the "Catena" (chain of commentary) by Luigi Lippomano (1500–1559).</note> regarding the Serpent is very peculiar and rare, one may not well pass it by here in silence. This Author says the Serpent was created footless, but through the actions of the Devil received feet, which it afterwards lost again by virtue of the sentence of the Supreme Judge. How does this proposition appear to the judicious Reader? For me, I find it very peculiar—namely, very clumsy and ridiculous. Why did the Serpent need feet, since it can easily do without them and yet could seduce Man? Why did those imagined feet have to be taken away by GOD’S command, which would undoubtedly have disappeared by themselves? How could Holy Scripture in this case call the footlessness of the Serpent a punishment, since it had only been reformed for some time by the power of the Devil, and was then restored to its previous and comfortable state? How, or by whom, did the evil Spirit come by such power that he could make Serpent-feet and fit them to its chest?

The Hebrew root word **Gachon** <note>Hebrew: גָּחוֹן (gachon), referring to the belly of a reptile.</note> signifies not only the **Belly** or the **lower body**, but also the **Chest**; it is from this that one reads in the Greek translation of the **LXX Translators** <note>The Septuagint, the earliest Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note>, **upon your Chest and upon your Belly**. Both are to be well understood, for the Chest of Serpents is also the Belly, and the Belly is the Chest. Moreover, since they have no diaphragm, the cavity that extends from their head to the tail may for the same reason be called the Belly and the Chest.
