# SPIRITUAL

<meta>catchword: to</meta>

...stood before the Deluge. Certainly, it did not accord well with the nature of plants that those produced in India should be transported to Europe or carried to the most remote regions of the North, just as our native plants would undoubtedly not grow in hot climates. If one wishes to establish the matter in this way, it may be said that *Noah* had no need for a rudder, except possibly during the first two or three weeks to avoid the rocks. But perhaps it was not necessary to avoid these at all, because the Ark was not only guided by the Divine Providence of GOD, but was also so well preserved that it never ran the slightest danger of striking against rocks, or of being overwhelmed by the waves, or overturned by heavy storm winds.

From all that has been said up to this point, one could nevertheless conclude that a round-built hull would have been much more suitable for the Ark than an elongated, square, flat-bottomed one; all the more so because it was not made to stand on solid ground, as one sees with all masonry buildings, but had to float like a ship on the

<column-break/>

water, in which all round-curved bodies can be moved much more easily, because they find less resistance and can overcome the surrounding fluids with far less effort than flat and angular ones. Such angular bodies—whether their corners are right angles and very strong or sharp—must suffer much and run the risk of being completely overwhelmed even by light waves, almost without violence. For the same reason, in former and even in later times, round towers and bulwarks were much more esteemed by all military architects <term>Krygsbouwkundigen: experts in the design and construction of fortifications</term> than square ones, according to the testimony of *Vitruvius*, Book 1, Chapter 5, Section 16 <note>original: "Vitruvius Lib. I. C. 5. §. 16."</note>; which round buildings, however, have nowadays been changed into angular bastions for particular reasons and by force of other principles. Certainly, if one examines the matter well, it will be found that *Noah's Ark*, had it not been particularly preserved by the all-governing hand of the LORD, would undoubtedly have run the greatest danger of being turned upside down even by light winds, or of perishing through some other minor mishap.

**T**he terrifying and irrevocable supreme verdict of the world’s general destruction was finally pronounced by the Supreme Judge: *Behold, I will destroy. Gen. VI. v. 13. Just as the general destruction of the earth had dragged the ruin of all living souls along with it, so the renewed world required new inhabitants. It is true that it

*to be preserved*. v. 19. 20. Moreover, God could have kept these animals, as well as the humans, alive within the Ark through a supernatural miracle; however, He willed that they should all be fed according to the general arrangement and specific nature that He had instilled into Nature. For this reason, He said again to *Noah*: *And you, take for yourself all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself, that it may be for food for you and for them.* v. 21. So that the Ark might be called a good larder and storehouse, indeed a general preserver of life, which served as a safe refuge for humans and beasts, the likes of which has never been seen again in the world in either former or later times.

Regarding aquatic animals, such as fish, snails, mussels, and all that live in the sea and in standing or running waters; it was unnecessary for these to enter the Ark, since they could sufficiently preserve their lives outside of it. Furthermore, one might concede that the so-called hybrid animals <note>The author refers to "basterd Dieren," meaning crossbreeds like mules.</note>, such as mules, which are bred from different species of animals, were not inside Noah's Ark. But as for the "vermin" <note>In this context, "vermin" or "ongedierte" refers to insects and small creeping creatures.</note>, which are excluded from the Ark by theologians following the example of *Augustine, The City of God, Book 15, Chapter 27*, I would grant them free entry just as much as the elephants and eagles. For no one need doubt whether that same God—who even today preserves the very smallest and nearly invisible creatures in so many manifold and rare ways, and what is much more, through the most wonderful transformations, and allows their species to multiply in the same way—was also concerned for their preservation at the time of the Deluge. One need not worry about where best to store all these creatures, since there remained abundant place and room for the vermin.

Noah also, without doubt, took into the Ark all kinds of food and such provisions as corresponded with the nature of each species of animal; so that the master of provisions would not set corn before the carnivorous animals, nor meat before the grain-eaters, as it would be a great folly to try to feed dogs with hay or straw, and donkeys with the remains of gnawed bones. One need not be concerned about sufficient space, as the old Church Fathers were in their time, since above we have been fully 

<column-break/>

convinced of the contrary. However, it is certain that one will sooner see carnivorous animals transition to eating plants and all kinds of greenery than see the hay-eaters use any kind of fleshly food, just as is found among humans, who enjoy meat as well as vegetables and fruits. Thus, it is not necessary here to take refuge in any supernatural miracle, nor to believe that there was a famine in the Ark, since a hungry stomach can even enjoy unusual food. Moreover, as soon as the Deluge ended, the animals had to be the very same—that is, of the same nature and constitution as they had been before—and retain their own rights and freedom in the renewed world which they had possessed before the Flood.

Furthermore, one finds in Holy Scripture the specific command regarding the number and the specific nature of the animals that *Noah* was to take with him and those of his kin into the Ark: *Of every clean beast you shall take to you, seven and seven, the male and his female: but of the beasts that are not clean, two, the male and his female. Also of the fowls of the air seven and seven, the male and the female, to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth.* Genesis 7: v. 2, 3. It should be noted here that the first distinction between clean and unclean cattle appears, which about eight hundred years later was prescribed by God as a Law to the Jewish people. From this, it is understandable that in *Noah’s* time, this undoubtedly did not happen without God's prior will nor outside His Providence; a view confirmed by many learned men, all the more because it seems grounded in Nature itself. *Seth's* descendants used the clean animals for food as well as for sacrifice, whereas, in contrast, the unclean and carnivorous birds of prey—known in *Tacitus* under the name of *foul and unholy cattle* <note>original: "vuyl en ongewyd Vee"</note>—were used for neither. Consequently, *Noah* had sufficient knowledge of this distinction. *And why not? # SPIRITUAL

Meanwhile, as the general flood of the entire world was shortly at hand, all the animals came from all sides and regions to the Patriarch *Noah* in the Ark, namely in such a manner as the particular nature and character of the animals brought with them: that is to say, the multitude on their feet, others flying, and some crawling on their bellies, dragging their flexible and footless bodies along the rough ground. Yet it should be especially noted here that this general assembly or gathering of all kinds of animals happened by no means through a single effect of their own movement, but certainly through God's special governance and Providence <note>Providence refers to God's divine intervention and care for His creation.</note>. He drove these irrational creatures through an uncommon and unsearchable miracle to that wholesome place of refuge and happy harbor of their preservation, in order to place them, along with the human race, beyond the danger of the upcoming destruction. That kind and merciful Universal Ruler, who still daily gives the mute beasts their food; and who governs these living instruments through the ever-working power of His Omnipotence, protects them from mishaps, keeps them alive, and lets each multiply in its kind, was without doubt their invisible leader: in a word, He who created them also gave them this command. What more is needed to make them obey? The irrational creatures strictly follow the command of their Creator, and even through their ready obedience, they convict all rebellious and unrepentant humans of their godlessness and the almost incomprehensible hardness of their hearts. Furthermore, it is well to think that all kinds of wild and cruel animals were undoubtedly tame and manageable in nature at that time, just as they were in the first state of Innocence <note>The "state of Innocence" refers to the period before the Fall of Adam and Eve, when all creatures were believed to live in harmony.</note>, when they were brought by the LORD to *Adam*, *Gen. 2:19*. Consequently, one may say that through God's Omnipotence, a double miracle was performed in this case; the first consists in the general calling together of the animals, the other in their wonderful change to a tame nature, which before that time seemed to be entirely calm and tamed. Those who, after the Fall, had become rebellious, malicious, and the open enemies of Man, and were scattered throughout the entire world, now leave their usual dwelling places—driven by a certain unknown power or blind urge—and come forth from forests, mountains, valleys, and subterranean hiding places, yes, even from under the waters, as if they wished to renew the ancient friendship and enter into a kind of Covenant <note>A formal, solemn agreement; here referring to the original peace between man and beast.</note> with Man. Therefore, they take their refuge with *Noah*, who was to be the general Father of the future world, and seek to preserve their lives under his protection, without however knowing the reason for this. From this, it appears sufficiently—to the shame and absolute conviction of those miserable and God-forgotten mortals who unhappily lived through the Deluge and miserably perished by it—that even the irrational animals had far more foresight than those hardened and unmovable sinners. This is even more so because the latter were informed beforehand of the sorrowful outcome of the general destruction, which had already been foretold to them for *one hundred and twenty* years, and were repeatedly exhorted to repentance by *Noah*, yet they persevered in their wickednesses until the last moment and remained entirely insensitive to this terrible threat. But if one looks into the matter properly, one will find the true reason for this was that the speechless and irrational creatures were led and governed by the Almighty hand of GOD; whereas, on the contrary, the blinded and degenerate humans, despite the Reason with which they were gifted, allowed themselves to be carried away by the mad and reckless urge of their corrupt passions, closing their ears to the Divine warnings without ever wishing to give any belief to the Fatherly warning that had been given to them so many times, yet always in vain, by *Noah*.

# PRINT SHEET XLIII.

->*In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month: on this very day all the Fountains of the great Abyss, and the Sluices of Heaven were opened. Genesis 7:11.*<-

The long-foretold time having finally appeared, in which *Noah* and his household were to be separated from the wicked and corrupt company of the rest of mortals, and the entire Human Race was to be destroyed and utterly rooted out by the universal Flood, this Patriarch—along with those of his Lineage and all the Animals—entered into the Ark after it had been completed for seven days; perhaps not without being mocked and laughed at, even pointed at with fingers, by the Godless and unbelieving onlookers and eyewitnesses. But what followed shortly thereafter? *It came to pass after those seven days*, says Holy Scripture, *that the waters of the flood were upon the Earth. Genesis 7:10.* This corresponds in every detail to the terrifying prophecy given to *Noah* in *verse 4*.

The entire span of time from the general Creation of the World to the Birth of the Anointed <note>original: "den Gezalfden"</note>, namely CHRIST our Savior, can conveniently be divided into nine Epochs or specific Chronologies. The first of these is from *Adam* to the Flood, amounting to *Sixteen Hundred and Fifty-Six years*. Observe how and in what manner this can be calculated:

It should be known that the *years* spoken of in Holy Scripture are, without doubt, complete *Solar Years*, which also consisted of Solar Months, each of thirty days: for it is well believed that the months before the Flood must have been such that five of them—namely, from the seventeenth day 

<column-break/>

of the second month to the seventeenth of the seventh month—together made up a total of one hundred and fifty days. This is clearly evident from the comparison or synthesis of the present Scripture passage with what one reads in *Genesis 8:3-4: The waters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters were abated. And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.* Thus it is that the year totals three hundred and sixty days, to which five more days were added, so that the year in its entirety would have three hundred and sixty-five days, though six hours less than what a so-called *Julian year* <note>The Julian year, introduced by Julius Caesar, averages 365.25 days.</note> used to be.

Furthermore, it should be especially noted here that the beginning of the year among the Jews was calculated in two ways, so that a Hebrew year had a double beginning; for the <term>Sacred Year</term> <note>The religious calendar used for festivals.</note> took its beginning in the month of *Nisan* or *Abib*, starting with the first New Moon when the Days and Nights in the Springtime are of equal length. The <term>Civil Year</term> <note>The secular calendar used for legal and agricultural matters.</note> began in the month of *Tishri*, that is to say, with the first New Moon when Day and Night in the Autumn are of equal length. According to the first, since the departure of the Israelites from *Egypt*, the *Ecclesiastical matters* have been arranged, and according to the other, the *Worldly* or *Civil matters*, following the ancient observations of the Patriarchs. This distinction of the year has caused very great difficulty among the Translators of Holy Scripture regarding the calculation of the Flood. That this universal Flood occurred in the *Autumn* or at the beginning of the *Civil Year* can be demonstrated not only by weightier reasons but also by the Authority of several learned Men—namely, by the nature of the aforementioned Patriarchal years, by the world's first beginning in the Autumn, as well as by the common custom of the Chaldeans, Persians, Egyptians, and Jews, who set the beginning of their years in the Autumn. Conversely, the Flood appears to have had its beginning in the *Spring*,

...because the usual manner of the year had been reformed on account of the Exodus from *Egypt*, the Civil year having been changed into the Sacred year. To this also serves the fact that *Moses* wrote after this change; and consequently, the Jewish writers could not interpret the first, second, and subsequent months in any other way than according to the newly introduced arrangement of the Sacred year. According to this arrangement, the second month mentioned in our Text—named *Iyar*, and called *Ziv* in the first Book of Kings 6:1 <note>original: "I. Kon. VII. 1." The text cites VII. 1, but the description of the temple's start in the month of Ziv is traditionally I Kings 6:1.</note>—is likewise ordered, and corresponds with *April*, but especially with the *month of May*. If one wishes to confirm this matter by the authority of many excellent writers, the credible testimonies of *Scaliger, Alstedius, Langius, Calvisius, Wasmuthus*, and many others can be cited in this case for further reinforcement. Moreover, *Reason* and *Nature* themselves seem to contend for this view. It is certain that the Flood lasted a full year, or at least that *Noah* kept his residence within the Ark for an entire year. From this it follows that, if it ended in the Autumn, it must also have had its beginning at that time. Furthermore, because of the manifold absurd consequences that would arise from this, it is not advisable to place the Flood in an earlier time: especially because it would hardly have been possible, without a supernatural miracle, for the plants of the earth to have reached their proper growth at that time of year. How or where would *Noah’s* descendants have found the necessary provisions for their maintenance, since the year had already progressed so far? How would the irrational animals have been able to spread across the entire world, and each depart to its own landscape or climate? In what way would the plants of the earth have been able to take root? How would they have come to bloom and finally to bear fruit? Without a doubt, everything would have been suppressed and destroyed by the cold. Furthermore, it would not have been possible for the animals, which were accustomed to warmth, to exist in a cold climate: the plants would have perished even in their first budding due to the excessive cold, frost, and snow; in a word, all of Nature, instead of being happily reborn, would have died out entirely. The slimy and muddy crust, with which the recently flooded and just-

<column-break/>

-relieved Earth was covered, required no harsh Winter time, but rather a pleasant and all-nourishing warmth, through which the redundant and harmful moisture could be driven away. The all-too-weak and damp plants likewise had to be restored by warmth, and nurtured by new sap. To be brief, almost all creatures, which—having been shut up for so long—seemed half dead, had to receive a new life through the warmth. To what has been said thus far, another even more powerful reason can be added, which in all parts corresponds with the beginning and the end of the Flood, and especially consists in this: namely, that among the countless multitude of so many remarkable and wonderful remains of the Flood, which we strive to collect and preserve with singular diligence and effort, very many are found from which one can perfectly conclude that the same must, without a doubt, have had its beginning in the Springtime, and especially in the month of May.

# ILLUSTRATION PLATE XLIV.

Holy Scripture posits two particular causes for the Deluge, which are explicitly contained in the following words: *All the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.* <note>A reference to Genesis 7:11.</note> Regarding the first, namely the great deep, some place it beneath the depths, or seek it in the hidden and desolate bowels of the Earth. But this reasoning is somewhat too obscure here. In my opinion, one should side with those who view all the subterranean water gatherings—which lie divided and stored here and there in various internal parts of the Earth, and penetrate many places through certain watercourses, or at least through manifold springs, and in that way spread everywhere—as that great deep or abyss. What the ancient writers intended to signify with their so-called *Erebus* and *Tartarus* <note>In Greek mythology, Erebus represents deep darkness or the underworld, and Tartarus is the deep abyss used as a dungeon of torment.</note>—certain subterranean places by which they understood this abyss—has been deemed unnecessary to investigate further.

Since Holy Scripture does not mention the manner in which this breaking open or bursting through of the subterranean waters occurred, Natural Philosophers are permitted to state their opinion on the matter, provided that their reasoning accords both with the facts themselves and with the nature of the Earth. Those who deviate from this guiding principle go astray. If one wishes to believe **Th. Burnet** <note>Thomas Burnet (c. 1635–1715), an English theologian and writer on cosmogony, famous for his *Telluris Theoria Sacra* (Sacred Theory of the Earth).</note> *Theory of the Earth, Book I, Chapter 6*, then one must compare the first Earth to a pair of bellows which, having become hot from the Sun, gradually split and burst, and finally at the time of the Flood tore and broke. Due to its uneven position, it sank down into the Abyss or water-depth that lay between the habitable upper-earth and the internal core. By this collapse, the waters of the Abyss were forced upward, overflowing the globe and consequently causing that unevenness of Mountains, Valleys, Lakes, and Islands that one finds on the Earth today.

<column-break/>

The opinion of **Whiston** <note>William Whiston (1667–1752), an English mathematician and theologian who succeeded Isaac Newton at Cambridge. He argued that the Flood was caused by a comet.</note> *Theory of the Earth, p. 444*, as well as the fundamental proposition of **Cluverus** <note>Detlev Clüver (c. 1645–1708), a German scholar who wrote on the intersection of geology and the Bible.</note> *Geology, Chapter 12, p. 171*, arouse considerably more attention. Both of these writers, finding no sufficient causes within the Earth for the rising of the waters from the abyss, nor for a continuous downpour of forty days, go to fetch them from the Heavens—namely, from a <term>Comet</term> <note>original: "Staartstarre," literally "tail-star."</note> passing close by the Earth. In a similar fashion, they also attribute the general conflagration of the world to such a Comet which shall appear at that time. The most remarkable thing of all is that they describe this imaginary Comet of the Deluge as naturally, and determine its entire course as accurately, as if they themselves had been present there and had observed everything with attention, or as if *Noah* himself had left them certain memoirs of it. See Figure I for its entire course of 150 days. It stands at **a** on the first day of the second month; at **b** on the tenth; at **l** on the seventeenth, passing close by the Earth, which then stands in its annual orbit **q h** in the 12th degree of **Taurus** <note>original: "Stier."</note>; at **C** on the twentieth; **d** on the thirtieth; at **e** on the tenth day of the third month; at **t** closest to the Sun **H**; at **f** on the thirtieth day of the third month; at **g** on the tenth day of the fourth month; and at **h** on the twentieth of the same, once again passing close by the Earth, which then stands under the celestial sign of **Cancer** <note>original: "Kreeft."</note>; at **i** on the thirtieth; and at **k** on the tenth day of the fifth month. Consequently, **a t k** is the proper course of the Comet, **t n** the rotation or movement of the axis, **H** the focal point, and **q h** the course of the Sun or rather that of the Earth.

approaching, it causes Ebb and Flow, both in the upper Ocean and in the Abyss, and these are all the greater as it draws nearer. By this, the round sphere of the Earth is changed into an oblong shape—such as the revolution *a b* of the oblong around the longer axis produces—usually split by cracks, and moreover pressed by the weight of the waters. Through these cracks now the waters from the Fountains of the Abyss were raised, and they burst forth with such successive speed that the world was flooded, and the surrounding Air filled with vapors, and the Earth not only pressed, but according to the laws of <term>hydrostatic pressure<note>The physical law governing how water exerts force when confined or weighted; original Dutch: "Waterperfling."</note></term> was pressed down. To clarify this matter, the following experiment may serve. Let Figure III, *ABCD*, be a wooden Vat, to whose hollow upper surface is very closely but flexibly fitted an oblong round shape *AEFBGH* of marble, pierced along the length of the center with the holes *EHML* and filled with oil up to *IK*. It is clear that if this oblong round shape is pressed down into the vat *O*, it will rise more and more above *IH*. And the oil will be driven out through the holes *EL* and *NP*, which expulsion will represent the flooding over the surface *AB*. Thus, the *Comet* was either the Puller <note>The force of gravity pulling the water.</note> or the Presser, and the Earth the suffering subject, which has by no means lacked its crevices since its first creation, and perhaps had less solid expansions, as if self-existing. That the Fountains were broken is confirmed by *Job 38:8: Who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?*

Let it be permitted to anyone to point out other causes for the eruption of the waters, such as could be a sudden stopping of the Earth's central motion, through which, according to the laws of Motion, the Abysses of water would further widen the cracks by their impact—cracks perhaps brought about by the first rotation of the Earth, now and then making others—and rise up into the heights. The waters first of the Ocean, and afterwards of the Abyss, would overflow and separate the entire Earth; which hypothesis can be illustrated by any oblong vessel spun in a circle, in which, if it is suddenly stopped, the water will continue the motion once impressed upon it, and because it cannot expand in width, it will climb high up the sides of the vessel.

<column-break/>

All these, and other means which could be devised for the greatest of floods, must not be regarded as if they were the works and motions of Nature alone. He who looks upon all these things—suspected by many without reason—with attentive eyes, beholds entirely extraordinary movements, indeed miracles. We have seen miracles in the created World; we see them in the destroyed one, in that which is to be renewed, and in the renewed one.

We proceed to the *Windows of Heaven*, <note>Hebrew: "Arboth Haschamain" (Arubbot ha-shamayim).</note> which the Holy Writer describes as being opened. These are not the *Cataracts of Heaven* <note>Greek: "Kataraktae tou Ouranou."</note> or the *Windows of Heaven* <note>Greek: "Thurides Ouranon."</note>, certain water-bringing Constellations, as the Astronomers dream—such as Cancer, Pisces, the Pleiades <note>original: "Zevengeflernte."</note>, Orion, Mars, Venus, the Moon. So claims *Mechlinas' Commentary on the Great Conjunctions of Albumasar*. He says that the Flood of Noah was preceded by the great meeting of *Jupiter* and *Saturn* at the end of Cancer, opposite the constellation of the *Ship Argo*. Which opinion, maintained by *Tiberius Calaber*, the Dominican *Hieronymus Armellinus* marked with a black coal <note>A phrase meaning to reject or condemn an idea.</note> and refuted in a special Book. We, having pushed all these trifles aside, understand by the Sluices of Heaven the Air around the Earth, very fertile in waters—the aerial heaven—not, as some wish, the Starry Heaven. The scriptural passages *Luke 4:25* and *2 Kings 7:2* provide clarification on this matter. And indeed, the *Air* is not unsuitably compared to *Windows*, transmitting the rays of Light, the Raindrops, the Snowflakes, and all kinds of atmospheric phenomena. Who is ignorant of the fact that, when Rain or Snow falls from Heaven, the Windows of Heaven are opened, and the air-holes of Heaven are expanded? On the contrary, in clear weather, they are contracted and closed. A more intrusive meaning is given by the aforementioned *Whiston* and *Kluverius*, whose Comet, encircling the Earth entirely with its rod-like tail, would have given abundant rains.

In *Gen. VII. 16.* one reads, *that the LORD shut him in*. Noah, already dwelling in the Ark, surrounded on all sides by the waters. These words are commonly explained as referring to the Door of the Ark, which Noah and his kin would have been powerless to close. ### PLATE XLV.

> *And the flood was forty days upon the earth; and the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lift up above the earth.*
> *And the waters prevailed, and were increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters.*
> *And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered.*
> *Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail; and the mountains were covered. Gen. VII. v. 17, 18, 19, 20.*

Moses acts here as a very precise hydrographer <term>waterbeschryver; a scholar who describes or maps the earth's waters</term>, carefully noting the successive increases of the waters, finally down to the cubits <term>ellen; an ancient unit of measurement based on the length of the forearm, roughly 18-22 inches</term>. *The first* was that by which the Ark, resting on the Earth, *was lifted up, so that it rose above the Earth v. 17. Secondly*, by which *the waters prevailing, and increasing greatly above the Earth, the Ark went upon the waters, v. 18.* Which increases must be attributed *both to the breaking up of all the Fountains of the great Deep, and to the opening of the Windows of Heaven*, to the rain of forty days; which having ended, the water continued, though more slowly, to burst out from the bowels of the Earth and to be poured from above by rains, though stopping now and then, until the end of 150 days mentioned in *Gen. VIII. 3.*, which passage is useful for explaining the 19th and 20th verses of the present Chapter.

But where, I ask you, shall we find in the entire Water- and Air-sphere such a great abundance of water that could be powerful enough to bring about a Deluge, and to cover the Earth to above the tops of the Mountains and higher? Here lies the knot <note>the central difficulty or crux of the argument</note>, here spring forth the detractors and enemies of the inherent credibility of the Holy Bible: just as there have been those who, having exhausted all the treasures of Earth, Seas, and Air, and furthermore, the calculation being made, require seven Oceans to create a Deluge...

Let him unravel all the phenomena in such a way that neither the Scripture is violated, nor the thoughts differ from the nature of things: let him separate the certain from the uncertain, holding it uncertain until, the shadows of darkness being driven away, he introduces the light of truth. Finally, let him take no refuge in miracles, unless required by the expressed command of GOD, or an unavoidable necessity, or the greatness of the work exceeding all the powers of Nature.

1. That the Earth, which is but a tiny point in comparison with other whole celestial bodies, contains more than enough water to be submerged to a height of one mile—not merely moistened by water, but entirely soaked through. The circulation and balance of massive water surges (whose exact location is not certain) remains constant between the Ocean, other waters, the Air, and the Earth.

2. It is certain that the waters bubbled up from these Fountains of the Deep, though the manner is uncertain: whether this occurred by the aid of Fire? Or by a sudden halting of the Earth's rotation? Through the intervention of a Comet? Or by other means? Infinite means are found working immediately in the voluntary and most powerful hand of GOD.

3. It is probable that the waters of the Abyss, which are also named in the first place, contributed the largest portion of this inundation; the Windows of Heaven contributed the least.

4. It is uncertain whether the Mountains of the first World were lower than ours, but it is certain that the peak of Mount Ararat was lower than the waters of the Deluge: it is also certain that our Mountains, even the highest, are a product of the Deluge, as is evident from reasons proven elsewhere.

5. # NATURAL PHILOSOPHY.

The Earth was a core surrounded on all sides by water, as it had been of old during the Creation, and is now shown again in Figure I; nevertheless, these were divided into their beds <note>original: "beddingen"; refers to geological strata or layers</note>.

6. Since these things were so, the consequence follows of itself: that the Earth, punished by the *Flood*, this newly-deformed and empty world, in order that it might be made dry and fit to be inhabited, was broken. The beds were raised, and thus an unequal order of arrangement arose, divided into Mountains and Valleys, which at first glance has the appearance of a building collapsed into its own ruins. Yet, far be it from us to think that all these things happened by mere chance. This elevation of the beds, arranged in the wisest manner, is the construction of the Building, not a product of chance. Here the laws of <term>Mechanical Nature<note>original: "Tuygwerkkundige Natuure"; the laws of physics and mechanics as understood in the 17th and 18th centuries</note></term> were by no means sufficient; Divine power was employed, just as in the first Creation of the Earth. Figure II shows this new state of the Earth to some extent, the cross-section being made through the largest circular diameter.

7. Through this same elevation of the Earth's beds—the raising of the Mountains, the pressing down of the Valleys, and the same occurring in stages down to the shores and even to the bottom of the Sea—hollows were created in the bowels of the Earth. Into these, the waters of the Flood could retreat, which shall provide the Rivers, Springs, and Clouds with their source-veins.

8. From these things it is clear, matters being as they are, that the Earth—with subterranean pillars supporting this Earth and sustaining Mountains—shall not be flooded again by natural causes. However, should GOD command the ruinous, eroded pillars to fall into the hollows of the Earth, then the waters of the Abyss could spring forth once more and put the Earth under water.

9. That there were Mountains before the Flood is evident not so much from the primary text as from *Proverbs 8:24, 25; Job 15:7; Psalm 90:1, 2.* By these verses, as if by a three-pointed lightning bolt, everything that could be brought forward against the existence of Mountains before the Flood is struck down. The mere runoff of waters across sloping plains required them.

10. Furthermore, the rising of the waters 15 <term>cubits<note>An ancient unit of length, roughly 18–22 inches; here translated from "ellen"</note></term>, or 24 5/6 Parisian feet, above the mountains required a general dwelling place suited for the living, the resting of the Ark upon Mount *Ararat*, and the deposition of Earthly particles from the very high water-column. However, whether this height of the waters was such that it could have covered not only the mountains of *Asia*, but even the highest *Alps* in *Europe* in the state in which they are now, I would not dare to confirm for certain.

<column-break/>

### P L A T E  XLVI.

> And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:
> All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.
> And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark. Genesis 7:21, 22, 23.

These three verses strike down all those who harbor peculiar opinions, which are also refuted by mute and yet most eloquent Nature, bearing this inscription throughout the whole world:

-> EVEN HERE THE FLOOD IS PRESENT. <-

For everywhere the footprints of that sorrowful event of the Deluge are present; but there are also everywhere such things...

->S P I R I T U A L<-

those who, blinded by prejudice, see nothing even with open eyes—yes, they refuse to see the remains of the **Flood** lying before their eyes and feet. They would rather attribute these to a chance occurrence, a "sport of Nature," not knowing which plastered-over ideas or similar refuges of ignorance to choose, rather than turning to the true sources. They are more unfortunate than even the Pagans and the Jews, who, guided only by the thread of **Nature**, have recognized this truth, which we shall confirm and present before your eyes through several successive plates. Read the supporting passages in *Strabo's Geography, Book I*; *Philo's On the World, page 1168 of the Paris edition.* If you desire the Ancient Church Fathers as witnesses, go to *Tertullian's On the Pallium, page 530 of the Basel edition.* If you wish to have witnesses among the Reformers, look up *Luther* in his *Commentary on Genesis, page 22.* I shall remain silent regarding a numerous host of modern and very discerning men who have brought this hypothesis to the certainty of proven truth. You would see that the simplest among the class of peasants reason far more fortunately; they immediately and correctly judge from pieces of wood dug deep from the Earth, and from the fish, plants, and shells found in stones, that these are remains of the Flood. They are more fortunate, I say, than those false philosophers who, through the cleverness of false reasoning, attempt to obscure even the clearest truths and entangle all things in the snares of difficulties.

The testimony of the Flood is imprinted upon all things, even upon the *Marpessian* <note>original: "Marpeffifche"; refers to Mount Marpessa on the island of Paros, famous in antiquity for its white marble</note> cliffs. Consider the composition of the Mountains, ordered in very neatly arranged layers <note>original: "Beddingen"; refers to geological strata</note>, indeed built up from the same; you will see that there are proofs of a sinking made in the highest column of water, as well as a certain splitting apart introduced thereafter. You shall judge from the placement of two parallel lines of these beds, the fractures, curves, and wondrous variations, that the earth is a substance <term>and arose from the water<note>original Greek: "καὶ γέγονα τῶ ὕδατος" (likely a reference to 2 Peter 3:5 regarding the earth being formed out of water)</note></term>: which truth *Metrodorus* has drawn from the nature of things in *Plutarch's On the Opinions of the Philosophers, Book III, Chapter 9.* I have demonstrated this truth more fully in my *Oreographia Helvetica* <note>Latin: "Description of the Swiss Mountains"</note>. Meanwhile, I show the reader here, by way of example, the layers of a wonderfully uniform shape in the vicinity of Lake *Uri*, especially towards the East and the West.

### PLATE XLVII.

I proceed to the remains from the **Kingdom of Plants**: here appear *Woods, Leaves, Fruits, and Entire Plants*, imprinted in stones, occurring in subterranean layers. Through the arrangement of even the smallest fibers, they strive for resemblance to their originals—indeed, they are the originals themselves, sunk onto beds during the Flood. They are to be carefully distinguished from <term>Dendrites<note>original: "Dentriken"; mineral patterns that look like trees but are not biological fossils</note></term>, Jasper, and Florentine marble. I do not intend to present all those which I have gathered together, but only the most select, and those which stand as primary witnesses for the truth we defend. He who desires to have an account of plants of this sort may find access to my *Herbarium of the Deluge <note>original: "Kruytboek van den Watervloed"</note>, Second Edition, Leiden 1725.*

### PLATE XLIX.

I shifted my step from Plants to *Humans*, the primary cause of that <term>πανoλεθρία</term> <note>original Greek: panolethria, meaning total destruction or utter ruin</note>, whose sins the other innocent sacrifices had to atone for. Of these, which is surprising, very few relics remain. Up to now, I have not been able to obtain more than two *Vertebrae* of the Back (Figure 14), entirely turned to stone and shining with a black luster. However, in the year 1725, there was brought into my study from the quarry of *Oeningen*, in the Bishopric of *Constance*, among others, a *relic* worthy of so much more attention because it is indubitable; it shows not just a single part, but very many, indeed nearly half a skeleton. Because not only is an image imprinted there, from which an uncertain and haughty imagination could fabricate one thing from another, but the very substance of the Bones, yes, of the flesh, and of parts even softer than flesh, remains in the exact proportions of size: in a word, a relic of the rarest of that cursed and under the waters buried Race. <note>This refers to the "Homo diluvii testis," which the author, Johann Jakob Scheuchzer, famously misidentified as a human victim of Noah's Flood; it was later identified by Georges Cuvier as a giant prehistoric salamander.</note> And that in two ways: from the front and from the back. It shall be enough to have included the latter here, as

<column-break/>

more complete, yet not in its natural size, but in a more compressed size. Therefore, you see in Fig. 15. a. b. c. the outline of the bone of the Forehead; d. d. the sockets of the Eyes; e. the Foramen below the circle, intended for the passage of the nerves of the fifth pair; f. the remains of either the Brain itself or of the *dura mater* <note>original: "harde Moeder," literally "hard mother," the outer membrane of the brain</note> covering it; g. the fragmented pieces of the eye sockets; h. the perforated and spongy bones; i. the Vomer <note>original: "Ploegschaar," literally "ploughshare," the bone separating the nasal passages</note> which divides the nose into two equal parts; k. k. the Zygomatic bone <note>original: "Jukbeen," or yoke-bone</note>; l. the fourth jawbone, which makes up the cheeks; m. the remains of the Nose; n. a notable piece of the chewing Jawbone; o. p. o. p. a cross-section of the posterior part of the lower jaw from top to bottom. Further, 16 spinal vertebrae, marked in order each with their numbers 1. 2. 3. etc., of which most have their processes turned the wrong way, now exposed, now covered; q. the Coracoid process <note>original: "Raven-bek," or Raven's beak</note> of the Shoulder blade; r. the first Rib covered with a stony skin; s. clear indications of the Liver, to be inferred from its position.

# NATURAL HISTORY.

Bb

### PLATE LI.

Figure XIX. of a **Sea-horse**, called *Rosmarus* <note>original: "Rosmarus"; while called a sea-horse here, this refers to a walrus</note>: a specimen found at Bologna <note>original: "Bononie"</note>, described by the very renowned Monti <note>Gaetano Lorenzo Monti (1712–1797), an Italian botanist and naturalist.</note>.

---

### PLATE LII.

Figure XX. Two remains of a **Crocodile**, one the larger from the library of Linkius <note>Johann Heinrich Linck (1674–1734), a famous pharmacist and collector from Leipzig.</note>, the other, which is smaller, from the study of Spener <note>Christian Maximilian Spener (1678–1714), a German physician and heraldist.</note>.

---

### PLATE LIII.

Figure XXI. The skeleton of an **Adder**, from my own study; of these, the most have been accounted for up to now, including many from those which are set to be described further on.

Whoever considers the anatomy of Birds—the bones, feathers, wings, and all things suited for flight—will not be surprised that very few, and almost no monuments of them remain from the **Great Flood**; meanwhile, he <note>The author, Scheuchzer, referring to himself in the third person.</note> brings forth from his own study:

Figure XXII. *A feather from the tail of a bird* beautifully imprinted in a stone excavated at Oeningen <note>Oehningen, a famous fossil site near Lake Constance.</note>.

There are also, for reasons already stated, rare bloodless animals <note>Insects or invertebrates.</note> in the studies. Because of their lightness, there was hardly an opportunity for them to sink down. Yet this very lightness, their easy attachment to heavier bodies, and the sliminess of many, have been the reason that some of those which lived before the Flood still remain. See here:

Figure XXIII, a ground beetle or **Beetle**, in a stone excavated at Oeningen.

Figure XXIV, a **Dragonfly** <note>original: "Rombout, of Puystebyter"</note> from a piece of land near Verona.

Figure XXV. A **Dragonfly** <note>original: "Puystebyter"</note> in a split stone at Oeningen.

The Fish were excluded from the Ark. They lived in their primary element <note>water</note>; yet, so that the other animals would not undergo a sadder fate, only the genera and species were preserved. In truth, there occurs such a great abundance of

<column-break/>

fish, and such a variety of those that existed before the Flood, that I would hold that a large, and indeed the largest part of them perished: sea fish, which could not endure the mixing with fresh water; those from marshes and rivers, whose constitution did not agree with salt water; many smothered in muddy and thick silt, in which they had perhaps immersed themselves, trying to flee death, only to become victims of death. One followed the other, and step by step upon one cliff, wishing to avoid the other, which is why you will often find very many of the same species in the same pit or stone quarry, and none in others. And, which I wish to be noted, there remains not only a shadowy form of the fish, but almost the entire structure: head, tail, fins, the vertebrae of the spine, the bones, and even the flesh. So that regarding the certainty of these specimens, not the slightest doubt remains. And how, I ask you, could this kind of animal, especially sea creatures, be transported to places far removed from the sea, into the bowels of very high mountains like the Swiss mountains, if not by cause of that general deluge? These and other arguments I urge more closely in my *Complaints and Vindication of the Fishes* <note>Refers to Scheuchzer's 1708 work "Piscium Querelae et Vindiciae", where he argues that fish fossils are victims of the Flood.</note>. The place and the time admonish me to show some specimens of that kind.

Figure XXVI, is the large tooth of a **Seal**.

The XXVII, XXVIII, XXIX, and XXX Figures are teeth of a **Sea-wolf** <note>original: "Meerwolf"; likely referring to fossil shark teeth or the wolffish.</note>.

### PRINTED PLATE LXII.

->*After that he sent forth a Dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground.*<-
->*But the Dove found no rest for the sole of her foot; so she returned to him into the Ark; for the waters were on the face of the whole Earth; and he put forth his hand, and took her, and pulled her in unto him into the Ark.* Gen. VIII. v. 8, 9.<-

---

Recently the Raven served as a scout, but an unfaithful one—that flesh-eating Bird, unclean, predatory, and wicked, whether for eating or for sacrifice. Now the *Dove* goes to work, a grain-eating Bird, a clean, gentle one, used both for food and for sacrifice, which has this trait: that she, even from distant places, flies back to her nest. The first <note>the Raven</note> had to investigate the remains of the dead corpses, and perhaps bring back flesh and bones, but the *Dove* did not. Concerning the *Raven* we have noted doubts as to whether he indeed returned? That the *Dove* returned, and that immediately, as it seems, is certain: *Moses* <note>the traditional author of Genesis</note> has added the reason. In a marshy Land, as *Josephus* <note>original: "Josephus"; the first-century Jewish historian Flavius Josephus</note> says, stagnant and full of holes—or at the very least soggy—she had found nothing upon which her foot could—

<column-break/>

—find rest, for the waters were over the whole Earth. Unless you except the tops of the Mountains protruding above the waters.

The Holy Writer remains silent on the time at which this *Dove* was sent out. *Joseph Scaliger* <note>original: "Josephus Scaliger"; a renowned 16th-century scholar of chronology</note> places 40 days between the sending of the *Raven* and the *Dove*. It is more likely that she was sent out either at the same time as the *Raven*, or immediately after him: and even more likely, that the *Dove* was sent out seven days after the *Raven*. This can be inferred from the 10th verse: *And he stayed yet other seven days: then he sent forth the Dove again out of the Ark.* Here there is certainly a reference to the seven preceding days. Consequently, this sending out falls on the day of the 4th of March, according to the previously accepted assumption.

## PLATE LXIII.

> *And he waited yet another seven days, then he let the Dove go out from the Ark again.*
> *And the Dove came to him towards evening, and behold, a plucked-off Olive leaf was in her beak: so NOAH noticed that the waters had subsided from the Earth.* Gen. VIII. v. 10, 11.

Seven days having passed since the sending out of the first *Dove*, the second now flies out, namely on the 11th of *March*, and brings to the Father a joyful message from the new World. She returned towards evening, carrying *a plucked Olive leaf in her beak*. Surely this was not from the groves of the land of *Israel*, or the Mount of Olives, or the fields of upper *Asia*, as was suggested by *Rabbi Abba* son of *Cabana*, and *R. Levi* in *Genesis Rabbah Ch. 33* <note>original: Brefith Rabba</note> and *Peyrerius* in his *System of Theology Book IV Ch. 8* <note>original: Systh. Theol. Lib. IV. C. 8.</note> who relied on a backward assumption of a localized Deluge, and a wrong interpretation of the passage in *Ezekiel 24:24*. It is clear from the Text that the Olive branch <note>The author uses the word branch here, though he argues for "leaf" later</note> which was brought along was a proof-sign of the receded waters on the Earth; and how could it have been there, if it had not been broken off from land no longer covered by water? I refrain from recounting other reasons, just as I refrain from refuting that ridiculous opinion which can be read in the sayings of the circumcised Teachers <note>A traditional, though dated, way of referring to Jewish Rabbis</note> in *Leviticus Rabbah Ch. 31* <note>original: Vajekra Raba</note>, who claim that the Branch was broken off in the Earthly Paradise, which the Jews have fabled to be above the peaks of the Mountains, spared from all floods, as some Church Fathers have also maintained.

But where is that fortunate landscape bearing Olive trees, which gave to Noah the first evidence of the reborn World? *Assyria* pleases *Bochart* in his *Sacred Zoology Part II Book I Ch. 5* <note>original: Bochart Hierozoic.</note> because it bears Olive trees and yields Oil (*2 Kings 18:32*), and so that the Traveler lacks no guide, he pairs the Dove with the North Wind, which drove the Bird (who naturally seeks the Southern region) thither. The overly long distance would discourage me, if Mount *Ararat* was located where the *Armenians* and *Persians* claim it to be, and where, according to the testimony of Travelers,

<column-break/>

no Olive trees grow. This doubt causes me no difficulty. In those regions where they do not otherwise grow, an Olive tree could have been transported by the rush of the waters, and the Branch could have been plucked not very far from the Ark. Serving as proof of such transport during the Deluge are the Pine trees found in England, the Fish and Sea shells on the Mountains of Switzerland, and the bones of Elephants and Crocodiles in Germany <note>The author is referring to fossils, which 18th-century naturalists often believed were deposited by Noah’s Flood.</note>. And it is very probable that this Olive tree lay upon the Earth, partially covered by the waters, with the branches meanwhile sticking out above the surface, from which a leaf was plucked; and from this *Noah* judged that the waters had subsided so far that the Trees, whether standing or lying, began to appear and stick out above the waters.

That which the Dove brought to Noah was not a *Branch* of an Olive tree, but a *Leaf*, <term>tarach guale tzaith</term> <note>Hebrew: a freshly plucked olive leaf</note>, <term>phullon elaias karphos</term> <note>Greek: a dry leaf or sprig of olive</note>; which could have been plucked from a standing or fallen tree, or even picked up by the Dove from small twigs or a single leaf lying on the ground. It should be noted here that the leaves of this Tree are of a tough composition, so that they last a long time under water, being invincible against the rays of the Sun and the water: as is generally the case with the leaves of Trees in the Eastern regions. Because of this, just as today the Indians cover their Huts with Palm leaves, the "Fish-eaters" <note>Referring to the Ichthyophagi, ancient coastal peoples described by Greek historians</note> of old covered theirs with Olive leaves. *Strabo* in his 16th Book calls them <term>Mandras, stegastas apo phullados elaieis</term> <note>Greek: Huts covered with olive foliage</note>. This leaf could also have sprouted from a Tree previously stripped of leaves; for it is known that the—

->S P I R I T U A L<-

<meta>The previous page ended mid-word; the sentence concludes here: "...all the waters, this tree very easily puts forth new buds and leaves."</meta>

this tree very easily puts forth new buds and leaves. *Virgil* says of it:

> *The olive-bearing root is produced from dry wood.* <note>original Latin: "Traditur è sicco radix oleagina ligno." From Virgil's Georgics, highlighting the olive's hardiness.</note>

That is: *The olive-like root is propagated from dry wood.* And it would do so all the more easily if this tree had been submerged in the silt of the Flood-waters, being rendered very fertile by those nourishing sediments.

We recognize the leaf brought to *Noah* as a true leaf of an olive tree, specifically from a *Seed-bearing* one (Fig. O). This was not a leaf from the olive tree described by *Theophrastus* (History of Plants, Book IV, Ch. 8) or *Pliny* (Book XIII, Ch. 25), nor was it the *narrow leaf* of the *Pondweed-Willow* <term>Potamogeton</term>, which does not differ much from the leaves of the olive tree. Certainly, from a broken piece of such a plant—whether from under the sea or the water—*Noah* would not have been able to surmise what he did indeed surmise.

For *Noah* understood from the olive leaf brought to him that the waters had been lifted from the Earth; that they had not only fallen below the peaks of the mountains, but that the lower places of the Earth were also relieved of the waters; and that the peaceful hills were protruding. He was mindful of the natural habitat of olive trees, which love neither the tops of the higher mountains nor the altogether lowest valley-plains, but rather *incline toward the slopes and open spaces of the earth* <note>original Greek: "ta teys geys schymata proskliney kai huptila"</note>, as *Florentius* says (Book IX, Ch. 6, "On the suitable air for olives and the shapes of the earth"). See also *Columella* (Book IV, Ch. 6) and *Palladius* (Book III, Ch. 18). Such was the situation of that Mount of Olives so 

<column-break/>

famous in the history of the Suffering of CHRIST. Namely, the olive trees would suffer more from the cold and frost on the higher peaks, and in the flat fields from the heat and excessive moisture. Furthermore, the Dove, that joyful Messenger, gave hope to Noah—who had now been imprisoned for nearly the course of an entire year—that the Earth, with all its store of growing things, had not perished; and that there remained remnants of fruit-bearing trees that would sprout again. In addition, he could conclude that the Dove had found a place where she had rested, and that the bird had not flown for the entire day, for she had returned in the evening, having perhaps been sent out in the morning. The judgment and patience of this best of men had to be tested, but his downcast spirit also had to be lifted up again.

And perhaps this so fortunate mission of the Dove gave occasion to the Eastern Peoples (who were later followed by others) to send Doves as Envoys or Messengers to carry news from one place to another. See *Pliny* (Book X, Ch. 37).

# PLATE LXIV.

> And in the second month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, was the earth dried. Gen. VIII. v. 13, 14.

It is the duty of envoys to make known to their Princes the true state of the matters they must handle, but our Dove, sent out for the second time, did not return to Noah, *verse 12.* Yet the absence itself, the very silence, served as an answer to the Patriarch. He could have concluded that the bird had found a place where it could easily rest and live. Nevertheless, he did not wish to go outside impulsively, nor to break open his "prisons," so to speak, trusting neither himself nor the Earth. Sound Reason taught him that a sufficiently long passage of time was necessary to dry the Earth—which he perhaps had in view—since it was slimy, muddy, and drying partly through evaporation and partly through the draining of the waters into their old and deep bosom <note>The author uses "bosom" to refer to the deep basins or interior of the earth where the floodwaters retreated.</note>. Some water had receded slowly, other water even more slowly, causing the water to flow down more toward the flat landscapes; these were undoubtedly still under water for some time after Noah himself left the Ark, due to the density of the soil beds. More vapors could rise into a surrounding mist than it was able to contain, leading to a slow and steady evaporation. However, *Noah* did not wish to rely on his own judgment; he had entered the *Ark* with his whole house by virtue of GOD’S express command, *Gen. VII. 1.* Now he expects a command from the same supreme Legislator; he requests it and receives it, *Gen. VIII. 15.* Then GOD spoke to *Noah*, saying: *v. 16. Go forth of the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons' wives with thee.* Until now he had experienced the most excellent and providential hand of GOD during the entire course of the Overflowing of the Flood; to the same GOD, his Creator and Preserver, he offers the sacrifice of Patience, Faith, Hope, and the most godly submission.

<column-break/>

GOD is a GOD of order. He did not intend for the Earth to dry through a miracle, but according to the laws of restored Nature, gradually and imperceptibly. The text bears witness to this gradual drying. We translate the word *Charbou* <note>original Hebrew: חָרְבוּ (charvu), meaning to be parched or dried up</note> in verse 13 as *dry*, and the word *Jabsha* <note>original Hebrew: יָבְשָׁה (yaveshah), indicating a more complete, structural dryness</note> as *the Earth was dried up*, verse 14. Specifically, it evaporated more and more from the pores <note>original: "zweetgaten", literally 'sweat-holes'</note> of the slimy and moist Earth, but it also receded more and more through the descending plains.

The Chronology of the Flood is to be concluded here. It appears from *Gen. VII. 1.* that the beginning of the flood occurs on the 17th day of the second month, which corresponds to the 3rd or 4th of June, 1658 <note>This year refers to the "Anno Mundi" or "Year of the World" calendar system used by early modern scholars to date biblical events from the moment of Creation.</note>. Now *Noah* removes the covering of the *Ark* on the first day of the first month; therefore

There are those who here, and elsewhere, entirely exclude the natural sense of the words, and as if carried above the air on Eagle's wings, explain everything in a hidden <note>allegorical or mystical</note> sense; there are also those who attribute everything to Nature, and often, whether they will or no, pull or surrender it wherever it seems good to them; finally, there are those who take the safest path in the middle, comparing Nature with Scripture, and the hidden interpretation with the literal sense.

# PHYSICS.
Dd
<meta>catchword: PRINT-</meta>

...is a natural sign of that which is signified, namely, that no more Floods shall come in the future. We have placed in the third rank those who say that the Rainbow was seen by Noah, but that it was not previously a natural sign of the Flood not returning in the future; rather, it was a voluntary sign, just as the signs of Circumcision, the Passover, the Blood of the Covenant, the Water in Baptism, and the Bread and Wine in the Lord’s Supper. See *Heidegger, Exercises on the Regeneration of the World, Thesis 29* <note>original: "Heidegger Exerc. de Paling. mundi Th. 29."</note>.

If this is so, and if this Rainbow was a sign of a Flood that would never come again, then according to the covenant established at its institution, it must also have been seen before the Flood. Many Christian teachers feel otherwise, following *Aben Ezra* <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a Spanish Jewish scholar and biblical commentator.</note>, and among these is our own very frequently praised *Sturmius, Explanation of Holy Scripture, page 115* <note>Johann Christoph Sturm (1635–1703), a German philosopher and mathematician.</note>, and *Burnet, Theory of the Earth, Book II, Chapter 5* <note>Thomas Burnet (c. 1635–1715), whose "Sacred Theory of the Earth" proposed that the antediluvian world was a perfect, smooth sphere without mountains or rain.</note>, as his "first Earth" was entirely different from this present one. Certainly, if we accept what we have gained—that the first world was nearly the same as this one which we now inhabit; if there were Mountains, Valleys, Rains, and Clouds—then I do not see why the Rainbow would not have appeared, for the Sun was there, as was the eye of the Beholder. Furthermore, no "new" bow can be derived from the Text that was not seen before, but only a new use, a new meaning according to the Divine institution.

Let us draw closer, to see the Letter of His Covenant fully opened—not inscribed in Copper, nor Marble, nor Parchment, as are those of Princes and Nations, but written in the fluid Air. It is all the more durable because it can be wiped away and brought forth again at any moment. Some things are subject to Rust, Moths, Worms, and decay; this is of equal durability with the World. The ways of GOD are different from the ways of men. Here, the most high and most excellent GOD writes the treaty of the Covenant with *Noah* and the human Race upon a thin cloud consisting of dew; the stylus or pen was the rays of the Sun, themselves of many forms and diversely shaded by colors; the ink, the Raindrops; the lines, the most neatly arranged colors within them; the various elevations, the reflection and refraction of the rays; the most mighty Chancellor, GOD Himself: *I have set My bow in the cloud.*

This atmospheric phenomenon was a very great wonder-sign, a marvel even to the Heathens; the *Daughter of Thaumantes* <note>In Greek mythology, Iris (the rainbow) is the daughter of Thaumas.</note> was placed in the rank of the Goddesses by *Plato in Theaetetus; Plutarch, Opinions of the Philosophers, Book III, Chapter 5; Apollodorus, Library, Book I* <note>original: "Plato in Theatetus Plutarch. Placit. Philos. III. 5. Apollodor. Biblioth. L. I."</note>. Yet seldom does the Daughter of Thaumantes, swift of foot, *Iris* the Goddess, dwell upon the vast back of the Sea, *save for when strife and discord have arisen among the Gods.*

Nor is it any wonder that they were swept away in admiration at the sight of an atmospheric phenomenon, which is marvelous for many reasons: that it comes suddenly and disappears suddenly. It is a Painting worked out with the most beautiful colors and the most well-arranged order by an entirely inimitable art, which prides itself: where the brushes are the Sunbeams themselves—which, as I have said, are multi-colored—and the Canvas is the most fluid Element of the Air. In this, one must wonder, and never enough, that all at once in an accurate circular shape, many millions of the same Painting—indeed, as many different Rainbows as there are beholders in the same Horizon or human eyes—are created. There are as many new ones as the beholder takes steps, or as many head-turnings as he changes. One must marvel that she is so swift of foot; if someone were to run quickly, they would be exhausted before they could overtake the Painting, unless that person stood in the very gathering of the drops and endured being rained upon—in which case the beholder stands upon the circular circumference of the Rainbow itself.

# SPIRITUAL

### PRINT PLATE LXVI.

It belongs to another place and another time to bring forth the entire history of the Rainbow; such would be a work of more than a specific explanation, to which we have bound ourselves. *Descartes* <note>original: "Cartesius." René Descartes (1596–1650) was one of the first to provide a mathematical explanation for the rainbow's angles.</note> began to bring speculative knowledge to a mathematical certainty, and finally *Isaac Newton*, the most ingenious and most accurate of all philosophers who have ever lived, brought the same to the highest peak of demonstration. Behold there the brief summary of the entire speculative knowledge.

Figure I. The eye is at O. The line OP. The parallel lines POE, POF, POG, POH. The angles of 40° 17', 42° 2', 50° 57', to 54° 7'; which angles, drawn around the lines OE, OF, OG, OH, form the sides of two Rainbows, AFBE and CHDG. The drops E, F, G, H, being placed in the middle of the tapered surface of the lines OE, OF, OG, OH, and illuminated by the Sun through the rays SE, SF, SG, SH, the angle SEO will be equal to the angle POE, 40° 17'. This is the largest of those in which the rays undergo the greatest refraction <note>The original Dutch uses "ombuyging" (bending/refraction).</note> and, after a single reflection, travel to the eye; consequently, all the drops on the line OE will display the most refracted rays, which is a sky-blue or violet color. And so the angle SFO, equal to the angle POF, 42° 2', will be the largest in which the rays undergo the least refraction of those which, after a single reflection, can come to the eye; and so all small drops in the line OF will cause redness in the eyes. It is the same with the rays that have intermediate stages of reflection and are located in the drops between E and F, coming forth from E, ascending to the colors F: violet-colored, Indian-colored <note>likely referring to Indigo</note>, blue, green, yellow, gold-colored, and red. Thus, in the second Rainbow, the angle SGO, equal to POG, 50° 57', will be the smallest of the angles in which the rays, which are the least refractable, come from the drops to the eye after two reflections. Therefore, all the drops in the line OG will constitute a red color. And the angle SHO, equal to POH, 54° 7', the smallest of those in which the most refractable rays, after two refractions, are reflected again

<column-break/>

to reach the eye, and therefore all the drops in the line OH give to the eye a violet-blue color, and the drops midway between G and H, ascending from G to H, give in order a golden-yellow, green, blue, and Indian violet color. Thus we shall obtain colored bows: the innermost and brightest formed by one reflection, the outermost by two. The width of the inner bow EOF shall be 1° 45'; of the outer GOH, 3° 10'; and the gap between them FOF, 8° 45'. This is how the matter would behave if the Sun were a single point. However, the width of the Sun increases the width of the Bow and decreases the width of the space between them. For the width of the inner Bow is 2° 15'; of the outer, 3° 40'; and of the gap between them, 8° 25'. The largest angle of the inner Bow POF is 42° 17', and the smallest of the outer POG is 50° 42'.

It is not for me to explain through allegory <note>original: "verbloeming," literally "flowering" or masking with metaphors.</note>, as the purpose of my office and intention does not require it. Man being returned to the Earth, and the Earth to Man, yet she produced no fruit of her own. The curse announced to sinful Man, and to the Earth itself in *Genesis 3:17, 18, 19,* had not been removed: But rather, although she had been surrendered to the curse in the destruction by the Deluge, it was greatly increased; namely, as fertile as she had once been, she had now become barren. Now labor was necessary to clear the obstacles out of the way; that is, Agriculture <term>Landbouw: the cultivation of the soil</term>, which did not begin with Noah as the last, but had the first mortals as its inventors. *Cain was a tiller of the ground, Genesis 4:2.* Noah, being mindful of that most righteous curse, but also of the very fresh promise in *Genesis 8:22: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest shall not cease,* began to till the Field. He did not exploit the peasants or haughtily despise their labors, but put his own hand to the work, to be a Husbandman.

<meta>The previous page discussed the geological origins of stone and building materials. This page continues the exploration of masonry, specifically shifting to the construction of the Tower of Babel and the historical use of bitumen versus mortar.</meta>

# NATURAL HISTORY.
Ee
<meta>catchword: But</meta>

...of a uniform rectangular shape, just like those used today for the construction of chimneys, houses, and the flooring of rooms. These are very useful in civil architecture, both for their durability and their shape, since they can be conveniently laid one above the other, allowing walls to be raised quickly. They are also useful in military science because, unlike cobblestones, they do not shatter into pieces but offer long resistance to heavy artillery and its cannonballs. This type of stone pleased those masters of architecture, the Greeks and Romans, as is evident from *Pliny* in *Book XXXV, Chapter 14*, *Vitruvius*, and others.

Stacking stones of uniform shape and great weight that have been neatly planed—primarily marble stones—to construct durable buildings can be done even without glue <note>original: "lym"; here meaning mortar or binding agent</note> between them to hold them together. A proof of this is *Solomon’s* Temple, that most perfect model of civil architecture, not to mention the Roman structures commonly found. However, this does not apply to baked bricks <note>original: "tichelsteenen"</note>. These must be bound together, especially for a tower of such massive size as the one spoken of here. Our master builders used *hachmar lamoor* <note>original: "hachmar lamoor," a transliteration of the Hebrew 'ha-chemar la-chomer' from Genesis 11:3, meaning "bitumen for mortar"</note>, clay in place of lime. Thus we translate it, leaning on the authority of the Arabic, Syrian, and Chaldean versions, as well as the Jews, who translate *chamar* as *Tsin* <note>Hebrew/Aramaic term for mud or mire</note>, silt—perhaps with the exception of *Kimchi* <note>David Kimchi (1160–1235), a famous medieval Jewish commentator and grammarian</note>, who has "cement," a mixture of lime and sand. Yet the translation of the Seventy Translators <note>The Septuagint (LXX), the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note>, the common Latin <note>The Vulgate</note>, and those of *Junius* and *Tremellius* are much to be preferred, which use "Jew's pitch" <note>original: "Jodenlym"; refers to bitumen or asphalt, specifically the type found in the Dead Sea</note>. However, a distinction must be made between liquid and hard bitumen: the former is *unsuitable for building* <note>original Greek: "gene eis oikodomein achryston"</note>, according to the testimony of *Diodorus of Tarsus* in the *Chain of the Fathers* <note>original: "Catena Patrum"; a form of biblical commentary consisting of a "chain" of interpretations from Church Fathers</note>; but the latter is very useful for construction because, like glue, it binds the stones together and fills the joints and all openings. That such a type of clay or slime, which is dug out of the earth, is found in *Babylonia* is testified by authors highly respected for both their authority and antiquity—even regarding the walls of *Babylon* itself. See *Herodotus*, *Strabo* in *Book XVI*, *Justinus* in *Book I, Chapter 2*, *Vitruvius* in *Book VIII, Chapter 3*, and *Curtius* in *Book V, Article 3*. From this it appears that for "clay" or "mud," one should substitute "Jew's pitch" <term>Bitumen: a naturally occurring petroleum product used as mortar in antiquity</term> or mortar made of lime; silt or clay is hardly a suitable material to build even a peasant's hut, much less a structure intended to last for as many centuries as that of *Babel*.

But you would also express *Chomar* better as *Mortar* than as *cement*. *Cement* refers to the stones themselves from which the walls are joined together, with lime or mortar being spread between them—specifically raw stones without a set shape, as opposed to square stones. See *Livy*, *Book XXI, Chapter 11*. Mortar, meanwhile, is sand mixed with lime. Unless you would rather express *Chemar* as silt and *Chomar* as cement, so that the meaning would be: that silt and potter's clay served them, but by making it hard through fire, it served as cement. However, the first explanation is more pleasing.

Noah's descendants, primarily the Hamites <note>The descendants of Ham, son of Noah, traditionally associated with the peoples of Africa and the Near East</note>, find it advisable—having until now lived scattered in huts—to gather closer together, to establish a Society, to change from Farmers into Citizens, and even, under the leadership of *Nimrod*, to found an Absolute Monarchy <note>original: "Alleenheerschappy"</note> as overlords of the other peoples. Therefore they said—notwithstanding that the *Shemites*, *Noah* himself, *Shem*, *Arphaxad*, *Shelah*, and *Eber* <note>These are the patriarchs of the line of Shem, representing the godly lineage</note> did not consent to it—*“Come now, we who have the loudest voices, we future Masters of the World, we Councilors and Mayors of the Tower-building, let us build a City, and a Tower, whose head (top) reaches unto the Heavens.”* This reason seems the most powerful, if it is not the sole and only reason for the plan and the existence of the project. *Nimrod* could easily foresee, as the Chief Architect of this excellent building—as *Josephus* <note>Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Jewish historian</note> regards him, and with him the Ministers of State—even if it were only by the light of reason, that such a great multitude of people as he needed could only remain gathered in one and the same Society if they assembled into a *Civil Body* <note>original: "Burgerschap"</note>. Nor could they defend themselves against all kinds of neighbors without a fortified place, nor subject other Peoples to themselves without a plausible pretext and such a grand construction. Indeed, a City cloaked in Walls could make all manner of Foreigners fearful, and the Tower, acting as the Citadel, could keep the Citizens themselves in check. Yes, these Builders also had to make a name for themselves, namely a famous Assembly or Parliament, which held its residence in the City of *Babylon* <note>original: "Babel"</note>, so that they might perhaps not be scattered over the whole Earth, and so that they would preserve the Holy Pledges of the Ancestors, the teachings handed down by the Fathers. This is evident from the punishment announced by GOD, *v. 6. And the LORD said: behold, they are one people, and they all have one language; and this is what they begin to do: but now, shall not everything they have thought to do be cut off from them? v. 7. Come, let us go down, and let us there confound their language: so that every man may not hear the speech of his neighbor. v. 8. So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of the whole Earth, and they ceased building the City.* Namely, the Founder of the supreme, even tyrannical Government, wanted all rights to come to a single center in his *Babylon*—those of Nature, of Nations, and Civil rights, yes, perhaps even the Divine—so that he alone could rule. But the purpose of the Most High GOD was the founding of various Republics <note>original: "Gemeenebesten"</note>, dispersed here and there; and to carry that out, He used the most suitable means: the confusion of Tongues, whereby no one could understand the other, and all wandered off into various paths of opinion.

For *Josephus, Glycas, Manasses, and Patricides*, <note>These are ancient and medieval historians; Flavius Josephus is the most famous, while the others are Byzantine chroniclers.</note> that building was intended to be a place of refuge during a future Deluge; others claim it was to be a monument to that inevitable flood. *Diodorus Siculus* <note>A Greek historian known for his monumental 'Bibliotheca historica'.</note> is of the opinion that it was to be an observation point for the Stars, just as it is certain that the *Chaldeans*, and particularly the Babylonians, have been very remarkable in every age for their observation of the Constellations. Others believed that they indeed intended to *build a Tower whose summit would reach to the Heavens*. This appears to be attributed to them by *Abydenus* in the works of *Cyril* and *Eusebius*. We read of something similar concerning the Emperor of China, *Hiaou*, in *Martinus Martinius’s History of China, Book I, page 365*, who intended to make an access for himself to the Moon to embrace his *Chang-o*, <note>Referring to the Chinese goddess of the moon; the text spells it 'Changon'.</note> whom a certain sorcerer had convinced him lived there. It would seem more agreeable if some wished to form from the City and Tower a *towered city*, provided with Towers for its protection, in the center of which there perhaps was a very high Tower, stronger and more elevated than the others, which would serve in place of a Citadel. That *Babel* was certainly surrounded by a great number of Towers is evident, even if only from *Diodorus*, who relates that *Semiramis* alone built 250 Towers.

Regarding the construction of the *Tower of Babel*, and for that reason regarding the meaning of the words of the Text, and the objective of the Heaven-stormers, various men hold various views. Let us choose those things which pertain to our subject. The most absurd opinion is that of those who, clinging too stubbornly to the literal letter, understand the star-bearing Heavens. Even the first principles of Mathematics reveal this absurdity; they turn a Tower touching the Heavens upside down and cast it down to the Earth. Suppose these fools had extended their effort only as far as the Moon—as *Hiaou* did—which, by the lowest estimation of the nearest point, is 50 Earth radii away from us. If the thickness at the base were moderate, it would have run to an immoderate size in height; a building which the Earth itself would have built in its own roundness, a mass perhaps fifty times larger than the Earth itself. The force of this proof was already understood in his time by *Philo the Jew*, in his book on *Moses* regarding the
